question: A laptop gets its IPv4 address from DHCP at the office. At a field site that has no DHCP server, it must use a fixed address without the user changing anything. Which part of the IPv4 Properties dialog provides this?
explanation: The Alternate Configuration tab can hold a user-configured address that Windows uses whenever it cannot get a DHCP lease, so a laptop can move between a DHCP network and one without DHCP with no changes. Use the following IP address sets one static address for every network, Obtain an IP address automatically uses DHCP and by default falls back to an APIPA address, and Advanced TCP/IP Settings adds extra addresses, gateways and DNS options.

question: A customer buys a boxed copy of an accounting application at a store, and the installer comes on a USB flash drive. Which distribution method is this?
explanation: Software delivered on something the buyer holds, such as a USB flash drive or a disc, is distributed on physical media. A mountable ISO file is a disc image that is downloaded and opened as a virtual drive, a downloadable package is an installer fetched from the vendor's site, and image deployment copies a prepared system image to many computers.

question: A pop-up that claims to come from Windows Security tells a user that the PC is infected. Which detail would show that the alert is fake?
options: It names the threat that it says it detected
It asks the user to call a support phone number
It appears near the clock on the taskbar
It offers to quarantine the detected threat
explanation: Microsoft's real error and warning messages never include a phone number to call, so a security alert that asks the user to phone for support is a tech support scam. Real Windows Security alerts do name the threat they found, do offer to quarantine it, and do appear as notifications near the clock, so none of those details shows that an alert is fake.

question: A technician has confirmed that an office workstation shows the symptoms of a known malware strain. Following CompTIA's malware removal procedure, what should the technician do NEXT?
options: Schedule regular scans of the computer
Disconnect the computer from the network
Disable System Restore on the computer
explanation: Quarantining an infected computer, usually by disconnecting it from the network, comes right after the symptoms are verified so that the malware cannot spread to other systems. Disabling System Restore follows quarantine, updating the anti-malware definitions is part of remediation, and scheduling regular scans comes after the malware has been removed.

question: A regulation requires a clinic to keep each patient's records for a set number of years, after which the clinic may securely destroy them. What is this kind of rule called?
explanation: A retention requirement sets how long records must be kept before they may be destroyed, and laws set such periods for health, financial and tax records. Data minimization limits collection to the data that is actually needed, a legal hold stops deletion while a lawsuit or investigation is pending, and a classification policy labels data by how sensitive it is.

question: On a Windows 11 Pro desktop, a technician wants a single window that holds Event Viewer, Device Manager, Task Scheduler, Shared Folders, and Local Users and Groups. Which tool provides this?
explanation: Computer Management (compmgmt.msc) gathers Task Scheduler, Event Viewer, Shared Folders, Local Users and Groups, Device Manager, Disk Management and Services into one MMC console. Windows Tools is a folder of shortcuts that open each tool in its own window, Control Panel holds settings applets, and System Information (msinfo32) reports hardware and software details without managing anything.

question: During remediation, a quarantined Windows PC must stay off the network until it is clean, but its anti-malware definitions are weeks out of date. How should the technician update them?
options: Download them in Safe Mode with Networking
Copy them from another computer on a USB drive
Turn on automatic updates in the scanner
Reinstall the scanner from its original setup media
explanation: When a quarantined computer must stay off the network, its anti-malware definitions are updated offline: they are downloaded on a clean computer and carried over on removable media such as a USB drive. Safe Mode with Networking and automatic updates both need the network connection that quarantine takes away, and the scanner's original setup media holds definitions even older than the ones already installed.

question: A shopping app needs the phone's location to list nearby stores, but the technician finds it has been collecting location data all day, even when it is not open. Which change should the technician make?
options: Switch the app to approximate location
Allow location access when the app is in use
Deny the app any location access
Turn off location services on the phone
explanation: Limiting an app's location permission to when the app is in use stops background tracking while keeping location features working whenever the app is open. Approximate location makes the position less exact but still lets the app collect it all day, while denying the app location or turning off location services for the whole phone would also stop it from finding nearby stores.

question: A technician must set a static IPv4 address on a desktop PC from Control Panel. Which Control Panel item leads to the window where the adapter's IPv4 properties are edited?
explanation: Network and Sharing Center shows the active networks and links to Change adapter settings, where an adapter's IPv4 properties, including a static address, are set. Device Manager lists the adapters but manages only their drivers and hardware settings, Internet Options holds browser and proxy settings, and RemoteApp and Desktop Connections connects to programs that an organization publishes for remote use.

question: A small business keeps its server backups on a shelf in the server room. A burst pipe floods the room and ruins both the servers and every backup. Which practice would have prevented the data loss?
options: Rotating the backup media in a GFS scheme
Keeping a backup copy at another location
Encrypting the backup media in storage
Testing restores from the backups regularly
explanation: Keeping at least one backup copy off-site, in another building or in cloud storage, means that a fire, flood or theft at the main site cannot destroy every copy at once. Encrypting media protects backups if they are stolen, regular test restores prove that backups can be recovered, and a GFS rotation sets how long each backup is kept, but none of these helps when every copy is in the same room.

question: A company moves its office wireless network from WPA2-Personal to WPA2-Enterprise. What security gain does the change bring?
options: Clients roam faster between access points
Each user signs in with their own credentials
Traffic is encrypted with AES rather than TKIP
Management frames are protected from forgery
explanation: WPA2-Enterprise replaces the shared passphrase with 802.1X sign-ins checked by a RADIUS server, so each user has their own credentials and one person's access can be removed without affecting anyone else. Both WPA2 modes use AES encryption, protected management frames are required by WPA3 rather than added by this change, and faster roaming comes from features such as 802.11r rather than from the sign-in method.

question: A technician's script, meant only to set a new desktop wallpaper, contained an error that also turned off the Windows firewall on every workstation that ran it. Which scripting risk does this show?
options: Exposure of passwords stored in the script
explanation: A script that runs with administrative rights can change settings it was never meant to touch, and one error can turn off a protection such as the firewall on every computer it reaches. Malware arrives through code taken from an untrusted source, crashes come from a script that exhausts memory or other resources, and exposed passwords come from credentials written into the script itself. Testing a script on one machine before a wide rollout limits this risk.

question: After a feature update, a Windows 11 PC's system drive is nearly full. The technician wants a built-in tool that can delete temporary files, old update files and the previous Windows installation. Which tool should the technician use?
explanation: Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) removes temporary files, and its Clean up system files option also removes Windows Update files and the previous Windows installation. Disk Management creates, resizes and formats partitions, the Recycle Bin holds only files that users have deleted, and File History backs up personal files to another drive.

question: On a company Mac, apps downloaded from developers' websites will not open, and only apps from the App Store run. Which macOS feature enforces this rule about where apps come from?
explanation: Gatekeeper checks where an app came from and whether its developer signed it, and it can be set to allow apps from the App Store only. XProtect scans apps for known malware, FileVault encrypts the startup disk, and Keychain stores passwords, keys and certificates.

question: A standard Linux user may run administrative commands by entering their own password but does not know the root password. Which command lets them edit /etc/hosts?
explanation: The sudo command runs a single command with root privileges after the user enters their own password, as long as the sudoers policy allows it. The su -c form also runs one command as root but asks for the root password, plain nano opens /etc/hosts without the right to save changes, and sudo cat only displays the file.

question: A technician removes spyware from a domain workstation on which the user had typed passwords for email and the company VPN for several weeks. What should be done about those credentials before the workstation is returned?
options: Enable account lockout on the domain
Have the user change the passwords
Clear the passwords saved in the browser
explanation: Spyware can capture anything typed while it runs, so every password entered on the infected computer must be treated as stolen and changed once the spyware is gone. Clearing saved browser passwords does not undo what was already captured, account lockout defends against guessing rather than theft, and a shorter maximum password age only forces a change later.

question: In a coffee shop, a user's phone joins a Wi-Fi network by itself. It is not the shop's network but one named after the free hotspot at an airport 300 kilometers away, which the user joined last month. What is the most likely explanation?
explanation: Phones rejoin saved open networks by name alone, so an attacker can broadcast a known hotspot's name from a rogue access point, an evil twin, and intercept the traffic of every phone that joins it. An airport's network has no reason to appear in a distant coffee shop. A captive portal is the sign-in page a legitimate hotspot shows before granting access, a deauthentication attack knocks devices off a network rather than drawing them in, and MAC address randomization hides the phone's hardware address from networks.

question: A technician PXE boots a new desktop from a WDS server to install Windows 11. During this process, what does the client use TFTP for?
options: Joining the computer to the domain
Copying the Windows image to the disk
explanation: In a PXE boot, TFTP carries the network boot program and the Windows PE boot image from the WDS server to the client before any OS has loaded. DHCP gives the client its IP address and points it to the boot server, Windows Setup copies the install image over SMB once Windows PE is running, and joining the domain happens later through a domain controller.

question: A user's Android phone gets no response at all from a store's contactless payment terminal, although a card is set up in Google Wallet. What should the technician check first?
options: Whether mobile data is turned on
explanation: Contactless payment uses NFC, a short-range radio that can be switched off in the phone's connection settings or quick settings, and with it off the terminal never detects the phone. Bluetooth pairs headsets and other accessories, and the tap itself needs neither mobile data nor Wi-Fi, since the phone already stores the payment details it sends.

question: Before an old CRT monitor is recycled, a technician is asked to remove a circuit board from inside it. The monitor has been unplugged for a week. What must be done before anyone reaches inside?
options: Hold the power button down to drain the charge
Discharge the tube's anode with a grounded probe
Clip an ESD wrist strap to the metal chassis
Set the monitor on a grounded antistatic mat
explanation: A CRT can hold a dangerous high-voltage charge on its tube long after it is unplugged, so a trained person must discharge the anode to ground with a proper probe before anyone reaches inside. A wrist strap grounds the technician and would give that charge a path through the body, an antistatic mat only protects parts from static, and holding the power button drains a computer's small standby charge, not the tube.

question: An hour ago, a user accidentally deleted half of a shared cloud document, and others have been editing it since. How should the technician recover the lost text without undoing the others' edits?
options: Recover the file from the cloud recycle bin
Copy the missing text back from an earlier version
Roll back the user's PC to last night's full system backup
Restore the version from before the deletion
explanation: Cloud documents in services such as Microsoft 365 and Google Docs keep a version history, so the technician can open a version from before the deletion and copy the missing text into the current one, which keeps everyone's later edits. Restoring that old version outright would roll the document back and remove the past hour's edits from it, the recycle bin holds deleted files rather than deleted text, and a PC backup does not contain the cloud copy.

question: A technician is hardening a workstation so that other computers can reach only the network services it needs, and every other incoming connection is refused. Which control should the technician configure?
explanation: A host-based firewall decides which incoming connections a single computer accepts, so it can leave the needed services reachable and refuse the rest. Host-based intrusion detection watches the computer for signs of attack and raises alerts without refusing connections. A data loss prevention agent stops sensitive data from leaving the device, and endpoint antivirus finds and removes malicious files.

question: A program's installer will not continue until the user accepts the publisher's terms for how the software may and may not be used. What are these terms called?
explanation: An end-user license agreement is the publisher's contract that a user accepts before installing software, and it sets out how the software may be used, copied and shared. A software maintenance agreement covers updates and support, a privacy policy explains what personal data the publisher collects, and an acceptable use policy is an employer's rules for its own computers and networks.

question: A small accounting firm finds that a PDF editor on its office PCs was installed under a free license that allows home use only. Which license does the firm need to stay compliant?
explanation: Software used for business work needs a corporate-use (commercial) license, because a free personal-use license covers only home, non-commercial use. A personal-use license is what the firm already has, educational licenses are for schools and students, and government licenses are sold to public agencies.

question: A technician must change one line of a configuration file on a Linux server that has no graphical desktop. Which editor runs in the terminal and lists its main shortcut keys along the bottom of the screen?
explanation: The nano editor runs in a terminal and lists its main shortcuts, such as Ctrl+O to save and Ctrl+X to exit, along the bottom of the screen. The vi editor also runs in a terminal but uses separate command and insert modes and shows no list of shortcuts, while gedit and Kate are graphical editors that need a desktop.

question: A user's documents no longer open, each has a new and unfamiliar file extension, and a text file on the desktop demands payment in Bitcoin for a decryption key. Which type of malware is this?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment, usually in cryptocurrency, for the key that decrypts them. A cryptominer uses the computer's processor to mine cryptocurrency without encrypting anything, a boot sector virus infects the startup code of a disk, and spyware quietly collects information about the user.

question: A technician wants six primary partitions on a new 1 TB disk. Why can this disk not be set up with the MBR partition style?
options: MBR keeps no backup of its partition table
MBR has just four entries in its partition table
MBR needs UEFI firmware to boot Windows
MBR cannot address more than 2 TB of disk
explanation: An MBR partition table has only four entries, so an MBR disk can hold at most four primary partitions, while GPT allows 128 partitions on Windows. The 2 TB limit of MBR does not matter on a 1 TB disk, it is GPT rather than MBR that needs UEFI firmware to boot Windows, and the missing backup table is a weakness of MBR that does not limit how many partitions it holds.

question: An MDM console flags a corporate iPhone as noncompliant because it has been jailbroken. Which change caused by jailbreaking makes the phone a security risk?
options: Loss of the phone's saved data
Support for other carriers' SIM cards
Access to the phone without a passcode
explanation: Jailbreaking removes the iOS restrictions that keep each app in its own sandbox and allow only signed code, so any app, including malware, can gain system-level access and work around MDM controls. Use with other carriers' SIM cards comes from a carrier unlock, a phone that opens without a passcode has its screen lock turned off, and lost data follows a factory reset, none of which jailbreaking itself causes.

question: A PC's Windows updates keep failing. The Windows Update service is disabled again each time the technician sets it back to Manual, and Microsoft Defender's real-time protection is off. What should the technician suspect?
options: Corruption in the component store that updates rely on
A third-party antivirus that has taken over from Defender
Updates paused in the Windows Update settings
Malware turning off updates and security software
explanation: Malware often disables Windows Update and antivirus protection so that it cannot be patched out or detected, and a service that is disabled again after every fix points to an infection, so the malware removal procedure applies. A third-party antivirus turns off Defender's real-time protection but leaves Windows Update alone, a corrupted component store makes updates fail without disabling the service, and paused updates leave the service's startup type unchanged.

question: A user's PC shows the desktop, but the taskbar and Start menu do not respond to clicks. Task Manager opens normally and shows low processor and memory use. What should the technician try first?
options: Roll back the latest display driver
Run System File Checker as an administrator
Rebuild the search index in Indexing Options
explanation: When the taskbar and Start menu freeze while the computer has resources to spare, the Explorer shell process is usually hung, and restarting it from Task Manager brings them back without a reboot. System File Checker repairs damaged protected system files, rebuilding the index fixes Start menu searches that return nothing, and rolling back a display driver fixes screen faults that began after a driver update.

question: A small business owner wants a Windows 11 Home laptop moved to Windows 11 Pro without losing any files or apps. What should the technician do?
options: Run a clean install from Windows 11 Pro media
Enter a Pro key in the Activation settings
Run a repair install from Windows 11 Home media
Reset the laptop from its recovery partition
explanation: Entering a Pro product key under Settings, System, Activation upgrades Windows 11 Home to Pro in place, keeping files, apps and settings. A clean install from Pro media would erase the apps and files, a repair install from Home media leaves the edition as Home, and a recovery partition returns the laptop to its factory state.

question: A technician wants a Windows 11 computer to start in Safe Mode with Networking at every restart until the setting is turned off again. Which command opens the tool that does this?
explanation: System Configuration (msconfig) has a Safe boot setting on its Boot tab that applies at every restart until it is cleared, and its Network option gives Safe Mode with Networking. System Properties (sysdm.cpl) sets the default operating system and recovery options, the Services console (services.msc) sets how each service starts, and Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) runs tasks at set times or events.

question: A technician manages Linux virtual machines on a KVM host and wants to open a VM's graphical console from a workstation, with USB redirection and audio. Which remote access protocol is designed for this?
explanation: SPICE (Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments) gives remote access to a virtual machine's display through the hypervisor, with USB redirection, audio and clipboard sharing. VNC can also show a KVM guest's console but has no USB redirection, RDP connects to a desktop service running inside the guest operating system, and WinRM runs remote management commands on Windows rather than showing a display.

question: When a domain user opens a file share, the user's computer presents a ticket from the domain controller instead of sending a password. Which authentication protocol is in use?
explanation: Kerberos is the default authentication protocol in Active Directory: the domain controller's key distribution center issues tickets, and the computer presents a ticket to each service instead of a password. NTLM is the older Windows challenge and response method used when Kerberos is not available, RADIUS checks sign-ins for wireless and VPN access, and TACACS+ checks administrators who manage network devices.

question: A technician must preserve a workstation's drive as evidence for an investigation. Before anyone analyzes the data, what should the technician do?
options: Encrypt the drive with BitLocker to protect it
Create a Windows system image of the drive
Make a bit-for-bit image of the drive
Copy the user's folders to a share
explanation: A bit-for-bit image copies every sector of the drive, including deleted and hidden data, and its hash value later proves that the evidence has not changed, so analysts work on the copy while the original stays untouched. A Windows system image runs on the live system and copies only the used parts of its volumes, BitLocker encryption rewrites the data on the evidence drive, and copying folders to a network share misses deleted data and changes metadata.

question: A user holds a phone sideways to watch a video, but the picture stays in portrait even in apps that support landscape. Which setting should the technician check first?
explanation: A phone turns the picture to landscape only while automatic rotation is allowed, so a rotation lock (Auto-rotate off on Android, or Portrait Orientation Lock on in the iPhone Control Center) keeps every app upright. Adaptive brightness changes the backlight to suit the room, screen timeout sets how long the display stays on, and battery saver limits background activity to save power.

question: Windows Update fails on a PC with errors saying the component store is corrupted, and a malware scan is clean. What is the BEST next step?
options: Run gpupdate /force, then restart the Windows Update and BITS services
Stop the update services, then rename the SoftwareDistribution folder
Boot into WinRE, then run bootrec /fixboot and bootrec /rebuildbcd
explanation: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth repairs the component store that Windows Update depends on, and sfc /scannow then repairs protected system files from the repaired store, after which the update can be retried. Renaming SoftwareDistribution clears the cache of downloaded updates, bootrec repairs the boot sector and the boot configuration data, and gpupdate /force reapplies Group Policy, so none of them repairs the component store.

question: A Linux user wants to read the detailed reference page for the ls command that was installed with the system, scrolling through it in the terminal. Which command opens it?
explanation: The man command followed by a command name opens that command's manual page, the full reference installed with the system. Running ls --help prints a shorter usage summary, help describes only bash built-in commands such as cd, and ls -h makes listed file sizes readable in units such as K and M rather than giving help.

question: A user types ls at the prompt in a Linux terminal window. Which component interprets that command and starts the ls program?
explanation: The shell, such as bash, is the command interpreter: it reads what the user types, works out which program is meant and has it started. The kernel manages hardware, memory and processes, the bootloader loads the kernel at startup, and the terminal emulator draws the window and passes keystrokes to the shell.

question: A company is clearing a storeroom of old CRT monitors. Why should the monitors go to a certified e-waste recycler rather than into the regular trash?
options: Their glass contains a large amount of lead
Their batteries can burn when crushed
Their leftover toner can ignite in a fire
explanation: CRT glass contains a large amount of lead, mostly in the funnel and neck of the tube, so CRTs are handled as hazardous waste and belong with a certified recycler. Mercury backlight lamps are found in older LCD monitors, batteries that burn when crushed are in laptops and phones, and toner powder that can ignite is the reason laser printer cartridges should not be burned.

question: A user's phone gets slow Wi-Fi while standing beside the office router, but a laptop next to it gets full speed on the same network name. What should the technician check on the phone?
options: The IP address the phone received
The frequency band the phone has joined
explanation: When one network name is broadcast on both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, a phone can join the slower and more crowded 2.4 GHz band even beside the router, so its Wi-Fi details should show which band it is using. A monthly data allowance and cellular signal strength affect mobile data rather than Wi-Fi, and a bad IP address stops traffic altogether instead of slowing it.

question: A team plans to migrate the company's file server to a new storage system. The change is not routine, is not urgent and carries moderate risk. How should it be handled?
options: As a service request handled by the help desk
As a standard change under a pre-approved procedure
As a normal change approved by the change board
As an emergency change with fast-tracked approval
explanation: A normal change is any change that is neither pre-approved nor urgent, so it goes through the full process: request form, risk analysis, rollback plan, change board approval and scheduling. Standard changes are pre-approved routine tasks, emergency changes are for urgent fixes only, and a service request covers routine user requests such as a password reset rather than changes to systems.

question: A desktop's fans run at full speed, and its CPU stays near 100 percent even when no programs are open. No files have changed and no messages have appeared. Which type of malware explains these symptoms?
explanation: A cryptominer uses the computer's processor or graphics card to mine cryptocurrency for an attacker, so constant heavy load, heat and fan noise with no other symptom are its usual signs. Ransomware announces itself by encrypting files and showing a demand, while a keylogger and spyware try to stay unnoticed and use little processing power as they record what the user does.

question: A small business wants customers in its waiting room to have wireless internet access without being able to reach the office computers or printers. Which SOHO router feature should the technician set up?
explanation: A guest network gives visitors their own wireless network with internet access, kept apart from the computers and printers on the main network. A screened subnet isolates servers that the internet must reach, IP filtering blocks traffic to or from listed addresses, and MAC filtering admits only listed devices, so none of them creates a separate network for visitors.

question: A help desk technician wants to paste a customer's ticket, including the customer's name, address and account number, into a free public AI chatbot to draft a reply. What is the MAIN concern?
explanation: Pasting personal data into a public AI tool sends it outside the company's control, where the provider may keep it or use it to train models, which can breach privacy law and policy. Remove the personal details or use an approved private AI tool instead. Hallucination is invented output, application integration is AI built into existing tools, and bias is unfair skew in results, so none of them is the risk of sharing this data.

question: A technician writes a batch file that runs a vendor's setup program with its silent switches on each new workstation, so that staff receive the standard software with no prompts. Which scripting use case is this?
explanation: Installing applications is a classic scripting use case: the script runs the vendor's installer with silent switches, so the same software arrives on every machine without anyone clicking through prompts. Initiating updates patches software that is already present, remapping network drives connects shared folders to drive letters, and gathering inventory data collects facts about each machine rather than adding anything to it.

question: A technician finds a photo editor on a company laptop. Its license allows free use at home for noncommercial purposes, but the user edits product images for the company's website with it. What is the licensing problem?
options: Its license covers a single computer, not several
Its license covers personal use, not business use
Its license covers a trial period, not ongoing use
Its license covers an older version, not the current one
explanation: A personal-use license allows a program only for private, noncommercial use, so using it for company work requires a corporate-use license. A single-computer limit matters when one license is installed on several machines, an expired trial matters when an evaluation period ends, and a version limit matters when a license for an older release is used for a newer one.

question: A company-owned phone holding client files is lost on a train, and the company wants every file on it erased before anyone can open them. Which mobile security feature does this?
explanation: A remote wipe erases a lost or stolen phone over the network, so the company's data is gone even if the phone is never found. Device encryption keeps the stored files unreadable without the passcode but leaves them on the phone, a remote lock stops the phone from being used without erasing anything, and a screen lock only blocks casual access to the phone.

question: A company is donating old laptops that have hard disk drives. The drives must keep working, but none of the old data may be recoverable. Which method fits?
explanation: Overwriting every sector of a hard disk drive with a wiping tool removes the old data and leaves the drive ready for a new owner. Degaussing erases the data but also leaves a modern hard drive unusable, drilling destroys the platters, and a quick format only replaces the file system, so recovery software can still find the old files.

question: A user with a standard account needs a single program to have elevated rights this one time. Her account and its group memberships must stay as they are. Which Windows option should she use?
explanation: Run as administrator starts a single program with elevated rights, and User Account Control then asks for an administrator's credentials, so the user's own account is unchanged. Local Users and Groups would change her group memberships, Local Security Policy sets password, lockout and audit policies, and the User Account Control settings decide when Windows prompts rather than granting any rights.

question: On a Mac, where does a user add a standard user account, change the display resolution and turn on the firewall?
explanation: System Settings, called System Preferences before macOS Ventura, holds the Mac's system-wide settings, including Users & Groups, Displays and the firewall under Network. Control Center offers quick switches for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, brightness and sound, Mission Control shows all open windows and desktops, and Finder's settings change only how Finder behaves.

question: A workstation's blue screen flashes for an instant and is gone before anyone can read it. Which Startup Settings choice should the technician make so that the stop code stays on the screen?
options: Turn off automatic restart on failure
Turn on boot logging of loaded drivers
Turn off early launch anti-malware protection
explanation: Windows restarts by itself after a stop error unless automatic restart on failure is turned off, and turning it off leaves the blue screen up so that the stop code can be read. Turning off early launch anti-malware protection lets a boot driver load that the protection would block, boot logging records the drivers that load in ntbtlog.txt, and low-resolution video helps when a display driver leaves the screen blank.

question: A printer fault keeps coming back on several floors. After clearing it once more, a technician writes up the symptoms, the cause and the steps that fixed it so that other technicians can reuse the fix. Which document has the technician created?
explanation: A knowledge base article records a known problem with its symptoms, cause and fix so that any technician who meets it again can find and apply the solution. An incident report documents one significant event and its impact, a change request form asks for approval to modify a system, and an onboarding checklist lists the setup tasks for a new user.

question: Each time a PC restarts to finish a feature update, it shows "Undoing changes made to your computer" and returns to the old version. In File Explorer, the usage bar for C: is red. What is the most likely cause?
options: Active hours are delaying the restart
The system drive is nearly full
The Windows Update service has been disabled
The network is set as a metered connection
explanation: File Explorer turns a drive's usage bar red when the drive is nearly full, and a feature update that runs out of space while it installs rolls itself back with the message about undoing changes. A disabled Windows Update service or a metered connection would keep the update from downloading at all, and active hours only postpone the automatic restart rather than reverse an installation.

question: Soon after a user installs a free game, an Android phone starts showing full-screen ads over other apps and warnings that the phone is infected. What should the technician do?
explanation: Full-screen ads over other apps and fake infection warnings that begin right after an install mark that app as adware, so removing it addresses the cause. Clearing its cache or installing its latest update leaves the adware in place, and turning off its notifications would not stop ads drawn over other apps or the fake warnings. If the app resists removal, safe mode lets it be uninstalled while it cannot run.

question: A company must be able to restore any file as it was at the end of any of the last 30 days. Which backup schedule meets this requirement?
options: A backup every hour, each kept for 7 days
A backup every night, each kept for 60 days
A backup every week, each kept for 90 days
A backup every month, each kept for 12 months
explanation: Backup frequency sets how close together the restore points are and retention sets how far back they reach, so restoring a file to the end of any of the last 30 days needs a backup every day, each kept for at least 30 days. Hourly backups kept for seven days reach back only a week, weekly backups leave gaps of up to six days, and monthly backups cannot return a file to a particular day.

question: A technician replaces the system drive in a Windows 11 desktop with a new 4 TB SSD and reinstalls Windows. Which setup lets Windows boot from the drive and use all of its space?
explanation: Windows 11 requires UEFI firmware, Windows boots in UEFI mode only from a GPT disk, and only GPT can use the space on a drive beyond 2 TB, so the new drive must be GPT with UEFI boot. An MBR disk can neither boot Windows in UEFI mode nor address more than 2 TB, and BIOS mode cannot boot Windows from a GPT disk.

question: A Mac user needs to copy a folder from a USB flash drive into Documents and then rename it. Which part of macOS is designed for this task?
explanation: Finder is the macOS file manager, the counterpart of File Explorer in Windows, and it copies, moves and renames files and folders on any connected drive. Disk Utility formats, partitions and repairs disks rather than managing the files on them, Spotlight finds files and apps by search, and the Dock launches and switches between apps.

question: A user has more than 80 online accounts and admits to reusing a few passwords. Which recommendation BEST lets them use a strong, unique password everywhere?
options: Use a password manager that generates and stores each site's password
Turn on multifactor authentication for each account that offers it
Sign in to sites with a Google or Microsoft account where offered
Check each password against a list of passwords exposed in breaches
explanation: A password manager generates a long, random password for every account and keeps them all in an encrypted vault, so the user remembers only one strong master passphrase, ideally protected with MFA as well. Multifactor authentication protects an account whose password leaks but leaves the reused passwords in place, a breach check finds exposed passwords without replacing them, and signing in with a Google or Microsoft account ties many sites to one password rather than giving each its own.

question: A technician types gpedit.msc on a user's Windows 11 PC to change a local policy, and Windows reports that it cannot find the file. What is the reason?
options: The user is not an administrator
The Group Policy Client service is off
The PC is running the Home edition
The PC is not joined to a domain
explanation: Windows 11 Home does not include the Local Group Policy Editor, so gpedit.msc is found only on Pro, Pro for Workstations, Enterprise and Education. Local policy needs no domain, a standard user is asked for administrator approval rather than told the file is missing, and the Group Policy Client service applies policies but does not hold the editor.

question: A company must destroy several thousand old backup tapes that will not be reused. It wants them processed quickly in bulk and reduced to small fragments. Which machine should the destruction vendor use?
explanation: An industrial shredder cuts tapes, drives and other media into small fragments and can process large volumes quickly, which suits media that will not be reused. A degausser erases magnetic tape but leaves each cartridge whole, an incinerator burns media to ash instead of leaving fragments, and a drill press puts holes through drive platters one drive at a time.

question: A CAD application requires a 64-bit OS, 16 GB of RAM, a quad-core CPU and a dedicated GPU with 4 GB of VRAM. A laptop has 64-bit Windows 11, 32 GB of RAM, an eight-core CPU and integrated graphics. Which requirement does it fail?
explanation: Integrated graphics share system RAM and have no dedicated GPU or VRAM of their own, so the laptop fails the application's video card requirement. Its 32 GB of RAM is above the 16 GB required, its eight-core CPU is above the quad-core minimum, and 64-bit Windows 11 meets the operating system requirement.

question: A company installs a row of short, thick concrete posts between its parking lot and the front entrance to stop anyone from driving a vehicle into the building. Which physical security control has it installed?
explanation: Bollards are short, sturdy posts that stop vehicles from reaching a building or entrance while still letting people walk between them. Fencing marks a boundary and keeps people on foot out, lighting removes the dark areas where intruders can hide, and guards check identity and respond to incidents, but none of these is built to stop a moving vehicle.

question: Two tickets arrive at the same time: one user cannot print a single page, and the order-entry system is down for the whole sales floor. Which ticket field tells technicians to work on the second ticket first?
explanation: Severity rates how badly a fault affects the business, so an outage that stops a whole department ranks above a single user's minor fault and is worked first. The category records what kind of problem it is, the escalation level records which support tier holds the ticket, and device information identifies the equipment involved.

question: A small office has no budget for a UPS but wants to protect its server and switch from voltage spikes during lightning storms. Which device should a technician install?
explanation: A surge suppressor diverts voltage spikes away from the equipment plugged into it, so it is the basic defense against lightning surges when a UPS is not affordable, though it supplies no power during an outage. A power strip only adds outlets, a generator supplies power during long outages, and a power inverter turns battery power into AC for devices away from an outlet.

question: A security team finds that an employee's Android phone, which joins the corporate Wi-Fi, has an app installed from an APK file the employee downloaded from a forum. Why is this a concern?
options: It turns on USB debugging on the phone
It bypassed the store's app review
It stops the phone from receiving OS updates
It runs with root access on the phone
explanation: Apps in the official store pass the store's security review before they are published, while an APK from a forum skips that review and may carry malware onto a phone that reaches the corporate network. A sideloaded app gets no root access unless the phone is rooted, installing it does not block OS updates, and it needs the permission to install unknown apps rather than USB debugging.

question: A line-of-business service stopped starting after the password of the account it runs under was changed. On which tab of the service's properties in services.msc does the technician enter the new password?
explanation: The Log On tab of a service's properties holds the account the service runs under and that account's password, so it must be updated whenever the password changes. The General tab sets the startup type and starts or stops the service, the Recovery tab sets what happens when the service fails, and the Dependencies tab lists the services it needs and the services that need it.

question: A technician arrives on time for a scheduled desk visit and finds the user on a personal phone call. The user signals that the call will end in a moment. What should the technician do?
options: Explain the purpose of the visit right away
Leave a note and return at another time
Step out of earshot and wait for the call to end
Begin the work quietly while the call goes on
explanation: A user on a private call deserves privacy, so the technician moves out of earshot and waits, then explains the visit once the call ends. Leaving a note suits a user who is away from the desk, explaining the visit at once suits a user who is free to talk, and working through the call means overhearing a private conversation.

question: A small accounting firm has no security staff of its own. It wants outside experts to watch alerts from its computers around the clock and respond to attacks for it. What should the firm buy?
explanation: Managed detection and response (MDR) is an outsourced service in which a provider's analysts monitor a company's alerts around the clock and respond to threats on its behalf. Endpoint detection and response (EDR) is the monitoring tool itself, which needs the firm's own staff to watch it, an email security gateway filters malicious mail before delivery, and anti-phishing training teaches staff to recognize suspicious messages.

question: A critical vulnerability in the company's VPN appliances is being actively exploited, and the vendor has released a patch. How should applying the patch be handled?
options: As a standard change under a pre-approved procedure
As an emergency change with expedited approval
As a service request handled by the help desk team
As a normal change approved at the next board meeting
explanation: An emergency change handles an urgent risk or outage that cannot wait for the normal schedule, so it gets expedited approval, often from a smaller emergency board, and is fully documented afterward. A normal change would wait for the next board meeting while the flaw is exploited, a standard change covers only pre-approved routine work, and a service request is for routine user requests rather than changes to systems.

question: A browser downloaded a security update in the background several days ago, but the user has kept it running without a break for weeks. What should the technician tell the user?
options: Clear the browser's cache and cookies
Turn on the browser's enhanced protection
Sign out of the browser and sign back in
explanation: Browsers such as Chrome and Edge download updates automatically but finish applying them only when the browser restarts, so one left open for weeks keeps running the vulnerable version. Clearing the cache and cookies removes stored site data, enhanced protection adds stronger Safe Browsing checks, and signing out and back in changes the profile session, but none of them installs the waiting update.

question: An administrator must stop users from choosing passwords shorter than 12 characters and from switching back to a password they used recently. Which two settings meet these requirements?
options: Password complexity and account expiration dates
Minimum password length and password history
Maximum password age and minimum age
Account lockout threshold and lockout duration
explanation: Minimum password length sets the fewest characters a password may have, and password history remembers earlier passwords so that a user cannot reuse them. Lockout threshold and duration respond to failed sign-ins, the maximum and minimum ages control when a password must or may change, and complexity and account expiration dates govern the character mix and when an account stops working.

question: Users at a clinic often walk away from their workstations while still signed in. Which setting makes each workstation ask for a password again after a few idle minutes?
explanation: A screensaver lock, also called a timeout screen lock, locks an idle session after a set number of minutes so that the user must sign in again. An account lockout threshold blocks sign-in after repeated wrong passwords, restricted log-in hours limit when an account can sign in, and a BIOS/UEFI password protects firmware settings and startup.

question: A malware scan reports a startup entry named Updater, stored as a value under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run. The technician wants to delete the value itself, rather than just stop it from starting. Which tool should be used?
explanation: Registry Editor (regedit) opens the registry hives, such as HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, so that a single value like a Run entry can be deleted or changed. Task Manager and the Startup page of Settings can only switch a startup app off, which leaves the value in place, and the Services console controls how services start rather than Run entries.

question: A school is moving its students to Chromebooks. In the design of ChromeOS, how are most applications delivered and most files kept?
options: As remote desktops, with files on a server
As web apps, with files kept in cloud storage
As installed programs, with files on the local drive
As store apps, with files kept in each app
explanation: ChromeOS is built around the Chrome browser, so most of its applications are web apps and most files are kept in cloud storage such as Google Drive. Installed programs with files on the local drive describe Windows, macOS and Linux desktops, store apps that each keep their own files describe the iPadOS model, and remote desktops with files on a server describe a thin-client setup.

question: After an office changed its Wi-Fi password, a Windows 11 laptop fails to join that network and never asks for the new key. Where does the technician remove the saved profile for that one network?
options: Control Panel > User Accounts > Credential Manager
Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks
Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center
Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Hardware properties
explanation: Windows 11 lists saved wireless profiles under Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks, where Forget deletes one profile and its stored key so the user can join again with the new password. Hardware properties shows details of the adapter and its current connection, Credential Manager stores sign-in details for websites and network resources rather than wireless keys, and Network and Sharing Center no longer lists saved wireless networks.

question: A technician sets up a backup job that reads every selected file from a workstation each time it runs, whether or not the file has changed since the last backup. Which backup type is this?
explanation: A full backup copies every selected file each time it runs, whether or not the file has changed, so each run is slow and large but a restore needs only that one backup. An incremental copies only what changed since the previous backup, a differential copies what changed since the last full backup, and a snapshot captures the state of a volume at one moment.

question: A help desk wants to stop users from choosing a new password that matches one of their last several passwords. Which Windows password policy setting does this?
explanation: Enforce password history remembers a set number of previous passwords and blocks their reuse. Minimum password age stops users from cycling through quick changes to get back to an old password but does not block reuse on its own, complexity requires a mix of character types, and the lockout threshold limits failed sign-in attempts.

question: Company email is blocked on any phone that is more than one major version behind the newest iOS or Android release. Which mobile security practice does this MDM rule enforce?
explanation: Keeping phones on a current operating system release means they still receive the vendor's security patches, which is the OS updates part of mobile patch management. Application updates patch individual apps rather than the operating system, device encryption protects stored data if a phone is lost, and antivirus software looks for malicious apps and files.

question: After a driver update, a laptop's wireless adapter stops connecting. The technician wants to put back the driver version that worked before the update. Which tool should the technician use?
explanation: Device Manager can roll a device back to its previous driver from the Driver tab of the device's properties, which undoes a bad driver update. System Information lists drivers without changing them, Event Viewer shows the errors that the adapter logged, and the Services console restarts services such as WLAN AutoConfig rather than drivers.

question: A company's MDM policy stops managed phones from opening gambling and adult websites, wherever the phones connect. Which type of endpoint security does this policy apply?
explanation: Content filtering blocks websites by category, such as gambling or adult content, and an MDM can enforce it on managed devices on any network. A spam filter screens unwanted email, a host firewall allows or blocks connections by port, address or program, and anti-malware software detects and removes malicious code rather than blocking kinds of sites.

question: A technician wants to automate a nightly copy of a Linux server's log files to a backup share, using only what a standard Linux installation provides. Which type of file should the technician write?
explanation: Shell scripts (.sh) run in Bash or another Unix shell that every Linux system includes, so they are the natural choice for a nightly task scheduled with cron. Batch files run in the Windows Command Prompt, VBScript runs under Windows Script Host, and PowerShell is built into Windows but has to be installed separately on Linux.

question: A technician starts diskpart for a new drive and runs list disk and then select disk 1. In what order should the remaining commands run to leave a formatted NTFS volume with a drive letter?
options: clean, create partition primary, format fs=ntfs quick, assign
clean, format fs=ntfs quick, create partition primary, assign
create partition primary, clean, format fs=ntfs quick, assign
create partition primary, format fs=ntfs quick, assign, clean
explanation: In diskpart, clean wipes the selected disk's partition table, create partition primary makes the partition, format fs=ntfs quick formats it and assign gives it a drive letter, in that order. Running clean after create partition primary erases the new partition, format fails while no partition exists, and ending with clean undoes all of the earlier work.

question: A school is setting up 150 identical lab PCs that all need the same office suite, browser and testing app. Which distribution method gets the applications onto every PC fastest and most consistently?
options: Insert each app's vendor disc and run its setup on every PC
Deploy one image that holds the three apps to every PC
Mount one ISO with the three installers on every PC
Download each app's installer package and run it on every PC
explanation: Image deployment installs the applications once on a reference PC, captures that PC as an image and copies it to every machine, so all 150 receive identical, tested installs at once. A mounted ISO, a downloaded package and a vendor disc all still run each setup program on every PC, which suits a few machines rather than a full lab and lets versions and settings drift apart.

question: A technician suspects a memory leak that builds up over several days. Which tool can log counters such as available memory to a file over that whole period and raise an alert when a threshold is crossed?
explanation: Performance Monitor records chosen counters over time in a Data Collector Set and can raise an alert when a counter crosses a set threshold. Resource Monitor and Task Manager show only what is happening now, and Windows Memory Diagnostic tests the RAM itself for faults at restart instead of tracking how programs use memory.

question: Which activity makes an organization of any size subject to PCI DSS?
explanation: PCI DSS is an industry standard set by the major card brands, and it applies to any organization that accepts, processes, stores or transmits payment card data, whatever its size. Medical charts fall under HIPAA in the United States, student records under FERPA, and the personal data of people in the EU under the GDPR.

question: Before approving a public AI service for staff, a security team reviews its terms of service. Which question is MOST important for data security?
options: Whether its answers cite the sources they are drawn from
Whether its license permits commercial use of the content it generates
Whether the provider keeps prompts or uses them to train its models
Whether its uptime commitment meets the company's service targets
explanation: With a public AI service, the provider holds whatever users submit, so data security depends on whether it keeps prompts, trains its models on them and lets its staff see them. Commercial-use terms concern licensing, uptime commitments concern availability, and cited sources concern the accuracy of answers, so none of them decides where company data goes or who can see it.

question: Drivers pay at a city's parking meters by scanning a printed square pattern with their phone camera. Criminals stick look-alike patterns over the real ones, and scanning them opens a convincing payment page that collects card details. What is this attack?
explanation: QR code phishing, or quishing, uses a QR code to send victims to a malicious site, and it works because nobody can tell where a code leads just by looking at it. Vishing uses voice calls, tailgating follows someone through a secure door, and an evil twin is a rogue Wi-Fi access point that imitates a legitimate one.

question: A technician runs Reset this PC on a Windows 11 laptop and chooses Keep my files. What does the reset do?
options: Windows returns to an earlier restore point, files are kept
Windows is reinstalled, files are kept, apps are removed
Windows is reinstalled, files and apps are both kept
Windows is reinstalled, files and apps are both removed
explanation: Reset this PC with Keep my files reinstalls Windows and keeps the personal files in each user profile, but removes the apps and drivers that were installed and resets settings. Keeping both files and apps is what an in-place repair installation does, removing both is the Remove everything choice, and returning to a restore point is System Restore, which does not touch personal files.

question: What distinguishes a whaling attack from other kinds of phishing?
options: It is aimed at senior executives
It is delivered as a voice call
It is sent to many people at once
It is delivered as a text message
explanation: Whaling is phishing aimed at senior executives, such as a chief executive or chief financial officer, so it is defined by whom it targets rather than by how the lure arrives. A lure sent to many people at once is ordinary phishing, one sent as a text message is smishing, and one delivered as a voice call is vishing.

question: A server receives a full backup every Sunday night and a differential backup on each of the other nights. It fails on Thursday afternoon. Which backups are needed to restore it to its most recent backed-up state?
options: Sunday's full and each differential since it
Sunday's full without any of the differentials
explanation: A differential backup holds every change since the last full backup, so a restore needs only that full backup and the latest differential, which here are Sunday's full and Wednesday night's differential. Restoring each backup since the full is what incremental backups require, a differential cannot be restored without the full it builds on, and Sunday's full alone would lose three days of changes.

question: A two-year-old iPhone drops from full to 10 percent in under two hours of light use, and Settings reports a maximum capacity of 71 percent. What should the technician recommend?
explanation: A lithium-ion battery loses capacity with every charge cycle, and once its maximum capacity falls below about 80 percent of the original, replacing the battery is the fix that restores a full day of use. Low Power Mode and limiting Background App Refresh only stretch the charge that is left, and an iOS update helps when a software bug causes the drain rather than a worn battery.

question: A technician finds a browser extension from an unknown publisher that can read every page the user visits, see the browsing history and take screenshots. The user does not need it. What should the technician do?
explanation: An extension that nobody needs, from a publisher nobody can vouch for, with permission to read every page should be uninstalled, because it can collect passwords and personal data from every site the browser opens. Updating it keeps the same permissions and publisher, clearing browsing data erases records but leaves the extension running, and pop-up blocking stops unwanted windows rather than data collection.

question: A company requires multifactor authentication for remote access to its network. Which sign-in combination meets that requirement?
options: A password and the answer to a security question
A smart card and a hardware security key
A password and a code from an authenticator app
A fingerprint scan and a face scan
explanation: Multifactor authentication needs factors from at least two different categories, and a password (something you know) with a code from an authenticator app (something you have) is such a pair. A password with a security answer uses two things you know, a smart card with a security key uses two things you have, and a fingerprint with a face scan uses two things you are, so each of these is still one factor type.

question: A user wants to see which apps may use the laptop's webcam and to turn off access for one of them. Where in Windows 11 Settings is this done?
explanation: Settings > Privacy & security > Camera lists the apps that may use the camera, with a switch for each app as well as one for all apps. Bluetooth & devices > Cameras adjusts or disables the webcam itself, Accounts > Sign-in options sets up face recognition for signing in, and Apps > Advanced app settings controls where apps may be installed from.

question: After a breach at a shopping website, attackers sign in to a user's work email with the same email address and password the user had used on the shopping site. Which practice would have prevented this?
options: Checking for HTTPS before typing in a password
Signing out of the shopping site after each visit
Locking accounts after several failed sign-ins
Using a different password for each account
explanation: Attackers take credentials leaked from one site and try them on others (credential stuffing), so a different password for every account keeps a breach in one place from opening the rest. Account lockout stops repeated wrong guesses, but these attackers had the right password on the first try, HTTPS protects a password in transit rather than in a breached database, and signing out ends a session without changing the stolen password.

question: Equipment went missing from a server room overnight. The manager needs to find out what each person did while inside the room. Which control would provide this?
explanation: Video surveillance records what happens in a space, so its footage shows what each person did there and when. Badge reader logs record whose badge opened the door and when, motion sensor alarms record only that something moved, and visitor sign-in sheets list the guests who signed in at reception, so none of them shows what anyone did inside.

question: A technician with a 10:00 appointment at a client's office is stuck in traffic and will arrive about 30 minutes late. What should the technician do now?
options: Record the reason for the delay in the ticket
Phone the client to give a revised arrival time
Take a faster route to make up the lost time
Apologize to the client in person on arrival
explanation: A technician who is running late should tell the customer before the appointment time and give a realistic new arrival time, so that the customer can plan around the delay. Apologizing on arrival leaves the customer waiting without word, a faster route may not recover half an hour, and recording the delay in the ticket is useful afterward but tells the customer nothing now.

question: A user who can still open other shares on a file server is now denied access to one shared folder that the user could open yesterday. The server's Security log records an audit failure for the user's account at each attempt. What has most likely changed?
options: The drive letter mapped to the folder
The permissions set for the user
The credentials saved for the server
The local Windows profile on the PC
explanation: A server that logs an audit failure for one folder, while the same account still opens other shares on it, is refusing that folder because of its permissions, so the user's permissions on it have most likely changed. Saved credentials for another account would put that account in the log rather than the user's, a changed drive letter would only break the mapping on the PC, and a damaged local profile cannot make the server refuse one folder.

question: A technician tries to assign a Microsoft 365 license to a user whose account was synced from on-premises Active Directory, and the admin center asks for one more detail before it will assign it. Which detail is it MOST likely to be?
explanation: Microsoft 365 needs a usage location, the country where the user will use its services, before it can assign a license, because the services offered vary by country, and accounts synced from on-premises Active Directory often have none. Office location, job title and phone number are optional directory details that do not affect licensing.

question: A technician runs a Python script across hundreds of workstations to record each one's CPU model, memory size and free disk space in a central spreadsheet. Which scripting use case is this?
explanation: Gathering information is a common scripting use case: one script collects details such as hardware specifications from every machine, work that would take hours by hand. Initiating updates installs patches, running automated backups copies data so that it can be restored, and restarting machines reboots computers on a schedule.

question: A user's Windows 11 laptop goes online through a phone's hotspot, which has a small monthly data plan. Which setting for that network makes Windows hold back most update downloads and lets apps cut their background data use?
explanation: Marking a network as a metered connection tells Windows that data on it is limited, so Windows Update holds back most downloads and apps that respect the setting use less background data. Public network hides the PC from other devices without reducing data use, Airplane mode turns off every wireless radio, and Mobile hotspot shares the laptop's own connection with other devices.

question: Logon auditing is turned on for a workstation. A technician now needs to review its successful and failed sign-in attempts to investigate suspected unauthorized access. Which tool shows these records?
explanation: Event Viewer shows the Security log, where Windows records successful sign-ins as event ID 4624 and failed ones as event ID 4625 once auditing is on. Local Security Policy is where that auditing is turned on, not where its records are read, Reliability Monitor charts application failures and updates, and Task Manager shows only the sessions open right now.

question: A technician sets a motherboard on an antistatic mat that is cabled to the bench's ground point. What is the mat's purpose?
options: Shielding stored parts from static fields
Draining static from parts set on it
Carrying fault current from a chassis to ground
explanation: An antistatic mat is a dissipative surface tied to ground, so static charge on a part laid on it bleeds away slowly instead of jumping through the part's circuits. A shielding bag protects a stored part from outside static fields, the ground prong of a power plug carries fault current from a chassis to ground, and an insulating rubber mat protects a worker standing near live wiring.

question: A summer intern has finished. The technician must make the local account intern on a kiosk PC unusable today but keep it, with its settings, for next summer. Which command does this?
explanation: The net user command's /active:no option disables an account so that nobody can sign in with it, while the account and its settings stay in place for /active:yes to turn it back on later. The /delete option removes the account entirely, /times limits sign-in to set days and hours, and /expires with a future date leaves the account usable until that date.

question: On a home PC, the browser's default search engine keeps changing to an unfamiliar one. Resetting the browser fixes it, but the change returns after each restart of the PC. What is the most likely cause?
options: A DNS server setting changed on the home router
A startup program that reapplies the setting
A corrupted user profile in the browser
An outdated browser that needs an update
explanation: A browser reset clears a hijacked search engine, so a hijack that comes back after every restart of the PC is being reapplied by an installed program, such as adware, that runs at startup. A corrupted browser profile would stay fixed after the reset, a DNS change on the router would redirect traffic for every device without changing the browser's setting, and an outdated browser causes crashes and compatibility problems rather than changed settings.

question: Office computers have been contacting a known malicious server at 203.0.113.50. Which router setting would stop all traffic between the office and that one address?
explanation: IP address filtering allows or blocks traffic by source or destination address, so one rule can cut off every connection to a single known malicious server. Content filtering blocks websites by category or keyword, MAC address filtering decides which local devices may join the network, and port forwarding sends inbound connections on a port to an internal host.

question: A contractor's work ends on June 30. Which setting makes sure the contractor's domain account stops working then, even if nobody remembers to disable it?
explanation: An account expiration date, set on the Account tab in Active Directory Users and Computers or with net user's /expires option, stops the account from signing in once that date passes, so temporary accounts do not linger. A password expiration policy only forces a new password, a lockout policy reacts to failed sign-in attempts, and log-in hours limit the time of day.

question: An Android phone can no longer update a banking app, and the Play Store says the device is not compatible with the latest build of the app. What is the most likely cause?
options: The app needs a newer Android version
The app's cached data has become corrupted
The Android System WebView is out of date
The phone has too little free storage space
explanation: Each app release declares the oldest Android version it supports, and the Play Store marks a phone as not compatible when its Android version is older than that minimum. Low storage produces an insufficient space error instead, corrupted cached data makes an installed app crash or misbehave until the cache is cleared, and an outdated Android System WebView breaks web content shown inside apps.

question: A Mac user downloads an app as a disk image file. After the user opens it, its window shows the app's icon. What does the user do next to install the app?
options: Drag the app to the Applications folder
Drag the app's icon onto the Dock
Add the app to Login Items in System Settings
Open the app from the mounted disk image
explanation: An app delivered on a .dmg disk image is installed by dragging its .app bundle into the Applications folder, after which the image can be ejected, and it is removed later by dragging it to the Trash. Putting the icon in the Dock only adds a shortcut, Login Items only opens an installed app at sign-in, and an app run from the mounted image is gone once the image is ejected.

question: Which page shows the installed version of Edge, checks for updates and installs any that are available?
explanation: About Microsoft Edge (edge://settings/help) shows the version, checks for updates and offers to restart the browser when one is ready to apply. The extensions page manages add-ons, the Privacy, search, and services page covers tracking prevention, clearing browsing data and secure DNS, and System and performance covers startup boost, efficiency mode and graphics acceleration.

question: Before upgrading a server, a technician wants to look up which applications and services depend on it. Which resource is designed to record these relationships?
options: An inventory list of the company's assets
A set of incident reports for the server
A knowledge base of support articles
explanation: A configuration management database (CMDB) records configuration items, such as servers, applications and services, and the relationships between them, so it shows what depends on a system before it is changed. An inventory list records which assets exist and who they are assigned to, a knowledge base holds fixes and how-to articles, and incident reports record what happened in past incidents.

question: A technician runs tracert www.example.com at a command prompt to find where traffic to a slow website is being delayed. What does the command list?
options: The address that the site name resolves to
Each router hop and its round-trip time
Each active connection and its current state
Packet loss at each hop over a few minutes
explanation: The tracert command lists each router (hop) on the path to a destination with the round-trip time to each, found by sending packets with a rising TTL. Measuring packet loss at each hop over a period is what pathping adds, nslookup shows the address that a name resolves to, and netstat lists active connections and their states.

question: A user who often types in French wants a French keyboard layout available alongside the English one on a Windows 11 PC. In which Settings category is the layout added?
explanation: Time & language holds the keyboard layouts for each language, under Language & region, along with the Windows display language. Bluetooth & devices pairs and configures keyboards and other hardware, Accessibility holds the on-screen keyboard and other typing aids, and System covers display, sound, power and storage settings.

question: A security team installs a device at the network edge that compares all passing traffic with a baseline of normal behavior and drops connections that depart from it. Which type of system is this?
explanation: A network-based IPS sits in the path of traffic for a whole segment and can drop connections that match an attack signature or depart from its baseline of normal behavior. A network-based IDS examines the same traffic but raises alerts instead of dropping anything, and a host-based IPS or a host-based IDS covers just the one computer it is installed on.

question: An attacker researches a company's payroll clerk on social media, then emails the clerk a message that names their manager and mentions a recent team event, with a link to a fake benefits portal. Which attack is this?
explanation: Spear phishing targets a specific person or small group with a message personalized from research, which makes it more convincing than mass phishing. Whaling is spear phishing aimed at senior executives, smishing uses text messages, and dumpster diving searches discarded material for information.

question: A man wearing a shirt with a well-known IT vendor's logo tells the receptionist he has come to service the servers, and she unlocks the server room for him. Which social engineering technique is this?
explanation: Impersonation means posing as someone with a legitimate reason to be trusted, such as a vendor's technician, so that staff grant access they would otherwise refuse. Tailgating is slipping through a secured door behind an authorized person without permission, shoulder surfing is watching someone enter a password or PIN, and dumpster diving is searching discarded material for information.

question: On one office PC, the browser warns that a banking site's certificate was issued for a different domain name, while other PCs in the same office open the site without any warning. What should the technician suspect?
options: An expired certificate on the web server
An on-path attack intercepting the PC's traffic
An incorrect date and time on the PC
A missing trusted root certificate on the PC
explanation: A certificate issued for a different domain means the browser cannot confirm that it reached the site it asked for, and when only one PC sees it, an on-path attacker intercepting that PC's traffic is the likely cause. An expired certificate on the server would warn on every PC in the office, a wrong clock on the PC produces a date warning rather than a name warning, and a missing root certificate produces a warning that the issuer is not trusted.

question: A website's server moved to a new IP address, and the DNS server already holds the new record, but one workstation still connects to the old address. Which command fixes this on the workstation without a restart?
explanation: The ipconfig /flushdns command empties the local DNS resolver cache at once, so the next lookup goes to the DNS server and returns the new address. The /displaydns switch only lists the cached entries, /registerdns registers the computer's own name in DNS again, and netsh winsock reset repairs the network socket settings and takes effect only after a restart.

question: Which example BEST describes AI application integration?
options: An AI assistant built into a word processor that drafts text in the document
A language model that the company hosts on its own servers
A chatbot website where a user pastes text and copies back the answer
A policy listing the AI tools staff may use and the data they may enter
explanation: Application integration means AI capabilities are built into the tools people already use, such as drafting in a word processor, summarizing a videoconference or analyzing a spreadsheet, using the app's own context. A list of approved tools is an appropriate use policy, a chatbot website used by copying and pasting is a separate tool, and a model hosted on company servers is a private AI deployment.

question: An employee wants company email on a personal phone, but the MDM will not enroll the phone until its owner sets a passcode of at least six characters. Which MDM concept does this apply?
explanation: Profile security requirements are the settings, such as a minimum passcode, that an MDM requires a device to meet before it may enroll or reach company data. A failed login attempts restriction locks or erases a phone after too many wrong passcodes, a remote backup application copies the phone's data to other storage, and a remote wipe erases a lost phone over the network.

question: A technician has repaired a user's mapped drive connection and recorded the steps taken in the ticket. What should the technician do before closing the ticket?
options: Send the user a satisfaction survey
Confirm with the user that the problem is fixed
Submit a change request that covers the fix
Escalate the ticket to the next support tier
explanation: Before a ticket is closed, the technician should confirm with the user that the problem is solved, because the user is the one who can say the fix works in daily use.
