question: A technician on a Windows laptop must see and control the desktop that a user is working on at a Linux workstation. The workstation has no RDP server installed. Which remote access method should the technician use?
explanation: Virtual Network Computing (VNC) shares a computer's graphical desktop with a remote viewer on any major operating system, typically on TCP port 5900. Its traffic should be tunneled through SSH or a VPN, because many VNC setups do not encrypt it. SSH gives a command line rather than the user's desktop, Microsoft Remote Assistance works only between Windows computers, and Windows Remote Management runs commands on Windows systems.

question: Classic Outlook fails to start on a user's PC, and a technician wants to create a new Outlook profile without opening Outlook. Which Control Panel item does this?
explanation: The Mail item, which appears in Control Panel once classic Outlook is installed, creates, repairs and removes Outlook profiles without Outlook running. User Accounts manages Windows sign-in accounts rather than Outlook profiles, Credential Manager stores and clears saved passwords, and Programs and Features can repair the Office installation but does not create profiles.

question: A user reports that a PC has slowed down and that contacts are receiving odd emails from the user's account. Which action does CompTIA's malware removal procedure call for FIRST?
options: Disconnect the PC from the office network
Investigate the symptoms and verify them
Update and run the anti-malware tools
Turn off System Restore on the PC
explanation: CompTIA's malware removal procedure begins by investigating and verifying the symptoms, because slowness and odd emails can also come from other faults or a stolen password. Quarantining the PC by disconnecting it comes next, then turning off System Restore, and updating and running anti-malware tools belongs to remediation.

question: A laptop that is set to obtain an IP address automatically reports the address 169.254.36.10. What does this address show?
options: Its DNS server is not answering name queries
Its subnet mask does not match the network
Its request for a DHCP lease was not answered
Its default gateway points to a wrong router
explanation: Windows assigns itself an APIPA address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range when it is set for DHCP but gets no lease, which lets it reach only other APIPA hosts on the same link. A DNS failure leaves a normal address in place and stops only name lookups, a wrong default gateway still leaves a valid address that works locally, and a wrong subnet mask makes some hosts seem local or remote when they are not.

question: A Windows 11 PC with a static IP address can open shares on servers in its own subnet, but it cannot ping any internet address, even by IP address. Which setting is MOST likely wrong?
explanation: The default gateway is the router address that a PC sends all traffic for other networks to, so a missing or wrong gateway leaves local traffic working while every remote address fails. A wrong DNS server breaks name lookups but not a ping by IP address, a wrong subnet mask usually cuts off some hosts on the local network, and a proxy server setting affects only web traffic.

question: A technician finds a workstation power cord whose third prong was snapped off so that it would fit an old two-slot outlet. Which protection has been lost?
options: Battery power through a short outage
A path for fault current to reach ground
Clamping of voltage spikes from the utility
Cutoff when too many devices share a circuit
explanation: The third prong bonds the metal case to earth ground, so a fault that makes the case live sends current safely to ground and trips the breaker instead of passing through a person. Clamping spikes is the job of a surge suppressor, battery power during an outage comes from a UPS, and the breaker still cuts off an overloaded circuit with or without the ground prong.

question: A phone shows full signal bars at the user's home, but calls made there drop after a minute or two. The drops began the week the household switched internet providers, and calls made anywhere else stay connected. What should the technician test first?
options: Calls after the SIM card is reseated
Calls with Wi-Fi calling turned off
Calls with the phone started in safe mode
explanation: Signal bars show radio strength, not call quality, and at home a phone with Wi-Fi calling may carry calls over the home internet link, so a test with Wi-Fi calling off shows whether the new connection is dropping them. A loose SIM card, an interfering third-party app or a Bluetooth headset would cause trouble away from home as well, and none of them would begin with a change of internet provider.

question: A technician finds that an app with microphone permission has been sending audio recordings to an outside server, although the user never used any recording feature. What type of malware is this?
explanation: Spyware secretly collects information such as audio, messages or location and sends it to the attacker, which is what an app that records and uploads sound without the user's knowledge is doing. Ransomware locks data and demands payment, a rootkit hides malware by gaining deep system access, and adware earns money by showing unwanted ads. Revoking the microphone permission and removing the app stops the leak.

question: A technician is hardening a SOHO router. Which configuration BEST secures access to the router's management interface?
options: Block admin logins from the WAN side and require HTTPS on the LAN
Turn on WPA3 and turn off WPS on the wireless network
Turn on the built-in firewall and turn off UPnP on the router
Turn on content filtering and set up a separate guest network for visitors
explanation: Securing management access means limiting who can reach the admin interface and protecting the session: turn off management from the internet side, use HTTPS or SSH rather than HTTP or Telnet, limit access to the LAN, and replace default credentials. WPA3 and turning off WPS protect the wireless network, the firewall and turning off UPnP protect the perimeter, and content filtering with a guest network controls what users reach, but none of them limits who can open the admin page.

question: A technician has replaced the worn lithium-ion packs in a dozen old laptops. What is the proper way to dispose of the used packs?
options: Place them in the scrap metal recycling bin
Add them to the toner take-back shipment
Take them to a battery recycling drop-off
Send them to the media shredding service
explanation: Used lithium-ion batteries go to a battery recycling drop-off, ideally with their terminals taped, because a damaged cell can start a fire in a garbage truck and the metals inside are worth recovering. A toner take-back shipment is meant for cartridges, a scrap metal bin for old cases and other bare metal, and a media shredding service for drives, where a crushed cell could short and burn.

question: A user who sounds angry reports that the same computer has crashed for the third time this week. How should the technician open the conversation?
options: Explain the steps that the repair will follow
Acknowledge how disruptive the crashes have been
Promise that the computer will be working again today
Transfer the call to the hardware support team
explanation: An upset user should first hear the technician acknowledge the problem and how disruptive it has been, which calms the call and builds the cooperation needed to troubleshoot. Promising a fix today commits to more than is known before any diagnosis, the repair steps cannot be explained until the fault is found, and a transfer passes the user to another team before anyone has listened.

question: A user wants File Explorer to open by itself whenever a USB flash drive is plugged into a Windows 11 PC. Which page under Bluetooth & devices in Settings controls this?
explanation: The AutoPlay page under Bluetooth & devices chooses what Windows does when a removable drive or memory card is connected, such as opening the drive in File Explorer. The USB page controls warnings about USB connection problems, the Devices page adds and removes devices, and Printers & scanners installs and manages printers.

question: Which protocol encrypts only the password field of an access request and sends the other fields, such as the username, in clear text?
explanation: RADIUS hides only the password in an access request, so the username and the other attributes can be read by anyone who captures the traffic. TACACS+ encrypts the whole body of every packet, Kerberos proves identity with tickets and never sends the password at all, and Diameter, the successor to RADIUS in mobile networks, relies on TLS or IPsec to protect its messages.

question: A vulnerability scan finds that a SOHO router is running a three-year-old software version with several published flaws. The manufacturer still supports the model. Which action removes these flaws?
options: Reset the router to factory defaults
explanation: Installing the newest firmware from the manufacturer replaces the vulnerable code with a version in which the published flaws are fixed. A factory reset erases the settings but keeps the same firmware, a new administrator password protects the login without fixing the code, and turning off remote management only limits who can reach the router.

question: A technician tries to turn on Windows Hello facial recognition for a user, but Settings says the option is not available on this laptop, although its built-in 720p webcam works in video calls. What does the laptop lack?
explanation: Windows Hello facial recognition needs a camera that sees in near-infrared light, so that a photograph cannot fool it, and an ordinary webcam captures visible light whatever its resolution. A fingerprint reader is needed for fingerprint sign-in, and a Bluetooth adapter is needed for Dynamic lock, which locks the computer when a paired phone moves away.

question: A technician wants to check the entries in /etc/hosts. Which command prints the whole file in the terminal and returns straight to the prompt?
explanation: The cat command writes the full contents of a file to the terminal and then exits, which makes it the quick way to read a short file. The nano editor stays open until it is closed, ls only confirms that the file exists, and du reports how much disk space the file takes up.

question: A Windows administrator writes a script made up of cmdlets such as Restart-Service to restart the Print Spooler each night. Which file extension should the script have?
explanation: PowerShell scripts use the .ps1 extension, and cmdlets such as Restart-Service, Get-Service and Stop-Service run only in PowerShell. A batch file (.bat) holds Command Prompt commands, a .vbs file holds VBScript for Windows Script Host, and a .sh file holds commands for a Unix shell such as Bash.

question: Two companies are exploring a joint project, and each will share confidential pricing and technical designs with the other. Which agreement fits BEST?
explanation: A mutual non-disclosure agreement (MNDA) binds both parties to protect each other's confidential information, which suits a two-way exchange. A one-way NDA protects only the information of the side that discloses it, a service-level agreement sets service targets, and an end-user license agreement sets the terms for using software.

question: A technician finds that a user keeps a sticky note with several work passwords on the monitor because the user cannot remember them all. Which solution would remove the user's need for the note?
explanation: A password manager stores the user's passwords and fills them in, so the user no longer has to remember them or write them down. A password expiration policy forces more frequent changes and makes remembering harder, a privacy filter only narrows the viewing angle of the screen, and a screen lock protects an unattended session but leaves the note in plain sight.

question: A technician planning a RAM upgrade wants to know how many memory slots are in use and the speed of the installed modules, without opening the case. Which built-in tool shows both?
explanation: The Memory view on the Performance page of Task Manager shows the RAM speed and how many slots are used, such as 2 of 4, along with the form factor. System Information reports the total installed memory without slot or speed details, Resource Monitor shows how processes use memory, and Device Manager does not list memory modules.

question: A user's iPhone still shows the app that was open, but the screen has stopped responding to touch. There is no visible damage and the phone has not been dropped. What should the technician do first?
options: Restore the iPhone in recovery mode
Perform a force restart of the iPhone
explanation: A screen that still shows an image but ignores touch usually means the software has frozen, and a force restart (press Volume Up, press Volume Down, then hold the side button on current models) clears it without erasing data. Restoring in recovery mode is the later step for a phone that still fails after a restart, AssistiveTouch is an on-screen control for a failed physical button and is itself operated by touch, and a new display is for a digitizer that is damaged.

question: A technician must give a user drive letter Z: for the shared folder \\FS01\Projects, using the graphical tools in Windows 11. Which tool does the technician use?
explanation: File Explorer maps a network drive from This PC, where Map network drive assigns a letter such as Z: to a share and can reconnect it at every sign-in. Disk Management assigns letters only to local volumes, Computer Management's Shared Folders creates and manages shares on the local PC, and Network and Sharing Center shows connection status and links to adapter settings.

question: On a home PC, the antivirus icon has vanished from the notification area, and Windows Security reports that no antivirus protection is active. The user did not uninstall or turn off anything. What should the technician suspect?
options: A Windows update removed it as an incompatible program
Malware disabled the antivirus to avoid removal
The antivirus subscription expired last month
A taskbar setting is hiding the antivirus icon from view
explanation: Malware often turns off or removes antivirus software to avoid being detected and removed, and protection that disappears without any action by the user is a strong sign of infection. An expired subscription leaves the program and its warnings in place, Windows turns on Microsoft Defender Antivirus when an update removes another antivirus program, and a hidden icon would not change the protection status that Windows Security reports.

question: A user's browser now uses an unfamiliar search engine and injects ads into every page. An extension installed last week asked for permission to read and change all data on all websites. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Remove the extension from the browser
Clear the browser cache and cookies
Reset the browser's default search engine
Update the extension to its latest version
explanation: Extensions with broad site permissions can hijack searches, inject ads and read page data, so the first step is to remove the suspicious one (at chrome://extensions or edge://extensions), then restore the default search engine and run an anti-malware scan. Updating a malicious extension keeps it installed, resetting the search engine first only lets the extension change it back, and clearing the cache and cookies leaves the extension in place.

question: A records policy requires that retired drives and optical discs be burned in a high-temperature furnace at a licensed facility. Which destruction method does the policy require?
explanation: Incineration burns storage media at very high temperature until only ash and melted residue remain, which leaves nothing readable and works on drives, tapes, discs and paper alike. Shredding cuts media into small pieces, degaussing erases magnetic media with a strong field and has no effect on optical discs, and drilling puts holes through hard drive platters.

question: A retailer's sign-in page receives thousands of attempts, each with a different user name and password pair. Many succeed, and the pairs turn out to match a list leaked from another company's breach. Which attack is this?
explanation: Credential stuffing replays user name and password pairs stolen in one breach against other sites, and it works because many people reuse the same password. Password spraying tries one common password across many accounts, a brute-force attack works through possible passwords one after another, and a rainbow table attack looks up stolen hashes in a precomputed table.

question: An administrator must run a maintenance script on a Windows 11 computer every Monday at 3:00 AM, even when no one is signed in. Which tool should the administrator use to set this up?
explanation: Task Scheduler runs a program or script on a time trigger, such as every Monday at 3:00 AM, and can run it whether or not a user is signed in. Group Policy Editor assigns scripts that run at startup, shutdown, logon or logoff rather than at a set time, Performance Monitor schedules data collector sets, and System Configuration controls how Windows starts.

question: A workstation remembers each user's last 10 passwords, yet some users change their password 10 times within a few minutes to get back to the old one. Which setting stops this?
explanation: Minimum password age makes a user keep a new password for a set number of days, which stops the rapid changes that cycle through the password history back to an old password. Password history is already in place and is what the users are cycling through, minimum password length controls how long a password must be, and a lockout threshold responds to failed sign-ins.

question: After each sign-in, a user's desktop appears quickly, but the PC then responds slowly for several minutes while icons keep appearing in the notification area. Event Viewer shows no errors. What is the most likely cause?
options: A roaming profile that has grown very large
Too many programs set to launch at startup
A damaged registry hive in the profile
A processor fan that has started to fail
explanation: Every program set to start at sign-in competes for the disk and processor in the first minutes after the desktop appears, and the Startup tab of Task Manager shows the impact of each one so that unneeded ones can be turned off. A large roaming profile delays the desktop itself, a damaged profile hive makes Windows load a temporary profile, and a failing fan slows the PC at all times through thermal throttling.

question: A company publishes a document stating which AI tools employees may use, what kinds of data they may enter into them, and that AI output must be reviewed before it is used. What is this?
explanation: An appropriate use policy for AI, often part of the acceptable use policy, sets which tools are approved, what data may be shared with them and how their output must be checked and disclosed. A non-disclosure agreement protects confidential information, a service-level agreement sets service targets, and a data retention policy sets how long records are kept.

question: In ls -l output, a script's permissions appear as -rwxr-xr--. Which octal value would chmod use to set exactly these permissions?
explanation: Each permission group becomes one digit by adding read 4, write 2 and execute 1, so rwx is 7, r-x is 5 and r-- is 4, giving 754. A value of 755 would also let others execute the file, 745 swaps the digits for the group and for others, and 765 would give the group write instead of execute and let others execute.

question: Users at a branch office report that some traffic to headquarters is being dropped. The technician wants the percentage of packets lost at each router along the route, measured over a period of time. Which command provides this?
explanation: The pathping command traces the route to a destination and then sends packets to every hop for a period, reporting the percentage of packets lost at each one. Its -n switch only skips name lookups, while a long ping -n 100 run gives the loss to the destination alone, tracert -h 64 lists up to 64 hops without loss figures, and netstat -e -s shows interface and protocol totals for the local computer.

question: On a standalone Windows 11 PC, an employee who has standard rights now needs administrator rights. Which Control Panel item lets a technician make this change?
explanation: User Accounts changes an account's type between Standard and Administrator, and it also links to the User Account Control settings. Credential Manager stores saved passwords for websites and network resources, Security and Maintenance collects alerts about protection and upkeep, and System leads to System Properties, where user profiles are copied or deleted but account types are not set.

question: An MDM report shows that a managed Android phone has developer options turned on, with USB debugging enabled. Why does the security team want USB debugging switched off?
options: Any app can read other apps' stored data
A connected computer can install apps on the phone
A rental car can copy the phone's contacts
Nearby phones can send it files unprompted
explanation: USB debugging lets a computer connected by cable control the phone through ADB, including installing apps and copying data, so a managed phone should keep it off. A rental car copies contacts only after the phone pairs with it and shares them, receiving files from strangers comes from a sharing setting, and apps reading each other's data is the risk of a rooted phone rather than of USB debugging.

question: Each weekend, a backup server builds a new complete backup of a workstation by merging the last complete backup with the incremental backups taken since, without reading the workstation's files again. Which backup type is this?
explanation: A synthetic full backup is assembled on the backup server from the last full backup and the incrementals taken since, so it gives a one-set restore without copying everything from the source again. A differential copies every change since the last full backup from the source, an incremental copies only the changes since the previous backup, and a snapshot records the state of a volume at one moment.

question: Which encryption method did WPA2 make mandatory for every certified device?
explanation: WPA2 requires AES-CCMP, which uses the AES cipher in counter mode for privacy and CBC-MAC for integrity, and every WPA2-certified device must support it. TKIP is the stopgap that came with the original WPA, WEP-104 is the original WEP with its longer key, and RC4 is the stream cipher that WEP and TKIP both use.

question: A user's personal iPhone sends all web traffic through an unknown VPN and lists an unfamiliar profile under Settings > General > VPN & Device Management. The user installed it from a free streaming website. What should the technician do?
options: Turn off the profile's VPN in Settings, then forget the Wi-Fi network
Change the Apple ID password, then turn on two-factor authentication
Remove the profile, then change the passwords used on the phone
Install the latest iOS update, then clear Safari's history and data
explanation: Configuration profiles can install VPNs, proxies and root certificates that let an attacker intercept traffic, so a profile from an untrusted website should be removed, which also removes its settings. Passwords used while it was installed should then be changed. An iOS update and clearing Safari's data leave the profile in place, a new Apple ID password protects one account while traffic is still intercepted, and turning off its VPN or forgetting the Wi-Fi network leaves the profile and any certificate it added installed.

question: A technician copies a script named inventory.py from a Linux server, where it runs, to a new Windows 11 laptop. On the laptop, Windows asks which app should open the file. What should the technician do so that the script can run?
options: Run it from the Command Prompt
Run it with Windows Script Host
explanation: Python scripts (.py) run on Windows, macOS and Linux alike, but only where the Python interpreter is installed, and Windows does not include it. Windows Script Host runs VBScript and JScript files, the Command Prompt runs batch files, and the execution policy governs PowerShell scripts, so none of them can run Python code.

question: Two employees install the same program on their computers. One sees a prompt with Yes and No buttons, while the other must type an administrator's user name and password. What explains the difference?
options: The second employee's sign-in uses a Windows Hello PIN
The second employee's account is a Microsoft account
The second employee's account is a standard user account
The second employee's PC has UAC at its highest level
explanation: Under User Account Control, an administrator sees a consent prompt with Yes and No, while a standard user sees a credentials prompt and must type an administrator's name and password. Setting UAC to its highest level changes when an administrator is prompted, not the kind of prompt, and signing in with a PIN or a Microsoft account does not change whether an account is an administrator.

question: An office owns a degausser and has a box of old storage media to sanitize before disposal. Which items in the box can the degausser sanitize?
explanation: A degausser erases only magnetic media, such as backup tapes and hard disk drives, by scrambling the magnetic patterns that hold the data. Solid-state drives and USB flash drives store data as electrical charges in flash memory, and DVD-R discs store it as marks that a laser reads, so a magnetic field leaves the data on all three intact.

question: A technician sets up one laptop with Windows 11, the company's apps and its settings, generalizes it with Sysprep, captures it, and copies it onto 200 new laptops of the same model. Which installation method is the technician using?
explanation: Image deployment copies one prepared and generalized system, with its apps and settings, onto many computers of the same kind. A clean install starts each computer from blank installation media, a repair install reinstalls Windows over itself to fix damaged system files, and an in-place upgrade moves one existing system to a newer version while keeping its apps and data.

question: A user wants to stop a chat program from launching at sign-in and to uninstall a game, both from Windows 11 Settings. Which Settings category holds both tasks?
explanation: Settings > Apps holds Startup, which stops apps from launching at sign-in, and Installed apps, where apps and games are uninstalled. Accounts manages sign-in methods and users rather than what runs after sign-in, Gaming holds Game Mode and capture settings but does not remove games, and System covers the display, sound, storage and power pages.

question: Task Manager on a slow PC shows scvhost.exe using 70 percent of the CPU, although the real Windows process is svchost.exe. Which malware technique does this show?
options: Hiding its own process from Task Manager
Naming itself to look like a system process
Running in memory inside a PowerShell session
Injecting its code into a genuine system process
explanation: Malware often gives its file a name one or two letters away from a real Windows process, such as scvhost.exe for svchost.exe, so that it passes a quick look in Task Manager. Code injected into a genuine process would appear under the real name, a rootkit that hides its process would not appear in Task Manager at all, and a script running in memory would appear as PowerShell.

question: A Mac user wants one search box, opened from the magnifying glass in the menu bar, that finds apps, documents, emails and contacts across the whole Mac. Which macOS feature provides it?
explanation: Spotlight is the system-wide search of macOS, opened from the menu bar or with Command+Space, and it finds apps, files, mail, contacts and web suggestions from one box. Finder searches for files and folders inside its own window, Siri answers spoken or typed requests, and Safari searches the web from its address bar.

question: A caller who says he works on the company help desk asks an employee to read him the sign-in code that the company's system has just sent to her phone by text message. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: Vishing is phishing by voice call, where the caller poses as someone trusted, such as the help desk, to talk the victim into giving up a password or a sign-in code. The text message came from the company's own system, so this is not smishing, which relies on a fraudulent text; whaling targets senior executives, and QR code phishing hides a malicious link in a QR code.

question: A user wants Windows 11 and its apps to switch to dark mode, with light text on dark backgrounds. Where in Settings is this changed?
explanation: Personalization > Colors holds Choose your mode, which switches Windows and apps between light and dark. Night light warms the screen's colors in the evening, HDR controls high dynamic range output on screens that support it, and Personalization > Start arranges the Start menu's layout and suggestions.

question: A local account has Full control NTFS permission on a sensitive folder, but company policy allows that account only Read. Where should the technician correct the permission?
explanation: NTFS permissions such as Full control and Read are set on the Security tab of the folder's Properties, where the account's entry can be changed. The Sharing tab sets share permissions, which apply only to access over the network, Local Security Policy sets password, audit and user rights policies, and Local Users and Groups manages accounts and group membership.

question: A note-taking app downloaded from the Play Store keeps stopping on an Android phone several times a day, and clearing the app's cache and storage did not help. What should the technician do next?
explanation: Reinstalling replaces the app's program files as well as its data, so it is the next step when clearing the cache and storage has not stopped the crashes. Force stopping is for an app that hangs and will not close, safe mode turns off every third-party app including this one, and a factory reset erases the whole phone and is kept for faults that survive a reinstall.

question: A user installs a free VPN app from an unknown developer on a personal phone that also holds corporate email. Why does the IT team treat the app as a risk?
options: It can change other apps' permissions
It can see the traffic of other apps
It can read files in other apps' private storage
It can log keys typed into other apps
explanation: A VPN app carries every connection the phone makes through its operator's servers, so a rogue VPN can log the traffic of every other app, read anything sent unencrypted and redirect connections to fake sites. Reading files in other apps' private storage needs a rooted or jailbroken phone, logging keystrokes is the risk of a third-party keyboard granted full access, and changing other apps' permissions is left to the user or an MDM.

question: In /etc/fstab, the last field is 1 for the root file system, 2 for a local data volume and 0 for a network share. What do these values control?
options: The order in which fsck checks the file systems at boot
The order in which the file systems are mounted at boot time
Whether the dump utility backs up each file system
The number of mounts permitted before fsck forces a check
explanation: The sixth and last field of /etc/fstab, fs_passno, sets the order of the boot-time fsck checks: 1 for the root file system, 2 for the others, and 0 to skip the check, which suits network shares. It does not set the mount order, the fifth field is the flag that tells the dump utility whether to back up a file system, and the number of mounts allowed between forced checks is set with tune2fs rather than in fstab.

question: An infected Windows 11 Home PC has been quarantined and is ready for remediation. Which task should the technician perform before scanning it?
options: Create a restore point to roll back to
Schedule recurring scans of the PC
Show the user how to recognize phishing
explanation: Remediation starts by updating the anti-malware software, because a scanner with old definitions can miss recent malware. A restore point made now could capture the infection, recurring scans are scheduled after the malware has been removed, and teaching the user to recognize phishing is the last step of the procedure.

question: Employees sign in to their domain-joined PCs with Active Directory accounts but have to remember a separate password for the company's Microsoft 365 apps. What should be deployed so they use the same user name and password for both?
options: Hybrid identity with Microsoft Entra Connect
Self-service password reset for the cloud accounts
Microsoft Authenticator on each employee's phone
A password manager on each user's PC
explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect syncs on-premises Active Directory accounts to Microsoft Entra ID, which Microsoft 365 uses, and with password hash synchronization users sign in to cloud apps with their AD password. A password manager still holds two passwords, self-service password reset only lets users reset a cloud password themselves, and Microsoft Authenticator adds a second sign-in factor without linking the two accounts.

question: At a small office, the router and switch sit on an open shelf in the reception area, where visitors and cleaning staff pass them every day. Which measure keeps these people from physically reaching the devices?
options: Watch the shelf with a video camera
Lock them inside an equipment cabinet
Fit a badge reader to the front door
Fasten them to the shelf with cable locks
explanation: Routers and switches belong in a locked cabinet or closet, because anyone who can touch them can reset them, plug into them or carry them off. Cable locks stop the devices from being carried away but leave them within reach, a video camera records access without preventing it, and a badge reader controls who enters the building but not what admitted visitors and cleaning staff can reach.

question: Photos and contacts from a user's phone appear on a public website, including photos that were never backed up to any cloud service. A week earlier, the user gave a new photo-editing app access to both. What is the most likely source of the leak?
options: A cloned copy of the SIM card
A breach of the user's cloud backup
explanation: An app granted access to photos and contacts can copy them to its own servers, and leaked photos that never reached a cloud service point to software on the phone itself, here the newly installed app. A cloud breach could expose only what was backed up, a cloned SIM card gives access to calls and texts rather than photos, and bluesnarfing targets old phones with vulnerable Bluetooth rather than data an app was given.

question: Company rules require accounts on a Windows 11 Pro workstation that is not joined to a domain to lock after five failed sign-in attempts. Which tool is used to set this?
explanation: On a workstation outside a domain, the account lockout threshold is set in Local Security Policy, under Account Policies and then Account Lockout Policy. Local Users and Groups creates, disables and unlocks individual accounts, Credential Manager stores saved sign-in details, and the Windows Security app manages antivirus and sign-in protection features such as Windows Hello.

question: An AI assistant summarizes a 40-page vendor contract for a manager. Which practice BEST addresses the accuracy limitations of AI?
options: Have the manager approve the summary before it goes on file
Switch to an AI model that reads the whole contract at once
Have a second AI tool review the summary for missed points
Have a person check the key points against the contract
explanation: AI output can omit, misread or invent details, so a person checks it against the source, especially dates, amounts and commitments. A second AI tool can make the same kinds of mistakes, a model that reads the whole contract at once can still misread it, and a manager's approval without comparing the summary with the contract approves whatever errors it holds.

question: A company in the United States wants its repair technicians to follow federal workplace safety rules, such as those for handling hazardous chemicals and wearing protective equipment. Which agency sets and enforces those rules?
explanation: OSHA, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, sets and enforces workplace safety rules in the United States, including the hazard communication rules that require safety data sheets. NIOSH researches workplace hazards and recommends limits but does not enforce them, NIST publishes technical standards such as its media sanitization guidance, and the EPA regulates pollution and waste disposal rather than worker safety.

question: A company sends all employee web traffic through a filtering server before it reaches the internet. What should a technician do in the browser on each workstation so that its requests go to that server?
explanation: A proxy setting tells the browser to send its web requests to an intermediate server, which can filter, log or cache them before they reach the internet. A secure DNS server only answers name lookups over an encrypted connection, safe browsing warns about known malicious sites, and browser data sync copies bookmarks and passwords to the user's account.

question: An iPhone shows a strong Wi-Fi connection, but no web pages or online apps load on it. Other devices on the same network work normally, and turning Wi-Fi off and on did not help. Which step should the technician take next without erasing the phone's other saved networks?
options: Restart the router and the modem
explanation: When one phone has a Wi-Fi connection but no internet while other devices on that network are fine, forgetting and rejoining the network clears the phone's saved settings for it and requests a new address. Restarting the router and modem is for an outage that affects every device, a network settings reset is the broader step that erases every saved network if rejoining fails, and an iOS update is a later step for a fault that follows the phone onto every network.

question: A small office's router supports nothing newer than WPA2-Personal. An attacker who captures a device's handshake could then test guesses offline. Which step limits that risk?
options: Turn off WPS on the router
explanation: A captured WPA2-Personal handshake can be tested against guesses offline at high speed, so the protection that matters is a long random passphrase that no wordlist contains. Turning off WPS stops attacks on its setup PIN, AES-CCMP protects the data more strongly than TKIP but does nothing to slow passphrase guessing, and changing the router's admin password protects its settings page rather than the wireless traffic.

question: A facility's entrance is a small room with two doors. The inner door will not open until the outer door has closed and the person inside has presented a badge again. What is this arrangement called?
explanation: An access control vestibule, once called a mantrap, holds a person between two interlocked doors until they are authorized, which stops tailgating. A guard checkpoint relies on a person checking identity, an electromagnetic lock holds a single door shut until it is released, and an optical turnstile lets one person through at a time without an enclosed space.

question: Why should a company check data retention requirements before wiping and recycling its old file servers?
options: Classification labels set the wipe method, so each drive is labeled before the wipe
Record-keeping laws set how long files must be kept, so they are archived before the wipe
Sanitization standards set the overwrite passes, so drives are wiped that many times
E-waste laws decide how hardware is recycled, so a certified recycler is chosen
explanation: Retention requirements, from tax and healthcare rules to legal holds, set how long records must be kept, so records still inside their period must be migrated or archived before the hardware is sanitized. The number of overwrite passes comes from sanitization standards, the wipe method from data classification and the choice of recycler from e-waste rules, and none of them decides which records must be kept.

question: A parent wants their child's iPhone to keep Safari from opening sexually explicit sites, without buying third-party software. Which built-in feature should the technician set up?
options: Software Update, with automatic downloads and installs turned on
VPN & Device Management, with a new VPN configuration that applies to Safari
Screen Time's Content & Privacy Restrictions, set to Limit Adult Websites
Location Services, turned off for Safari in the Privacy & Security settings
explanation: Screen Time's Content & Privacy Restrictions include a Web Content setting that can limit adult websites or allow only listed sites, a content filter built into iOS. VPN & Device Management lists profiles and VPN configurations, Location Services controls access to location, and Software Update installs iOS updates.

question: A technician sets the PowerShell execution policy on a shared kiosk computer to Restricted. Which of these will the policy then prevent from running?
options: A VBScript file run by WSH
explanation: The Restricted policy, the default on Windows client computers, blocks every PowerShell script file while still allowing commands typed at the prompt. Execution policy applies only to PowerShell, so batch files run by the Command Prompt and VBScript files run by Windows Script Host are not affected, and a typed cmdlet such as Get-Service still runs.

question: A technician needs to see just the lines of app.log that contain the word timeout. Which command prints them?
explanation: The grep command prints each line of a file, or of piped output, that matches a pattern, so grep timeout app.log shows just the lines that mention timeout. The find command looks for files whose names match, tail -f follows new lines as they are added to a file, and cat prints every line of the file.

question: A company wants to be warned about attack attempts on its internal network, with no chance that its own monitoring blocks legitimate traffic. Which technology should it deploy?
explanation: An intrusion detection system watches network traffic and raises alerts about attacks but does not block anything, so it cannot interrupt legitimate traffic by mistake. An intrusion prevention system and a next-generation firewall sit in the traffic path and drop what they judge malicious, and network access control decides which devices may join the network at all.

question: A company requires every Windows 11 PC to send all web requests through a server at 10.20.0.8 on port 8080, which fetches pages on the PC's behalf. Under Network & internet in Settings, which page does a technician use to set this up?
explanation: Windows 11 sets a proxy server for the whole PC under Settings > Network & internet > Proxy, where a manual setup takes the server's address and port and an automatic setup takes a script address. Ethernet and Wi-Fi hold the IP and DNS settings of each connection, and VPN adds and manages VPN connections, which carry traffic through an encrypted tunnel rather than a web proxy.

question: A technician is setting up the Outlook desktop app for a new employee whose mailbox is in Microsoft 365. What does the technician normally need to enter?
options: The IMAP and SMTP server names and their port numbers
The user's email address and a product key
The user's email address and then their password
The Exchange server name and the user's domain
explanation: Microsoft 365 supports Autodiscover, so Outlook needs only the user's email address and a sign-in, with MFA if required, and then finds the mailbox settings itself. IMAP and SMTP server names and ports are entered by hand only for providers without automatic setup, naming an Exchange server manually belongs to older on-premises setups that current Outlook versions no longer offer, and Microsoft 365 apps activate through the user's sign-in rather than a product key.

question: After a Linux update on a dual-boot UEFI laptop, the PC always starts the Linux loader, which no longer offers Windows. The Windows partition is intact. What should the technician do first to start Windows?
options: Run bootrec /fixmbr from the Windows recovery prompt
Choose Windows Boot Manager in the firmware boot menu
Turn off Secure Boot in the firmware settings
Run System Restore from recovery media
explanation: On a UEFI computer each installed system has its own entry in the firmware's boot list, so choosing Windows Boot Manager there starts Windows even when the Linux loader no longer lists it. The bootrec /fixmbr command rewrites the master boot record of an older BIOS disk, turning off Secure Boot lets unsigned loaders run, and System Restore returns Windows settings to an earlier point without changing which loader the firmware starts.

question: On a Linux workstation, df -h shows the file system holding /var at 97% used. What is the BEST next step to find what is using the space?
options: Run sudo du -sh /var/* and then examine the largest subdirectory
Run ls -lh /var and compare the sizes of the files it lists
Run sudo fsck on the /var file system and repair any errors it reports
Run df -i and check whether the file system has run out of inodes
explanation: The df command shows how full each file system is, and du breaks that use down by directory, so du -sh /var/* totals each item in /var and leads to the largest, often /var/log or a cache. The fsck tool repairs file system errors rather than freeing space, df -i reports inode use, which matters when writes fail while space remains, and ls -lh shows the size of each directory entry rather than the total of its contents.

question: A technician checks whether an older desktop can be upgraded in place to Windows 11. It has a supported 64-bit CPU, 8 GB of RAM, a 256 GB SSD and UEFI firmware with Secure Boot. What else must it have?
explanation: Windows 11 requires a TPM 2.0 chip in addition to UEFI firmware with Secure Boot, a supported CPU, at least 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage. A TPM 1.2 chip works with BitLocker on Windows 10 but does not meet the Windows 11 requirement, an NVMe drive is faster but not required, and an NPU is needed only for Copilot+ PC features.

question: A technician must encrypt an entire USB flash drive so that it can be unlocked with a password on other Windows computers. Which feature should the technician use?
explanation: BitLocker To Go encrypts a whole removable drive and unlocks it with a password or smart card on other Windows computers. Device encryption protects only a computer's internal drives, EFS encrypts individual files with a key tied to one user's account, and NTFS compression saves disk space without encrypting anything.

question: A user's start page and search provider have switched to a site the user does not recognize, and clicking search results opens advertising pages. Which type of malware is most likely responsible?
explanation: A browser hijacker changes the home page and search engine and sends searches through pages that earn the attacker advertising money. A boot sector virus infects the code that starts the computer, a cryptominer loads the processor to mine cryptocurrency, and a keylogger records keystrokes to steal passwords, so none of them explains changed browser settings.

question: Users report that a cloud application is slow. Which command, run on a Linux workstation, shows each router between the workstation and the application's server, with the response time at each hop?
explanation: The traceroute command lists each router (hop) on the path to a destination with its round-trip times, which shows where along the path the delay begins. A ping, even of 100 packets, measures only the round trip to the destination itself, dig looks up DNS records, and ip route show displays the workstation's own routing table rather than the path across the network.

question: A colleague sends a technician a .sh script to run on a Windows 11 workstation. Which environment would let the technician run the script without rewriting it?
explanation: A .sh file is a shell script for Bash or another Unix shell, so on Windows it needs a Linux environment such as the Windows Subsystem for Linux to run unchanged. Windows Script Host runs VBScript and JScript files, Windows PowerShell runs .ps1 scripts and the Command Prompt runs batch files, and none of them reads Bash syntax.

question: A technician installs Ubuntu Desktop on a new laptop and accepts the installer's default disk layout. Which file system is the root partition formatted with?
explanation: Ubuntu and Debian format the root partition with ext4 by default, the journaling file system native to Linux. XFS is the default on Red Hat Enterprise Linux, APFS is the default file system of macOS, and FAT32 is used on a UEFI computer only for the small EFI system partition that holds the boot loader.

question: A small office's owner wants to manage the office router from home. Which approach allows this MOST securely?
options: Turn on WAN-side management over HTTPS with a long admin password
Connect over a VPN, then open the router's admin page at its LAN address
Move remote management to a nonstandard port, such as 8443, on the WAN side
Forward port 3389 to the office PC, then open the router's page from that PC
explanation: A VPN authenticates and encrypts the connection into the office network, so the router's admin page never has to face the internet. WAN-side management over HTTPS still exposes the login page to every attacker online, however long its password, forwarding port 3389 exposes Remote Desktop, a frequent target of attacks, and a nonstandard port only hides the exposed admin page from casual scans.

question: An organization's standard applications are updated almost every month, and rebuilding its Windows image each time is taking too long. Which change BEST reduces the work while keeping deployments consistent?
options: Install Windows and the apps on each PC from a USB installer drive
Use a thin image and add the apps afterward from current packages
Use one thick image per department with that department's apps built in
Rebuild the thick image monthly on a faster build server
explanation: A thin image holds only the OS and baseline settings, and the applications are added after deployment from current packages, so an app update changes one package instead of the whole image. Thick images per department multiply the images to rebuild, installing from a USB drive on each PC gives up consistency, and a faster build server shortens each rebuild without removing the monthly work.

question: On a Windows 10 workstation, which Control Panel item opens a folder of shortcuts to Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, Services and Performance Monitor?
explanation: Administrative Tools is the Control Panel folder of shortcuts to management consoles such as Event Viewer, Task Scheduler, Services and Performance Monitor. Windows 11 renames it Windows Tools. Programs and Features removes programs and turns Windows features on or off, Security and Maintenance lists alerts about firewall, virus protection and backup status, and System shows the computer's specifications and name.

question: A firm is deciding whether to buy Windows 11 Pro for Workstations rather than Windows 11 Pro for its new engineering computers. Which capability would that edition add?
explanation: Pro for Workstations adds support for persistent memory modules (NVDIMM-N), together with SMB Direct file sharing and room for more processors and memory than Pro allows. Windows Sandbox, Assigned Access kiosk mode and BitLocker drive encryption are already part of Windows 11 Pro, so paying for the upgrade would not add them.

question: A seized laptop passes from the technician who found it to a manager and then to a police investigator, and each person signs and dates a form at every hand-off. Which forensic practice is this?
explanation: Chain of custody is the signed and dated record of everyone who has held a piece of evidence, and a gap in it can make the evidence unusable in court. Order of volatility sets which data to collect first, a legal hold stops records from being deleted, and disk imaging makes an exact copy of a drive for examination.

question: Which encryption protocol came with the original WPA, is now deprecated, and should be disabled on any router that still offers it?
explanation: TKIP arrived with the original WPA as a stopgap that could run on WEP-era hardware, and it is now deprecated, so a router should use AES-CCMP instead. CCMP is the AES-based protocol that WPA2 requires, GCMP-256 is used by the 192-bit mode of WPA3-Enterprise, and WEP-104 is the original WEP with its longer key, which WPA was created to replace.

question: A new video editing desktop has 192 GB of RAM, but Windows reports that only 128 GB of it is usable, and the memory passes every hardware test. Which Windows 11 edition is the desktop running?
explanation: Windows 11 Home can use at most 128 GB of RAM, so memory above that is installed but unusable until the computer moves to a higher edition. Windows 11 Pro can use up to 2 TB, and Pro for Workstations and Enterprise can each use up to 6 TB.

question: An Android phone used several gigabytes of its mobile plan overnight, mostly around 3 AM while it sat idle on its charger. Which screen should the technician check first to find the cause?
explanation: Heavy data use while a phone sits idle at night suggests an app, often malware, sending data in the background, and the per-app data usage list shows which app moved the data so that it can be investigated and removed. The storage list shows space rather than traffic, the permissions list shows what apps may access rather than what they sent, and the saved networks list matters when a phone joins networks it should not.

question: On a crowded train, a Bluetooth pairing request from an unknown device appears on a user's phone, and the user accepts it without reading it. Which practice would most likely have kept such requests from reaching the phone?
options: Using a VPN on public networks
explanation: A phone in discoverable mode announces itself to every nearby device, so keeping Bluetooth non-discoverable except while deliberately pairing, or off when not in use, keeps strangers from finding it and sending pairing requests. Removing old pairings tidies the list afterward but does not stop new requests, turning off automatic Wi-Fi joining protects against evil twin networks, and a VPN protects traffic on public Wi-Fi.

question: After malware was removed from a PC, a user cannot open files the user created. Each file's Security tab lists an unfamiliar account as owner with full control, and even an administrator cannot change the permissions. What should the technician do first?
options: Add the user to the share permissions
Take ownership of the files from the other user
Clear the read-only attribute on the files
Decrypt the files with an EFS certificate
explanation: An administrator can take ownership of any file, and a file's owner can change its permissions, so taking ownership is the first step when the permission list cannot be edited, after which the user's access can be added back. A read-only attribute stops changes but still lets a file open, EFS encryption would need the encrypting account's key rather than new permissions, and share permissions apply only when files are opened over the network.

question: A technician has removed malware from a Windows 11 Home PC, set up recurring scans and installed the latest updates. Which step of CompTIA's procedure comes next?
options: Run another full scan from bootable external media
Reimage the PC from a known-good image
Enable System Restore and create a restore point
Educate the user and explain how the malware got in
explanation: CompTIA's malware removal procedure turns System Restore back on and creates a fresh restore point once scans are scheduled and updates are run, so that the first new restore point is a clean one. Educating the user is the final step that follows, reimaging is the remediation option for malware that cannot be removed, and a further bootable scan belongs to remediation.

question: While installing a free PDF converter, a user leaves a preselected box checked, and a browser toolbar and a PC cleanup tool are installed with it. Neither is built to cause harm, but the antivirus flags both. Which category of software are they?
explanation: A potentially unwanted program is bundled software that the user technically agreed to install, such as a toolbar or a cleanup tool, and antivirus flags it because it is unwanted rather than malicious. A remote access Trojan hides a tool that gives an attacker control of the computer, fileless malware runs in memory through built-in tools, and a boot sector virus infects the code that starts the computer.

question: A sales representative's company phone falls into a lake. IT issues a replacement, but the contacts, notes and photos from the old phone cannot be recovered. Which feature would have prevented this loss?
explanation: A remote backup application copies a phone's data to cloud or company storage on a schedule, so it can be restored to a replacement phone after a loss. A locator application only shows where a missing phone is, device encryption keeps data on the phone unreadable to others without saving a copy, and a selective wipe removes company data from a phone rather than preserving it.

question: On a Windows 11 Pro computer that is not in a domain, a technician must create a new group, add three existing accounts to it and later disable one of the accounts. Which tool is built for these tasks?
explanation: Local Users and Groups (lusrmgr.msc) creates local groups, sets their membership and disables local accounts on Pro and higher editions. The netplwiz tool can put an account into an existing group but cannot create groups or disable accounts, and Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) and Local Security Policy (secpol.msc) set account policies such as password length rather than managing the accounts themselves.

question: A port scan run from outside a home office shows that the login page for the router's settings can be reached from the internet. Which change removes this exposure?
options: Disable remote management from the WAN
Turn off UPnP on the home router
explanation: Turning off remote management makes the router's settings page answer only on the local network, which removes it from the internet altogether. Turning off UPnP stops devices from opening ports by themselves, a firmware update patches known flaws without changing who can reach the page, and a stronger password protects the login while leaving the page on the internet.

question: A user's documents are disappearing, and in their place are files with the same names plus an unfamiliar extension that no program can open. The drive passes its health check. Which type of malware is most likely responsible?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts the user's files, usually renames them with a new extension, and then demands payment for the key, so documents replaced by unreadable copies with an added extension point to it. A cryptominer uses the processor without touching files, a browser hijacker changes browser settings, and a boot sector virus infects the code that starts the computer rather than the user's documents.

question: A user has started using the same login for dozens of websites because unique ones are hard to remember. Which browser feature can generate, store and fill in a different strong login for each site?
explanation: A password manager generates a strong, unique password for each site, stores them encrypted and fills them in, so the user has to remember only one master password. Browser data sync copies saved items between devices, private browsing discards history when the window closes, and clearing browsing data deletes stored records.

question: On a website's sign-in form, an attacker enters ' OR '1'='1 in the password field. The site passes the input straight into its database query and signs the attacker in without a valid password. Which attack is this?
explanation: SQL injection works when a site builds database queries from user input without checking it, so input such as ' OR '1'='1 changes the query's logic, here making the password check come out true. Cross-site scripting injects script that runs in other users' browsers, a brute-force attack guesses passwords until one works, and a replay attack resends captured traffic, such as a valid session, to gain access.

question: An administrator changed several Group Policy settings for a domain. Which command makes a workstation reapply every policy setting right away, including settings that have not changed?
explanation: The gpupdate /force command reapplies every Group Policy setting at once, changed or not, instead of waiting for the background refresh of about 90 minutes. Without /force, gpupdate /target:user applies only the changed user settings, and the /boot and /logoff switches restart the computer or sign the user out after the refresh when a setting needs it.

question: An approved change to a branch office's routing causes an outage, and the team must put the routers back to their previous working configuration. Which part of the change documentation sets out how to do this?
explanation: A rollback plan gives the steps, and the saved configuration, needed to undo a change and return systems to their last working state if the change fails. The risk level rates how likely and how harmful a failure would be, the affected systems section lists what the change will touch, and the scope defines what the change includes.

question: An administrator assigns a script that runs as each user signs in and connects H: and S: to that user's shared folders on the file server. Which scripting use case is this?
explanation: Remapping network drives is a standard logon script task: each time a user signs in, the script connects drive letters to shared folders so that everyone sees the same layout. Installing applications adds software, backing up user files copies data so that it can be restored, and restarting machines reboots computers, usually after updates.

question: A growing company asks its IT department to adopt a formal change management process. What is the main goal of such a process?
options: To restore normal service as quickly as possible after an outage
To reduce the risk that modifications to systems cause outages
To track each hardware asset from purchase through to disposal
To find and remove the underlying causes of repeated faults
explanation: Change management exists to reduce the risk that modifications to systems cause outages, by having each change planned, assessed, approved and recorded before it is made. Restoring service after an outage is incident management, removing the causes of repeated faults is problem management, and tracking assets from purchase to disposal is asset management.

question: A packet capture of a remote management session to a network switch shows the administrator's password as plain, readable text. Which protocol carried the session?
explanation: Telnet sends everything, including usernames and passwords, as unencrypted text over TCP port 23, so anyone capturing the traffic can read it. SSH carries the same kind of command-line session inside encryption, HTTPS protects a switch's web interface with TLS, and SNMPv3 adds the authentication and encryption that earlier SNMP versions lacked.

question: A technician opens the Ethernet page of a Windows 11 PC's Settings to give it a fixed address, subnet mask and default gateway. Which setting on that page does the technician edit?
explanation: On a Windows 11 connection's page in Settings, IP assignment switches between Automatic (DHCP) and Manual, and Manual is where a fixed address, subnet and gateway are entered. DNS server assignment sets only the DNS servers, Network profile type chooses between Public and Private, and Metered connection limits background data on that network.

question: A user grows defensive and insists that nothing was changed before a problem began, but the symptoms point to a newly installed program. How should the technician respond to the user?
options: Take the user at their word and look elsewhere
Show the user the log entry for the new install
Ask what the user was doing when it started
Escalate the ticket to a more senior colleague
explanation: With a defensive user, the technician should ask nonjudgmental, open-ended questions, such as what the user was doing when the problem started, which help the user recall recent activity without feeling accused. Showing a log that contradicts the user turns the call into an argument, looking elsewhere drops the likeliest cause, and escalation is for a fault beyond the technician's skill rather than a difficult conversation.

question: A new workstation is installed inside a closed cabinet under a desk, with its rear vents almost touching the cabinet's back panel. It now shuts down without warning after about an hour of use. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Static from the carpet under the desk
Heat building up around the case
Dust packed into the heat sink fins
explanation: A computer needs open space around its vents, and one shut in a closed cabinet with its exhaust against a panel draws its own hot air back in until it shuts itself down to prevent damage. Dust in the heat sink causes the same symptom in an older machine rather than a new one, static from carpet damages parts when they are handled, and voltage sags would also trouble other equipment on the same circuit.

question: After malware was removed from a Windows 11 PC, every browser on it fails to load any website, yet ping reaches those same sites by name at their correct IP addresses. Other PCs on the network browse normally. What should the technician check?
explanation: Malware often points the system proxy at an address it controls so that it can intercept web traffic, and once the malware is gone that leftover proxy setting leaves every browser unable to load pages. Ping reaching the same sites by name at their correct addresses shows that name resolution, the hosts file and the default gateway are all working, and ping never passes through a proxy.

question: A warehouse worker wears thick gloves all shift. The company wants a phone screen lock that confirms who the user is, works with the gloves on, and cannot be learned by someone watching. Which lock type fits?
explanation: Facial recognition confirms the user by the face, so it works while the hands are covered and gives an onlooker nothing to copy. A fingerprint lock needs a bare finger on the sensor, and a PIN code or a pattern is a secret that someone can watch being entered and that is hard to enter in thick gloves.

question: A technician boots a new UEFI computer with Secure Boot turned on from a USB drive that holds an older Linux rescue tool. The firmware refuses to load it and reports a Secure Boot violation. What is the cause?
options: The boot partition is formatted with FAT32
The boot loader lacks a trusted signature
The drive uses the GPT partition style
The computer's TPM has not been initialized
explanation: Secure Boot lets the firmware start only boot loaders that are signed with a key it trusts, so an older tool without such a signature is blocked. FAT32 is the format UEFI firmware expects on boot media, GPT is the partition style UEFI is designed for, and the TPM stores keys and measurements but does not decide which boot loaders may run.

question: An employee's company-managed iPad has no App Store icon, and the employee cannot install any apps. Storage and the iPadOS version are fine. What should the technician check?
options: The MDM restriction that prevents the installation of new apps
The App Store option that updates apps automatically
The Low Power Mode setting that pauses background downloads
The MDM setting that defers new iPadOS updates
explanation: An MDM restriction that turns off app installation, or the same setting in Screen Time's Content and Privacy Restrictions, removes the App Store icon and blocks new apps until the restriction is lifted. Deferring iPadOS updates and updating apps automatically change when updates arrive, and Low Power Mode only pauses background downloads, so none of them hides the store.

question: In a cold, dry winter, technicians in a server room keep feeling static shocks when they touch the racks, and two network cards have failed. Which environmental change addresses the cause?
options: Putting surge suppressors on the racks
Raising the relative humidity of the air
Adding blanking panels to the racks
Lowering the cooling units' set point
explanation: Dry air lets static charge build up on people and equipment, so raising the relative humidity is the environmental fix for repeated static shocks and the failed cards that come with them. Blanking panels improve airflow through the racks, a lower cooling set point deals with overheating, and surge suppressors stop voltage spikes on the power lines, but none of them reduces static in dry air.

question: In a coffee shop, a person at the next table points a phone camera at an employee's laptop keyboard and records her typing her password. What is this attack called?
explanation: Shoulder surfing is watching someone enter a password, PIN or other private information, either directly or from a distance with a camera, which is why privacy screens and shielding the keyboard help. Impersonation is posing as a trusted person, tailgating is following someone through a secured door, and dumpster diving is searching discarded material.

question: A Linux workstation's /home partition is nearly full. Which command lists only the files under /home, in any subfolder, that are larger than 1 GB?
explanation: The find command searches a directory tree for files that pass a test, so find /home -size +1G lists every file under /home larger than 1 GB, however deep it sits. A recursive ls sorted by size still lists every file in each folder, du -h -d 1 totals each user's folder without naming the files in it, and df -h reports how full the whole file system is.

question: A technician is hardening a Windows workstation so that a program on a USB drive or disc cannot start by itself when the media is inserted. Which feature should the technician disable?
explanation: Disabling AutoRun stops Windows from starting a program named on removable media as soon as the media is inserted, which closes a common route for malware. Turning off Remote Desktop blocks remote sign-ins, disabling SMBv1 removes the old file-sharing protocol that the WannaCry worm exploited, and removing Telnet ends clear-text remote sessions, but none of these stops inserted media from launching a program.

question: A file server's motherboard failed. When the technician tries to restore its shares onto a replacement server, the backup files turn out to be unreadable. Which practice would have revealed this problem earlier?
options: Running scheduled test restores of the backups
Storing a second copy of the backups offsite
Switching from incremental to differential backups
explanation: Regular test restores prove that backups can actually be read and restored, so a failed or corrupt backup job is found before the data is needed. Differential backups shorten a restore but do not check it, an offsite copy protects against losing the site, and a grandfather-father-son rotation keeps older restore points without testing any of them.

question: An attacker breaks into a fully patched, vendor-supported server through a flaw that the vendor did not know about and has no fix for. What made this attack possible?
explanation: A zero-day vulnerability is a flaw that the vendor does not yet know about or has not yet fixed, so even a fully patched system is exposed until a patch is released. A missing patch leaves open a flaw that already has a fix, an end-of-life OS no longer receives fixes even for known flaws, and a non-compliant setting falls short of the organization's security baseline.

question: During the year-end change freeze, a vendor releases an unscheduled patch for a flaw that attackers are already exploiting in the company's web servers. How should the IT team handle the patch?
options: Apply it as a pre-approved standard change
Hold it until the change freeze ends
Submit it to the board as a normal change
explanation: An emergency change is approved quickly by a small group of authorized people and documented and reviewed afterward, so that an urgent fix such as a patch for an exploited flaw can go in even during a change freeze. Holding the patch until the freeze ends or waiting for the next board meeting leaves the flaw open to attack, and a standard change covers routine, low-risk work that was approved in advance.

question: A technician must encrypt a laptop's system drive with BitLocker and require a PIN at startup. The laptop runs Windows 11 Home. What must the technician do first?
options: Turn on Secure Boot in the firmware
Turn on Device encryption in Settings
Upgrade it to the Pro edition
Encrypt the user folders with EFS
explanation: BitLocker, with its startup PIN and recovery options, is included in Windows 11 Pro and higher editions but not in Home, so the laptop must be upgraded first. Device encryption on Home encrypts the drive without BitLocker management or a startup PIN, EFS encrypts individual files and is also missing from Home, and Secure Boot protects the startup process rather than encrypting anything.

question: A user's phone is set to join any open Wi-Fi network it finds, without asking the user first. Which risk does this setting create?
options: Malware installed from an unofficial app store
Traffic interception by an on-path attacker
Tracking of its location by apps in the background
explanation: A phone that joins open Wi-Fi networks on its own can end up on a network that an attacker runs or watches, where an on-path attacker can read or alter its unencrypted traffic. Unsolicited Bluetooth messages depend on Bluetooth being discoverable, malware from an unofficial store depends on sideloading, and background location tracking depends on app permissions, so none of them comes from this Wi-Fi setting.

question: A user wants to back up the personal certificate and private key that EFS uses to encrypt the user's files. Which console opens the current user's certificate store so that the certificate can be exported?
explanation: Certificate Manager (certmgr.msc) opens the current user's certificate store, where the personal EFS certificate can be exported with its private key. The certlm.msc console opens the local computer's store instead, Local Users and Groups (lusrmgr.msc) manages accounts, and Local Security Policy (secpol.msc) sets the EFS recovery agent rather than holding a user's own certificate.

question: A manager wants to reach her office desktop from her home laptop over the company VPN with Remote Desktop Connection. The desktop runs Windows 11 Home and the laptop runs Windows 11 Pro. What must change?
options: Open port 3389 on the home router
Upgrade the office desktop to the Pro edition
Install the RDP client on the laptop
Join the office desktop to a domain
explanation: Windows 11 Home can start Remote Desktop connections as a client but cannot accept them, so the office desktop must run Pro or a higher edition before it can be reached. The Remote Desktop Connection client is built into every edition, hosting Remote Desktop needs no domain, and the home router needs no open port for an outgoing connection over a VPN.

question: A shop has eight Windows 11 Pro PCs that need to share files and two printers. It has no server and no plans to buy one. Which network model fits?
explanation: A workgroup is a peer-to-peer arrangement in which each PC keeps its own accounts and shares its own folders and printers, so it needs no server. An Active Directory domain and any client-server network depend on a dedicated server, and HomeGroup was removed from Windows 10 in 2018, so it does not exist on Windows 11.

question: While securing a SOHO router, a technician finds that it accepts Telnet and FTP logins, although the owner manages it only through its HTTPS web page. Which hardening step deals with this finding?
explanation: Disabling services that nobody uses removes ways into the router, and Telnet and FTP are especially risky because they send passwords in clear text. Changing default passwords protects the login itself, updating the firmware fixes known flaws in the code, and content filtering controls which websites users can reach, so none of them closes the two services.

question: A tablet has become slow to respond over several months. Its storage page shows 500 MB free out of 32 GB. What should the technician recommend?
explanation: A mobile OS needs free storage for temporary files, caches and updates, so a tablet with almost no space left runs slowly until apps the user does not need are removed. Battery saver mode extends battery life by limiting performance, a network settings reset is for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth faults, and an OS update needs several gigabytes of free space before it can install.

question: A project team wants quick back-and-forth conversations, with searchable history organized by topic and @mentions to get someone's attention, instead of long email threads. Which cloud collaboration tool fits BEST?
options: A chat platform with persistent team channels
A shared spreadsheet of open questions
A shared mailbox for the project team
explanation: Chat platforms with persistent channels, such as Microsoft Teams and Slack, give quick conversations, @mentions, presence status and a searchable history grouped by channel. A shared mailbox is still email with long threads, a spreadsheet tracks items rather than conversations, and a daily videoconference leaves no searchable written record.

question: A thief removes the storage chip from a company phone and reads it with forensic equipment, bypassing the phone's own software. Which feature keeps the stored data unreadable in this case?
explanation: Device encryption keeps stored data unreadable without the key, so storage that is removed and read on other equipment shows only scrambled data. A passcode complexity rule and a fingerprint lock are enforced by the phone's own software, which the thief bypassed, and a remote backup application copies the data elsewhere without protecting the copy left on the phone.

question: A technician opens mmc.exe to build one custom console that holds Device Manager, Event Viewer and Disk Management, and plans to save it as an .msc file. How are these tools put into the blank console?
options: Add the tools to the Favorites menu
Choose Add/Remove Snap-in from the File menu
Install the tools from Optional features
Drag each tool's .msc file into the window
