explanation: Tools are added to a custom MMC console as snap-ins through Add/Remove Snap-in on the File menu, and the finished console is saved as an .msc file. An .msc file opens as its own console rather than merging into another, Optional features installs extra tools such as RSAT before they can be added, and Favorites only bookmarks items already in the console.

question: A company wants an alarm raised whenever anyone moves inside an empty records room at night, but its privacy policy forbids recording images of staff. Which control fits these needs?
explanation: A motion sensor detects movement in a space and can trigger an alarm the moment someone moves, without capturing any image. Video surveillance records images, which the policy forbids, guard patrols see the room only when a guard passes by, and badge reader logs record the badges used at the door rather than movement inside the room.

question: On a WPA3-Personal network, which feature keeps an attacker who records a device joining from testing passphrase guesses offline?
explanation: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) replaces the pre-shared key authentication of WPA2 with an exchange that gives a listener nothing to test guesses against, so each guess needs a live attempt with the access point. TKIP is the deprecated protocol from the original WPA, 802.1X is the per-user sign-in of the Enterprise modes, and AES-256 is a stronger cipher for the data, which does nothing about how the passphrase is checked.

question: Which control BEST protects a company from business email compromise requests to change a vendor's payment details?
options: Train the finance team to hover over each link before clicking
Scan each vendor attachment in a sandbox before it is delivered
Call the vendor back at a phone number already on file to confirm
Tag mail from outside the company with an external sender banner
explanation: Business email compromise works when people trust the email itself, so the defense is to verify a payment change through a separate, known channel, such as a phone number already on file. Sandboxing catches malicious attachments and hovering exposes disguised links, but a payment-change request usually carries neither, and an external sender banner flags outside mail, which every genuine vendor message already is.

question: A workstation is backed up in full on Sunday night and incrementally on each night from Monday to Saturday. What does Wednesday night's backup copy?
options: Sunday's full merged with each later backup
Each selected file, whether or not it changed
Files changed since Tuesday night's backup
Files changed since Sunday night's full backup
explanation: An incremental backup copies only what has changed since the previous backup of any type and then clears the archive bit, so Wednesday night's run picks up the changes made since Tuesday night's backup. Copying every change since Sunday's full is what a differential does, copying each selected file is a full backup, and merging the full with later backups describes a synthetic full.

question: A technician copies Windows 11 setup files to a USB drive formatted with NTFS. A new computer whose firmware supports only UEFI boot does not list the drive as a boot device. What should the technician do?
options: Switch the firmware setup to legacy CSM boot mode
Mark the drive's NTFS partition active in diskpart
Turn on TPM 2.0 in the firmware setup screen
Re-create the drive with a FAT32 boot partition
explanation: The UEFI standard requires firmware to read FAT file systems but not NTFS, so Windows boot media for a UEFI-only computer needs a FAT32 partition that holds its boot files. The Media Creation Tool builds the drive this way, and a setup image larger than the 4 GB file limit of FAT32 is split or kept on a second partition. An active partition matters only to legacy BIOS boot, CSM is not offered on this computer, and TPM 2.0 is needed to install Windows 11, not to start from the drive.

question: A dental office's front-desk PCs still run Windows 10, which reached end of support in October 2025, and the office has no extended support contract. What should a technician recommend?
options: Roll back the last feature update
Run a repair install of Windows 10
explanation: An OS that has reached end of life receives no further security patches, so the lasting fix is to move to a release that the vendor still supports, here Windows 11. Automatic updates help only while updates are still being published, a repair install fixes damaged system files rather than missing patches, and rolling back a feature update undoes a change that caused a problem.

question: A manager worries that her six-digit Windows Hello PIN is weaker than the long password on her Microsoft account. What makes the PIN hard for an attacker to misuse?
options: It is checked by Microsoft servers at sign-in
It changes to a new value at short intervals
It is tied to the one device where it was set up
It unlocks the encrypted drive at startup
explanation: A Windows Hello PIN unlocks a key kept on the one device where it was set up, usually protected by its TPM, so a stolen PIN is useless on any other computer and is not sent over the network. A code that changes at short intervals comes from an authenticator app, an online account password is what Microsoft's servers check, and a PIN entered at startup to unlock a drive belongs to BitLocker.

question: A Mac reports errors whenever it opens files on an external drive. Which built-in tool should the technician use to check the drive's file system and repair it?
explanation: Disk Utility checks and repairs a disk's file system with its First Aid feature, and it also erases, formats and partitions drives. System Information reports hardware details such as a drive's model and capacity, Activity Monitor shows how much each process reads from and writes to disk, and Startup Disk chooses the volume that the Mac starts from.

question: On a workstation that is not joined to a domain, a technician must make every local account use a password of at least 12 characters. Where is this set?
explanation: Local Security Policy (secpol.msc) holds the password policy, including Minimum password length, for every local account on a computer that is not in a domain. Local Users and Groups sets or resets one account's password, Sign-in options in Settings adds a PIN or biometric sign-in, and User Accounts in Control Panel changes an account's name, type or password.

question: Settings on a PC show System type: 32-bit operating system, x64-based processor. A required application comes only as a 64-bit version and will not install. What will let it run?
options: Replacing the CPU with a 64-bit model
explanation: A 64-bit application needs a 64-bit operating system, and an x64-based processor can run one, so a clean install of 64-bit Windows lets the application run (there is no in-place upgrade from 32-bit). The processor is already 64-bit capable, virtualization support matters for virtual machines, and administrator rights cannot make 64-bit code run on a 32-bit system.

question: In a Linux home folder, ls does not show the file .bashrc, although the file exists. Which command lists it?
explanation: Files whose names begin with a dot are hidden, and ls -a lists them along with every other entry. The -l option adds details such as permissions and sizes, -R lists subfolders recursively and -t sorts by modification time, but all three still leave hidden files out.

question: An Android phone is texting everyone in its contact list without the owner's action. Each text links to a website that offers a parcel-tracking app as an APK file. How was the phone most likely infected?
options: The owner charged it at a public USB port
The owner sideloaded an app from outside Google Play
The owner accepted a Bluetooth pairing request
The owner joined an open Wi-Fi network in public
explanation: Android malware that texts a download link to every contact spreads by getting each victim to install its APK from outside Google Play, so the owner most likely sideloaded the same app from an earlier text of this kind. The text is only the lure. An open Wi-Fi network exposes traffic to interception, a stranger's pairing request can expose the phone over Bluetooth, and a public USB port can reach data through the cable, but none of these installs an app that texts every contact.

question: A company wants software on each laptop that records process, file and network activity, flags behavior such as a document starting PowerShell, and lets its own analysts cut a laptop off the network from a console. What should it install?
explanation: Endpoint detection and response puts an agent on each device that records activity, detects suspicious behavior and lets responders isolate the device remotely. A managed detection and response service is an outside team rather than software the company runs, a network intrusion prevention system inspects traffic on the network instead of on laptops, and signature-based antivirus matches known files without recording behavior.

question: A technician needs to add a built-in VPN connection and enter a manual proxy server address on a Windows 11 laptop. Which Settings category holds both?
explanation: Network & internet holds the VPN page, where built-in VPN connections are added, and the Proxy page, where a manual proxy server is set. Privacy & security covers Windows Security, encryption and app permissions, Accounts connects work or school accounts and manages sign-in, and Apps manages installed apps, including third-party VPN clients.

question: A company turns on an AI assistant integrated with its email, documents and chat. Soon after, an employee asks it about salaries and gets details from an HR spreadsheet the employee could technically open but was never meant to see. What does this reveal?
options: The assistant is hallucinating, so the salary details it gave are invented
The assistant works within each user's access, so overshared files are easy to find
The assistant ignores file permissions, so it reads any file in the company
The assistant was trained on the HR data, so it repeats what it learned before
explanation: AI assistants built into productivity apps can surface anything the user already has access to, so oversharing that went unnoticed becomes easy to find. Review and tighten permissions and data labels before turning on the integration. The assistant found the file through the employee's own access rather than from earlier training, the salary data is real rather than invented, and the assistant respects existing permissions rather than ignoring them.

question: The IT department agrees with the sales department that failed laptops will be repaired or replaced by the next business day. Which type of agreement is this?
explanation: An internal service-level agreement (SLA) sets service expectations between departments of the same organization, such as IT and sales. An external SLA is made with an outside provider or customer, and mutual and one-way non-disclosure agreements protect confidential information rather than setting service levels.

question: From a Linux workstation, a technician wants to check whether an internal web server responds, seeing only its HTTP response headers without downloading the page. Which command does this?
explanation: With -I, curl sends a HEAD request, so the web server returns only its response headers, such as the status code 200 or 404, and no page body. Given a bare host name, curl assumes HTTP. A ping tests reachability with ICMP, traceroute shows the routers along the path and dig queries DNS records; none of the three speaks HTTP to the server.

question: An attacker records a small office's WPA3-Personal traffic and, months later, learns the passphrase. The recordings still cannot be decrypted. Which property of the WPA3-Personal handshake explains this?
explanation: Forward secrecy means each session key comes from a fresh exchange that the passphrase alone cannot reproduce, so learning the passphrase later does not unlock traffic recorded earlier. Mutual authentication proves to each side that the other knows the passphrase, key stretching slows down the guessing of a password, and data integrity detects packets that were changed in transit, and none of these protects old recordings.

question: Malware on a company workstation keeps returning after removal attempts in Safe Mode and from a preinstallation environment. The user's files are kept on a network share, and IT maintains a tested build for this model. What should the technician do?
options: Repair Windows files with System File Checker
Reimage the workstation from the standard image
Rebuild the user's profile on the workstation
Run Startup Repair from the recovery menu
explanation: When malware survives repeated removal attempts, reimaging from a known-good image is the reliable fix, because no scan can prove that every trace is gone. Startup Repair fixes problems that stop Windows from starting, System File Checker repairs protected Windows files, and rebuilding the user's profile leaves the infected system in place.

question: On an Ubuntu server, apt install reports that it is unable to locate a package, although the configured repositories hold it. Which command should be run first?
explanation: Running apt update downloads the current package lists from the configured repositories, and until those lists are current, apt cannot find packages that the repositories hold. The apt upgrade and apt full-upgrade commands install newer versions of packages already installed (full-upgrade may also remove some), and apt autoremove removes packages that are no longer needed.

question: In a company's monthly test, about a third of staff click the link in a fake email and type their password on the page it opens. The company wants staff to recognize such messages and report them instead of clicking. What should it provide?
explanation: Anti-phishing training teaches staff to spot the signs of a phishing message and to report it, so it works on the people who receive the message rather than on the message itself. An email security gateway filters messages before delivery, endpoint detection and response watches activity on devices, and managed detection and response is an outside team that handles security alerts.

question: A company blocks malicious and banned sites with its internal DNS servers. Users who turned on secure DNS with a public provider in their browsers are no longer filtered. What should the administrator do?
options: Ask users to clear the browser cache at the end of each working day
Use browser policies to turn secure DNS off or point it at the company's resolver
Turn off private-browsing mode in each browser through Group Policy
Block outbound port 53 at the firewall so that secure DNS lookups cannot leave the network
explanation: DNS over HTTPS sends lookups over HTTPS, on port 443, to whichever resolver the browser is set to, bypassing internal DNS filtering; managed browser policies for Chrome and Edge can turn secure DNS off or require the company's resolver. Blocking port 53 does not affect DNS over HTTPS, clearing the cache does not change where lookups go, and private browsing does not control DNS.

question: SSDs that held patient records are being retired and will not be reused. Which method gives the highest assurance that no data can be recovered from them, even in a forensic lab?
explanation: Shredding an SSD into small pieces destroys its flash memory chips, which gives the highest assurance that no data can be recovered from drives that will not be reused. Degaussing has no effect on flash memory, low-level formatting can miss cells that the drive's wear leveling has set aside, and standard formatting only rebuilds the file system and is not a sanitization method.

question: An iPhone app shows a connection error whenever the phone is on the corporate Wi-Fi network, although other apps work there. The same app works on cellular data and on home Wi-Fi. What is the most likely cause?
options: The app lacks permission to use cellular data
The office firewall blocks the app's servers
The phone's clock is set to the wrong time
The app's cached data has become corrupted
explanation: An app that fails on one network but works on others points to that network filtering its traffic, such as a firewall or content filter that blocks the servers the app depends on. Missing permission for cellular data would make the app fail on cellular data instead, while corrupted cached data or a wrong clock, which breaks certificate checks, would cause errors on every network.

question: On a user's iPhone, a green dot keeps appearing at the top of the screen while the phone sits idle with no app open. Which privacy setting should the technician check?
options: Apps allowed to use location services
Apps allowed to use the camera
Apps allowed to read the photo library
Apps allowed to use the microphone
explanation: On an iPhone, a green dot at the top of the screen means that an app is using the camera, so a dot that appears with no app open points to an app using the camera in the background. An orange dot would mean the microphone is in use, location use shows an arrow icon rather than a dot, and the photo library has no indicator of its own.

question: An accounting firm wants Credential Guard to protect the sign-in secrets on its Windows 11 PCs, even from malware that has administrator rights. Which edition should it deploy?
explanation: Credential Guard, which uses virtualization-based security to isolate sign-in secrets, is included only in the Enterprise and Education editions of Windows 11. Pro and Pro for Workstations do not include it, although Pro for Workstations adds support for high-end hardware, and Home also lacks business features such as domain join and BitLocker.

question: A domain workstation's clock has drifted more than five minutes ahead of the domain controller's, and its users now get sign-in errors, while other workstations keep the controller's time. What should the technician check first?
explanation: Domain computers keep their clocks matched to a domain controller through the Windows Time service, so a clock that drifts minutes away from the controller's time points to that service being stopped or failing to sync. Domain sign-in fails once the difference passes five minutes. A weak CMOS battery makes the clock lose time while the PC is unplugged, a wrong time zone shifts the clock by a fixed offset rather than a drift, and the daylight saving setting moves it by an hour when the season changes.

question: An organization installs its standard applications as part of its Windows image. A critical security update for one of those applications is released. Which drawback of this distribution method does the update expose?
options: Each PC that receives the image needs a license for the app
The image grows larger with each application built into it
Each hardware model needs its own drivers added to the image
New PCs get the old version until the image is rebuilt and retested
explanation: Applications built into an image stay at the version that was captured, so after an update the image must be rebuilt and retested, or every new PC starts with the vulnerable version until it is patched. Per-device licensing, a growing image and drivers for each hardware model are real costs of imaging as well, but none of them is caused by the new update.

question: A company's contract with an outside IT support firm says critical incidents get a response within 1 hour and a resolution within 4 hours, with credits on the bill if these targets are missed. What is this document?
explanation: A service-level agreement (SLA) sets measurable service commitments, such as response and resolution times for each priority, and the remedies when they are missed. One made with an outside provider is an external SLA. An acceptable use policy governs how users may use systems, a non-disclosure agreement protects confidential information, and a standard operating procedure gives step-by-step instructions for a task.

question: A managed phone with cloud backup turned off uploads several gigabytes every night to an IP address that no company service uses. Which cause is most consistent with this traffic?
options: An app texting premium numbers for an attacker
An app sending the user's files to an attacker
An app showing an attacker's ads over other apps
An app mining cryptocurrency for an attacker
explanation: Heavy uploads every night to an address that no company service uses are the mark of data exfiltration, an app sending stolen files to an attacker. A cryptominer loads the processor and drains the battery while exchanging little data, adware downloads its ads rather than uploading files, and texts to premium-rate numbers run up charges on the phone bill without sending data over the internet.

question: A phone has downloaded an OS update, but the installation will not start. The phone has 30 GB of free storage, is on Wi-Fi, and shows 10 percent battery. What should the technician do first?
options: Free up more storage on the phone
Connect the phone to a charger
Delete and download the update again
explanation: Mobile operating systems will not begin installing an update on a low battery, since a power loss part way through could leave the phone unable to start, so connecting a charger comes first. Deleting and downloading the update again is for a damaged download, freeing storage is for a phone without room for the update, and a network settings reset is for connection faults.

question: An attacker has a stolen, salted password hash and runs a tool that tries aaaa, aaab, aaac and onward through every combination of characters until one produces a matching hash. Which attack is this?
explanation: A brute-force attack tries every possible combination of characters in turn, so it will eventually find the password, but a long password makes the search take impractically long. A rainbow table attack looks hashes up in a precomputed table, which a salt defeats, a pass-the-hash attack uses the hash to sign in without cracking it, and a password spraying attack tries one common password against many accounts.

question: After several cd commands, a technician is unsure which folder the shell is now in. Which command prints the full path of that folder?
explanation: The pwd command (print working directory) shows the full path of the folder the shell is working in. The whoami command prints the signed-in user's name, hostname prints the computer's name, and ls lists what the current folder contains without naming the folder itself.

question: A free video player downloaded from a file-sharing site plays videos normally, but it also lets a remote attacker take control of the computer. Which type of malware is this?
explanation: A Trojan hides a malicious payload, such as a remote access backdoor, inside a program that looks useful and often works as expected. Adware is commonly bundled with free programs, but it displays unwanted advertising rather than handing over control. A virus spreads by inserting itself into other files and a worm copies itself across a network; neither depends on posing as a useful application.

question: During a storm, the office lights dim for a few seconds and several workstations restart. Which kind of power problem is this?
explanation: An under-voltage event, such as a sag or brownout, is a drop in voltage that can dim lights and make computers restart without the power going out completely. A surge is a brief rise in voltage rather than a drop, a power failure is a complete loss of power that would put the lights out, and line noise is interference riding on the circuit rather than a fall in voltage.

question: A user brings in a new Windows 11 Home laptop that must join the company's Active Directory domain. In System Properties, the option to join a domain is grayed out. What is the cause?
options: The user is signed in without admin rights
The laptop cannot reach a domain controller
The installed edition does not support domain join
The laptop clock differs from the domain clock
explanation: Windows 11 Home cannot join an Active Directory domain, so its domain setting stays grayed out until the computer is upgraded to Pro or a higher edition. Missing administrator rights lead to a request for administrator credentials rather than a grayed-out option, an unreachable domain controller causes an error only after the domain name is entered, and a clock difference breaks Kerberos sign-ins after the join.

question: A technician signed in as root needs a shell running as the user kim, with that account's own environment, to test which files the account can read. Which command starts one?
explanation: The su command switches to another account, and su -l kim starts a login shell as kim with that account's own environment, without asking root for a password. Running sudo kim would start a program named kim as root, id -G kim lists the IDs of the groups the account belongs to, and last kim shows when the account last signed in.

question: A change that will take the main file server offline for 30 minutes has been approved. When should the work be carried out?
options: After the next change board meeting
explanation: A maintenance window is a period agreed in advance, usually at a time of low use, when approved changes are carried out and users have been told to expect disruption. A change freeze is a period when changes are suspended, the backup window is kept for backup jobs, and the change board meeting is where changes are approved rather than carried out.

question: A Windows PC restarts without warning several times a day, always while it is busy, and never shows a stop error. The firmware's hardware monitor shows the CPU temperature at its rated maximum under load. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: When a processor reaches its rated maximum temperature, the hardware cuts power or resets the computer at once to protect the chip, so no stop error is ever shown. A failing power supply can also cause sudden restarts but would not raise the processor temperature, while a faulty memory module or a corrupted system file usually ends in a blue screen with a stop code.

question: Several employees share one company Mac. The administrator wants to stop them from changing system-wide settings and installing software that needs administrator approval. In System Settings, where are their accounts changed from administrator to standard?
explanation: Users & Groups is where macOS adds accounts and sets each one as an administrator or a standard user, and a standard user cannot change system-wide settings or approve installs that need an administrator. Screen Time limits app use and content, Internet Accounts adds mail, contacts and calendar accounts, and Lock Screen sets when a password is required and what the login window shows.

question: A user accidentally emailed a spreadsheet of employee salaries to the entire company. Which control could have recognized the salary data and stopped the message before it was delivered?
explanation: Data loss prevention inspects outgoing messages and files for sensitive content such as salary or identity data and can block or quarantine them before they leave. Antivirus scanning looks for malware rather than sensitive data, email encryption protects a message in transit but still delivers it to every recipient, and spam filtering screens unwanted incoming mail.

question: A tablet with no visible damage registers taps and swipes that nobody made, opening apps on its own, whether or not it is charging. What should the technician try first?
options: Wipe the screen with a dry cloth
explanation: Moisture, grease or grit on a capacitive touchscreen can register as touches, so cleaning and drying the glass, then removing any screen protector, comes before anything else. Increased touch sensitivity is for a screen that misses touches through a thick protector or gloves and would make phantom touches worse, recalibrating the accelerometer is for wrong screen rotation, and replacing the digitizer is the last step once surface causes are ruled out.

question: A technician will use compressed air to clear years of dust from inside an office desktop. Which equipment protects the technician's own health during this job?
options: An ESD wrist strap and a grounded mat
Goggles and an air filtration mask
Insulated rubber gloves and safety boots
Hearing protection and a hard hat
explanation: Compressed air throws fine dust and debris into the air, so safety goggles protect the eyes and an air filtration mask keeps the dust out of the lungs. An ESD strap and grounded mat protect the computer's parts rather than the person, insulated gloves and safety boots are for work near live circuits, and hearing protection and a hard hat suit noisy equipment rooms and overhead work.

question: A technician enters sfc /scannow at an elevated command prompt. What does the tool do?
options: Rebuilds the boot configuration data store
Replaces damaged system files with cached copies
Repairs the component store from Windows Update
Repairs errors in the file system of a volume
explanation: System File Checker compares each protected Windows system file with a known good copy kept in the component store and replaces any file that is damaged or missing. The chkdsk command repairs file system errors on a volume, DISM with /RestoreHealth repairs the component store itself, and bootrec /rebuildbcd rebuilds the list of installations that Windows Boot Manager reads.

question: A laptop gets an address but cannot reach the internet. The technician wants to see which DHCP server issued its lease, when the lease expires and which DNS servers the adapter uses. Which command shows these details?
explanation: The ipconfig /all command adds the DHCP server, lease times, DNS servers and MAC address to the basic address details. Plain ipconfig shows the addresses, subnet mask and default gateway but not the lease or DNS servers, ipconfig /renew requests a new lease instead of reporting the current one, and ipconfig /displaydns lists cached name lookups.

question: A laptop was taken from an employee's desk in a shared office while the employee was at lunch. Which end-user best practice addresses this risk?
options: Lock the screen when leaving the desk
Fasten the computer down with a cable lock
Log off at the end of each workday
Keep passwords in a password manager
explanation: Securing critical hardware, for example by fastening a laptop to the desk with a cable lock or locking it away, stops it from being carried off while its user is elsewhere. Locking the screen protects an unattended session but not the laptop itself, a password manager keeps passwords unique and out of sight, and logging off at the end of the day protects the account overnight, so none of them prevents theft.

question: A browser vendor releases an update that fixes a flaw already being exploited by malicious websites. The update has downloaded on every office computer, but users leave their browsers open for days. What must users do for the fix to take effect?
explanation: Browsers download updates in the background but finish installing them only when the browser is closed and opened again, so an open copy keeps running the vulnerable code until it restarts. Clearing the cache removes stored page files, safe browsing warns about known malicious sites without fixing the flaw, and a private window runs the same unpatched code.

question: Overnight, the same malware appeared on most of the unpatched computers on a network, although no one had opened a file or started a program on them. Which type of malware spreads this way?
explanation: A worm copies itself from computer to computer across a network by exploiting vulnerabilities, with no host file and no action by a user. A virus spreads only when a user runs the infected file it is attached to, a Trojan must be installed by a user it has fooled, and a rootkit hides malware rather than spreading it.

question: A café owner wants to offer customers Wi-Fi without giving them any access to the point-of-sale system and office PC on the same router. Which configuration BEST does this?
options: A guest network with client isolation turned on
MAC address filtering set up for the café's own devices
WPA3 on the main network, with a password given to customers
A captive portal on the main network for customer sign-in
explanation: A guest network puts visitors on a separate SSID and network segment that reaches the internet but not internal devices, and client isolation stops guests from reaching each other. A captive portal on the main network collects sign-ins but leaves customers beside the point-of-sale system, MAC filtering for the café's devices keeps customers off the network rather than giving them Wi-Fi, and WPA3 encrypts the main network while its shared password still lets customers onto it.

question: An old logon script that Windows Script Host runs on each computer is written in a language that Microsoft has deprecated and plans to remove from Windows. Which script type is it?
explanation: VBScript files (.vbs) run under Windows Script Host and were long used for logon scripts, but Microsoft deprecated VBScript in 2023 and is phasing it out of Windows. Batch files run in the Command Prompt, PowerShell scripts are the modern replacement for most VBScript tasks, and Python scripts need a separately installed interpreter.

question: When a user opens an online store, the browser warns that the site's certificate expired last week. What does this warning tell the user?
options: The browser is missing a security update
The site's identity cannot be confirmed
The page is being sent without encryption
The site is listed as a source of malware
explanation: An expired certificate means the browser can no longer confirm that the server is the site it claims to be, so the user could be dealing with an impostor and should not enter personal details. The connection itself would still be encrypted, a malware listing produces a separate safe browsing warning, and an out-of-date browser does not make a valid certificate expire.

question: A laptop that holds client files in several folders is often taken off site. IT wants every file on it, Windows included, to stay unreadable if its storage is removed and attached to another computer. What should be configured?
explanation: BitLocker on the system drive encrypts the whole volume, Windows included, so nothing on it can be read when the drive is moved to another computer without the key. EFS protects only the files a user chooses to encrypt, NTFS permissions can be bypassed by taking ownership on another computer, and a UEFI password stops the laptop from starting but leaves the drive itself readable.

question: Before selling a used computer, a technician runs a quick format on its hard disk drive. The buyer later recovers the previous owner's files with recovery software. Why was this possible?
options: System Restore kept the files in restore points
The files stayed in sectors marked as free
Wear leveling kept copies in spare flash cells
The Recycle Bin still held the deleted files
explanation: A quick format writes a new, empty file system but leaves the old data in sectors that are now marked as free, so recovery software can still read the files. Wear leveling explains leftover data on SSDs rather than hard disk drives, the Recycle Bin sits on the formatted volume and is cleared with it, and System Restore protects system files and settings, not personal files.

question: A Mac app has frozen and ignores Command+Q. Which key combination opens the window that lists the open apps so that the frozen one can be closed?
explanation: Option+Command+Esc opens the Force Quit window, which lists the open apps and closes the one that has stopped responding, and the same window is on the Apple menu. Option+Shift+Command+Q logs the user out without asking, Control+Command+Power button forces a restart without saving open work, and Control+Command+Space bar opens the Character Viewer for emoji and symbols.

question: Antivirus has removed ransomware from a user's PC, but the user's documents are still encrypted and no decryption tool exists for this strain. How should the technician recover the documents?
options: Repair them with the chkdsk command
Restore them from a backup of the files
Repair them with System File Checker
Roll the PC back to a restore point
explanation: When no decryption tool exists, files that ransomware has encrypted are recovered from a backup made before the infection, so restoring a clean backup is the dependable way to get them back. System Restore does not bring back personal documents, System File Checker repairs protected Windows files, and chkdsk fixes file system errors rather than undoing encryption.

question: An IT team needs one central console from which it can deploy software, push configuration settings and run scripts on 400 company workstations. Which type of third-party tool is built for this?
explanation: Desktop management software, such as Microsoft Configuration Manager or Intune, manages many computers from one console, deploying applications, applying settings and running scripts on all of them at once. Screen-sharing software connects one technician to one computer, video-conferencing software hosts meetings, and file transfer software moves files without managing the systems.

question: A traceroute from a Linux workstation shows only asterisks after the fifth hop, but tracert from a Windows PC on the same network completes. A firewall beyond hop five drops UDP probes but allows ICMP. Which command should the technician try on Linux?
explanation: By default, Linux traceroute sends UDP probes to high ports, starting at 33434, while Windows tracert sends ICMP echo requests, so traceroute -I, which switches to ICMP echo probes, gets past this firewall. Sending ICMP can need root rights, hence sudo. The -n option only skips looking up hop names, -q 5 sends five UDP probes per hop instead of three, and -w 10 waits longer for replies that the firewall has already dropped.

question: A cracking tool hashes each entry in a list of ten million commonly used passwords, such as sunshine and qwerty123, and compares every result with a stolen hash. Which attack is this?
explanation: A dictionary attack tries a prepared list of likely passwords, such as common words and leaked passwords, which is why it is far faster than trying every combination and why an uncommon passphrase defeats it. A brute-force attack tries every combination rather than a list, a rainbow table attack looks hashes up in a precomputed table instead of hashing each guess, and a password spraying attack tries a few common passwords against many accounts on a live sign-in page.

question: A company keeps its working data on a file server and one backup copy in a cloud storage service. What should it add to meet the 3-2-1 backup rule?
options: Another copy on an office NAS
A RAID 1 mirror of the server's disks
explanation: The 3-2-1 rule calls for three copies of the data on at least two kinds of storage with one copy off-site, so a file server plus one cloud backup is a copy short, and another copy on a local NAS completes the set. A RAID 1 mirror repeats every deletion or corruption and is not a backup, encryption protects the cloud copy without adding one, and backing up more often reduces data loss but still leaves two copies.

question: A company's internal AI assistant answers questions from the company's own policy documents rather than from the open internet. What is an advantage of controlling the data source this way?
options: Answers cover a wider range of topics, drawn from across the web
The model improves over time by learning from each employee's questions
Answers rest on approved company data, and access to it is governed
It works offline on any laptop, because it needs no web access
explanation: The data source an AI draws on shapes its answers, so grounding a private assistant in approved internal documents keeps answers relevant and lets the company control and audit what data it uses. Drawing on the open web is the breadth this design gives up, an assistant that runs on company servers still needs a network connection to answer, and an assistant that reads a set of documents does not learn from employees' questions.

question: A technician must sanitize a used server's SATA solid-state drive for reuse, including the spare cells that the operating system cannot address. Which method should the technician use?
explanation: ATA Secure Erase is a command built into the drive that has the SSD's own controller erase its cells, including spare areas that software cannot reach, and it leaves the drive ready for reuse. A multipass overwrite was designed for magnetic disks and writes only to addresses the operating system can see, standard formatting does not sanitize a drive, and degaussing has no effect on flash memory.

question: A high-priority ticket will breach its SLA resolution time in 30 minutes, and the assigned technician is still waiting on a part. What should happen, following good ticketing practice?
options: Move the ticket to the hardware category
Add the part's tracking number to the ticket
Reassign the ticket to another technician
Escalate the ticket to a supervisor
explanation: When an SLA deadline is at risk, the ticket is escalated under the escalation procedure so that someone with more authority can act, for example by rushing the part or arranging a loaner, and the user is kept informed. Reassigning it to a peer leaves the same wait for the part, changing its category only corrects how it is filed, and adding the tracking number is useful documentation but does nothing about the deadline.

question: A laptop runs Windows 11 Home. Its owner has bought a Windows 11 Pro license and wants to keep every installed app and file. How should the technician change the edition?
options: Run the Installation Assistant to upgrade in place
Enter a Pro product key on the Activation page
Reset the PC and keep personal files
Boot from Pro media and perform a clean install
explanation: Moving from Windows 11 Home to Pro is an in-place upgrade: entering a Pro product key on the Activation page of Settings unlocks the Pro features and keeps apps, files and settings. A clean install from Pro media would also give Pro but erases the apps, Reset this PC reinstalls Home and removes apps, and the Installation Assistant moves Windows 10 to Windows 11 without changing the edition.

question: A company policy requires the full BitLocker feature on every laptop's system drive. One laptop runs Windows 11 Home. What must the technician do before BitLocker can be set up on it?
options: Upgrade the computer to the Pro edition
Switch the computer out of S mode
Enable Secure Boot in the firmware
explanation: BitLocker Drive Encryption is part of Windows 11 Pro and higher editions but not Home, so a Home computer has to be upgraded to Pro before BitLocker can be used. Leaving S mode only lets a computer install apps from outside the Microsoft Store, Secure Boot protects the startup process without adding BitLocker, and BitLocker is an installable feature only on Windows Server.

question: A small office on a tight budget needs a nightly on-site backup of a workstation that holds 2 TB, and no one will be there overnight to change media. Which backup destination fits BEST?
explanation: An external USB hard drive is the usual on-site backup for a small office, since it is inexpensive, holds several terabytes and needs no one to change media overnight. LTO tape needs a costly tape drive and suits larger archives, 2 TB would fill a stack of Blu-ray discs that someone has to swap, and a cloud plan keeps its copy off site, which is its strength but not an on-site backup.

question: A company requires every technician to install its custom accounting package on finance workstations with the same approved steps and settings. Which document should set out those steps?
explanation: A standard operating procedure sets out the approved steps for a routine task, such as a custom software installation, so that every technician carries it out the same way. A knowledge base article records a known problem and its fix, a service-level agreement sets the response and resolution times that support has promised, and an onboarding checklist lists the setup tasks for a new user.

question: An MDM console shows that an employee has removed the management profile from an enrolled iPhone, and the phone has stopped checking in. What should the IT team do to protect company data?
options: Reset the employee's password and require a new sign-in
Block the phone from company data until it re-enrolls
Send a remote wipe to the phone from the MDM console
Lock the phone with an MDM command until the employee calls
explanation: Once its management profile is removed, a phone stops checking in with the MDM, so commands sent from the console no longer reach it, and the way to protect company data is to block the phone's access until it is enrolled again. A wipe or a lock sent through the MDM waits for a check-in that will not come, and a password reset only makes the employee sign in again on the same unmanaged phone.

question: A company's phones get OS updates promptly, but a security review finds many of their apps months out of date. Which step BEST closes this gap?
options: Block app installs from anywhere but the official app store
Push OS updates through MDM as soon as they become available
Remove apps that nobody has opened in the past 90 days
Enforce automatic app updates on the devices through MDM
explanation: Patch management on mobile devices covers apps as well as the OS: automatic updates from the App Store or Google Play, or app versions enforced through MDM, close known app vulnerabilities quickly. Pushing OS updates repeats what is already working, blocking installs from outside the store stops sideloading but updates nothing, and removing unused apps leaves the apps people use out of date.

question: A small company's web server stops answering customers because one outside computer is sending it thousands of requests every second. Which action should the technician take to restore service?
options: Enable account lockout on the server
Block the source address at the firewall
Restore the website from last night's backup
explanation: A denial of service attack from a single source can be stopped by blocking that one address at the firewall, which a distributed attack from thousands of addresses does not allow. Account lockout stops repeated password guessing, restoring from a backup undoes damage such as a defaced site, and a new TLS certificate fixes certificate errors; none of them stops a flood of requests.

question: After adding a line for /dev/sdb1 to /etc/fstab, an administrator wants to test the new line without rebooting. Which command attaches every file system listed in fstab that is not attached yet?
explanation: Running mount -a mounts every file system listed in /etc/fstab except those marked noauto or already mounted, so a mistake in the new line shows up now instead of at the next boot. The df -h command reports space on file systems that are already mounted, umount -a unmounts file systems, and fsck -N only shows what fsck would do without checking anything.

question: On one office PC, typing the bank's address opens a look-alike site, while other PCs reach the real site. Running nslookup on that PC returns the bank's correct IP address. What should the technician check?
explanation: Windows checks the hosts file before it asks a DNS server, so a hosts entry can send one PC to a fake site while nslookup, which queries the DNS server directly, still returns the correct address. A wrong DNS setting on the router would affect every PC and show up in nslookup, the browser's home page only sets the first page that opens, and firewall rules block traffic rather than redirect it.

question: A technician suspects that a Windows PC has a kernel-level rootkit that hides its files and processes from the running operating system. Which approach gives the BEST chance of detecting it?
options: Boot from a USB drive and scan the disk
Restart in Safe Mode and scan the disk
Run a full scan with the installed antivirus
explanation: A kernel-level rootkit controls what the running operating system reports, so the disk is scanned most reliably from a separate environment booted from external media, where the rootkit's code is not running. Safe Mode still starts the installed copy of Windows, so the rootkit can load there; a full scan with the installed antivirus depends on the same compromised system; and Task Manager shows only what the rootkit lets Windows report.

question: At a hotel, an attacker sets up an access point that broadcasts the same network name as the hotel's guest Wi-Fi, so that guests connect to it and their traffic passes through the attacker's equipment. Which attack is this?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue access point that copies a legitimate network's name so that users connect to it, which lets the attacker capture or alter their traffic. Wardriving is searching an area for wireless networks, bluesnarfing steals data from a device over Bluetooth, and jamming floods the radio channel with interference so that no one can connect.

question: After a user installs a free photo editor, a scan finds a hidden component that shows no advertisements but records every website the user visits and sends the list to a marketing company. Which type of malware is this component?
explanation: Spyware secretly collects information such as browsing history and sends it to a third party, and it often arrives bundled with free software. Adware exists to display advertising, a keylogger captures keystrokes rather than a list of visited sites, and stalkerware is installed deliberately by someone who wants to watch a particular person.

question: A technician will replace the power supply in a desktop that the user has just shut down. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Set the case on an ESD mat
Put on an ESD wrist strap
explanation: A computer that is shut down still receives standby power while it is plugged in, so the cord must come out of the wall before anything else is done to the case. The wrist strap and antistatic mat protect parts from static once the power is disconnected, and a photograph of the cable layout is taken after the case is open, before the old supply's connectors are removed.

question: A company is deciding whether to buy tablets for its delivery drivers or let them use their own under a BYOD policy. Which advantage does buying company-owned tablets give the company?
options: Less hardware inventory for IT to manage
Lower spending on new devices and repairs
Tighter control of settings and apps
Shorter learning curve on familiar devices
explanation: A company-owned device lets IT set every policy, app and setting and wipe it whenever needed, a degree of control that is hard to justify on a device an employee owns. Lower spending on devices and repairs, a shorter learning curve and less hardware for IT to track are all advantages of BYOD, since staff then work on phones and tablets they already own and know.

question: A user needs to add a printer that is shared as HPLaser from a Windows 11 workstation named WKSTN01. Which path does the user enter under Select a shared printer by name in the Add Printer wizard?
explanation: Windows connects to a printer shared from another Windows computer by its UNC path: two backslashes, the computer name, one backslash and the share name, as in \\WKSTN01\HPLaser. The smb:// form is how macOS and Linux address SMB shares, print$ is the hidden share from which clients download printer drivers, and a path that puts the share name before the computer name does not resolve.

question: A company uses a dedicated password manager and does not want passwords saved in web browsers. Which browser feature should be turned off, ideally through policy?
options: The pop-up blocker for unwanted windows
Secure DNS for encrypted name lookups
Tracking prevention, which blocks third-party trackers
The built-in offer to save and autofill credentials
explanation: Browser feature management lets administrators turn individual features on or off: disabling the built-in password saving stops credentials from being stored in browser profiles, which may sync to personal accounts, outside the company's approved tool. The pop-up blocker, secure DNS and tracking prevention protect users and should stay on.

question: A consultant will spend a week at a client site with no internet access and needs a project folder that is stored in OneDrive. Which option should be set on that folder before leaving?
explanation: Always keep on this device downloads the folder's files and keeps them on the laptop, marked with a solid green circle and white check mark, so they open offline and sync their changes once the laptop is back online. Free up space does the opposite, making the files online-only, which cannot be opened without an internet connection, and a sharing link or version history does not make files available offline.

question: A thief switches a stolen company phone to airplane mode and starts guessing its passcode. Which feature can still erase the phone's data after ten wrong guesses in a row?
explanation: A failed login attempts restriction erases or locks a phone after a set number of wrong passcode entries, and it works without a network connection because the phone itself counts the attempts. A remote wipe needs the phone to receive a command over the network, which airplane mode blocks, a passcode complexity rule only sets how strong the passcode must be, and data-at-rest encryption keeps stored data unreadable without erasing it.

question: A technician adds a VPN connection in Windows 11 Settings, and the company requires IKEv2 rather than letting Windows pick the protocol. Which field of the Add a VPN connection form does the technician change?
explanation: The VPN type field of a Windows VPN connection chooses the tunneling protocol, such as IKEv2, SSTP or L2TP/IPsec, and its default of Automatic lets Windows choose one. VPN provider picks the built-in Windows client or an installed VPN app, Type of sign-in info chooses between a user name and password, a smart card, a one-time password or a certificate, and Server name or address names the VPN server.

question: A gaming laptop's built-in 144 Hz screen is running at only 60 Hz. Which page in Windows 11 Settings lets the user set the screen back to 144 Hz?
explanation: System > Display > Advanced display is where a screen's refresh rate is chosen. The same page shows the signal details and any dynamic refresh rate option. Graphics sets which GPU each app uses and game options such as variable refresh rate, HDR controls high dynamic range output, and Night light warms the screen's colors in the evening.

question: Which order lists these from MOST to LEAST volatile: (1) disk contents, (2) RAM, (3) archived backup media, (4) temporary file systems?
explanation: Under the order of volatility in RFC 3227, memory is lost at power-off, temporary file systems are cleared on restart or cleanup, disk contents persist but change as the system runs, and archived backup media change least. Putting disk contents first, putting temporary files ahead of RAM, or placing disk ahead of temporary file systems each collects longer-lasting evidence before more volatile evidence.

question: A user insists that a PC has a virus and describes several problems. While investigating the symptoms, which problem should the technician treat as a sign of malware?
options: Colored vertical lines run down the screen from startup
The browser home page changes back after each reset
The clock shows an old date each time it starts
The PC shuts off without warning during games
explanation: A browser home page that changes back after being reset is a typical sign of a browser hijacker, so it points to malware. Sudden shutdowns during games suggest overheating or a weak power supply, a clock that loses its date points to a failing CMOS battery, and lines on the screen from startup point to the display or graphics hardware.

question: A technician brings a new laptop into a heated office from a car that sat outside overnight in freezing weather, and droplets of water form on its case. What should the technician do?
options: Wipe the case and keyboard with isopropyl alcohol
Leave it off until it warms to room temperature
Plug in its charger to top up the battery
Blow out its vents with compressed air
explanation: Cold equipment brought into warm air collects condensation inside as well as out, so it should stay powered off until it reaches room temperature and the moisture has evaporated. Compressed air clears dust from vents and isopropyl alcohol cleans surfaces, but neither removes the moisture inside the case, and plugging in the charger puts power into the circuits just as switching the laptop on would.

question: An audit of a small office finds that any visitor on its wireless network could sign in to the router's settings page with the login details listed in the model's online manual. Which practice prevents this?
explanation: Changing the factory administrator username and password matters because the defaults for each model are printed in manuals and shared online, so anyone who can reach the login page can try them. Firmware updates fix flaws in the router's code, disabling SSID broadcast only hides the network name, and a new SSID stops the name from revealing the router's make, but none of them changes the login.

question: After a user describes a printing fault, the technician says, "So the printer shows a paper jam message, but no paper is stuck inside. Is that right?" Which communication technique is this?
options: Restating the issue to confirm it
Setting a timeline for the repair
explanation: Restating the user's description in the technician's own words and asking for confirmation checks that the problem has been understood before any work begins. An open-ended question invites the user to describe the problem rather than confirm it, a timeline tells the user when to expect a fix, and a follow-up checks satisfaction after the work is done.

question: By default, which TCP ports do WinRM listeners use for HTTP and HTTPS?
explanation: Since WinRM 2.0, the default listener ports are 5985 for HTTP and 5986 for HTTPS, and with Kerberos or NTLM authentication the messages are encrypted even over HTTP. Ports 8080 and 8443 are common alternate web ports, 3268 and 3269 serve the Active Directory global catalog over LDAP and LDAPS, and 5900 and 5901 are used by VNC.

question: During a recovery, a technician finds that the backup files from the past month are corrupted and cannot be opened. Which practice would have revealed this before the data was needed?
options: A second copy stored off site
explanation: A backup is proven usable only by restoring from it, so test restores belong on a regular schedule instead of being tried for the first time during an emergency. Encrypting each set protects lost media from being read, an off-site copy survives the loss of the building, and nightly full backups shorten the restore chain, but none of them shows whether the stored files can be opened.

question: A company keeps its servers and all of its backup tapes in one office. The owner wants the data to survive a fire or flood in that office. Which change achieves this?
options: Copying the data to a cloud service
Storing the tapes in a locked cabinet
explanation: A copy held by a cloud service is off site by design, so it survives a fire or flood that destroys the office and everything in it. A locked cabinet protects tapes from theft but not from fire or water, monthly test restores prove that backups can be read, and differential backups change how much each run copies, yet all three leave every copy in the same building.

question: After a user installed a free VPN download, all their browser traffic goes through an unknown proxy server and they see certificate warnings on banking sites. What should the technician do?
options: Add the banking sites to the proxy's bypass list, then restart the browser
Reset the browser to its defaults, then clear its cache, cookies and site data
Turn on secure DNS and enhanced protection, then restart the browser
Remove the proxy setting and the free app, then check for added root certificates
explanation: Malicious software and untrustworthy VPN apps can set a proxy to intercept traffic, and certificate warnings appear when it presents certificates the browser does not trust. Removing the proxy setting and the app, then removing any root certificate it added and scanning, restores direct, trusted connections. A browser reset leaves the system proxy and the app in place, secure DNS and enhanced protection do not route traffic around a proxy, and a bypass list for banking sites leaves every other site intercepted.

question: A dental clinic's billing record shows a patient's name, insurance member number and the dates of her appointments. Which category of regulated data is this?
explanation: Protected health information is any health-related record that can be tied to a person, and it covers billing and insurance details held by a health care provider as well as diagnoses. The record holds no card numbers, so it is not payment card data, and it is neither a company's intellectual property nor government classified information. In the United States, HIPAA sets the rules for protecting it.

question: During a remote session to fix a user's email client, a technician sees an open spreadsheet of staff salaries on the user's screen. What should the technician do?
options: Check whether the file is related to the fault
Report the open file to the security team
Ask the user to close the file before continuing
Capture a screenshot for the ticket record
explanation: Confidential material that has nothing to do with the repair should be kept out of view, so the technician asks the user to close it and then carries on without reading it or mentioning what it contains. A screenshot would copy the salaries into the ticket, reporting the file treats the user's normal work as an incident, and checking whether it is related means reading data the technician does not need.

question: Device Manager shows a yellow warning on a USB host controller with Code 12. What does this code mean?
options: The device reported a fault to Windows
The device cannot find enough free resources
The device has been disabled by a user
No driver is installed for the device
explanation: Code 12 in Device Manager means the device cannot find enough free resources, such as memory ranges or interrupts, usually because other devices already claim them. Code 22 means the device has been disabled, Code 28 means its driver is not installed, and Code 43 means Windows stopped the device after it reported a problem.

question: A user wants every PDF on a Windows 11 PC to open in Adobe Acrobat from now on. In File Explorer, which right-click path leads to the dialog that makes Acrobat the default?
explanation: Open with > Choose another app opens a dialog in which the user selects Acrobat and clicks Always, which makes it the default app for that file type. Choosing Acrobat directly from the Open with list opens only that one file, the Security tab of Properties sets the file's permissions, and the Details tab shows its metadata.

question: A technician sets up a sign-in option on a laptop that uses a short numeric code. The code is checked on the laptop itself and works with no internet connection. Which sign-in option is this?
explanation: A Windows Hello PIN is a numeric code that is checked on the device where it was set up, so it works offline and cannot be used from another computer. A security key and a smart card also take a PIN, but the key or the card checks it, and a picture password uses gestures drawn on a chosen image rather than numbers.

question: A technician plugs a USB drive into a Linux desktop and needs to attach its partition, /dev/sdc1, to the existing empty directory /mnt/usb. Which command does this?
explanation: The mount command attaches the file system on a device to a directory, the mount point, so the drive's files appear under /mnt/usb; umount detaches it again. A symbolic link to /dev/sdc1 points at the device node rather than at its files, dd copies raw blocks, which suits imaging a partition to a file, and mkdir only creates another empty directory.

question: A firewall is set to permit traffic from 192.168.1.0/24 to the web server on port 443 and to deny all other inbound traffic. Which security function do these rules perform?
explanation: Rules that permit or deny traffic by source address, destination and port perform packet filtering, which is the job of an access control list. Intrusion detection looks inside traffic for signs of attack, data encryption protects the contents of traffic in transit, and malware scanning inspects files for malicious code, none of which a permit or deny rule does.

question: A technician sets up a training room where power and network cables would cross a walkway to the instructor's desk. Which action BEST follows safe cable management?
options: Put warning signs at both ends of the cable crossing
Run the cables under the carpet so they lie flat and out of sight
Tape the cables flat across the walkway with hazard tape
Route the cables along the walls inside a surface raceway
explanation: Safe cable management keeps cables out of walkways, routing them along walls or in raceways, and uses a rated floor cable cover only where a crossing cannot be avoided. Hazard tape marks a trip hazard without removing it, cables under carpet can be damaged and overheat unseen, and warning signs suit a short-lived hazard such as a wet floor rather than a permanent crossing.

question: A company's chief executive receives an email that claims to be from a law firm, warns of an urgent lawsuit and asks her to open the attached summons. No one else received it. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: Whaling is phishing aimed at a senior executive, such as a chief executive, whose authority and access make a successful attack especially valuable. Smishing arrives by text message, QR code phishing hides a malicious link in a QR code, and pharming redirects people to a fake website by tampering with name resolution, so none of them is defined by the rank of its target.

question: Before taking a new memory module out of its antistatic bag, what should a technician put on to protect the module from static?
explanation: An ESD wrist strap clipped to a ground point keeps the technician's body at ground potential, so static built up on the body drains away instead of jumping into the module. Insulated rubber gloves guard against electric shock but do not drain static and can even build it up, while safety goggles and an air filtration mask protect the eyes and lungs from dust and debris.

question: A technician finds a program the user never installed that saves everything typed on the workstation to a file and emails that file to an outside address every hour. Which type of malware is this?
explanation: A keylogger records keystrokes and sends them to an attacker, which exposes passwords, card numbers and private messages. A rootkit hides malware from the operating system, adware displays unwanted advertising, and a virus spreads by attaching itself to files that users run.

question: On a Windows Home PC, CompTIA's malware removal procedure turns off System Restore before remediation begins. What is the reason for this step?
options: The malware may start again with Windows
Old restore points may hold the malware
The malware may spread to other computers
Restore points may use space the scan needs
explanation: Turning off System Restore deletes the existing restore points, and old restore points may hold copies of the malware that a later restore would put back on the computer. Keeping the malware from reaching other computers is the reason for quarantine, keeping it from starting with Windows is a reason to scan in Safe Mode, and clearing restore points to free disk space is a job for Disk Cleanup rather than a step of malware removal.

question: A user opens a compromised website. Without the user clicking anything or approving a prompt, the page exploits a flaw in the out-of-date browser and installs malware. Which delivery method is this?
explanation: A drive-by download installs malware through a flaw in a browser or plug-in simply because a page was visited, with no click or approval, which is why keeping browsers updated matters. A phishing attachment has to be opened, bundled software has to be installed, and an infected USB drive has to be connected, so each of them needs an action by the user.

question: To reach a printer, a technician runs a 10-meter patch cable across the floor of a busy hallway. Which risk does this create?
options: A trip hazard for people walking past
A shock to anyone who steps on it
Signal loss from the cable's length
explanation: A cable laid across a walkway is a trip hazard, so it should be run along the walls or overhead, or covered with a cord protector, before people use the hallway. A network cable carries only low voltages that pose no shock risk to someone who steps on it, signal loss matters only as a copper run nears its 100-meter limit, and interference from lighting affects cables run close to fluorescent fixtures.

question: An Android user installed a navigation app as an APK file from a website. Months later, the Google Play version has security fixes, but the user's copy is still on the old version, while the user's other apps stay current. What is the MOST likely reason?
options: It was sideloaded, so Google Play is not managing its updates
It uses location data, so Google Play holds back its updates
A content filter blocks its downloads from the Google Play servers
Play Protect flagged it, so Google Play is blocking its updates
explanation: An app sideloaded from a website is installed outside Google Play, which generally does not keep such apps updated, so it can stay on an old, vulnerable version while store apps update. Reinstalling it from Google Play restores store updates and Play Protect checks. Google Play does not hold back updates for apps that use location, Play Protect warns about or disables harmful apps rather than blocking their updates, and a filter that blocked Google Play would stop every app from updating.

question: A shared folder's share permissions give Sales Full Control and Everyone Read. Its NTFS permissions give Sales Modify and Users Read & execute. A member of both Sales and Users opens the folder from another computer. What access does that user get?
explanation: Over the network, a user gets the more restrictive of the share permissions and the NTFS permissions, after each set is added up across the user's groups. Here the share permissions add up to Full Control and the NTFS permissions to Modify, which already includes Read & execute, so the result is Modify. Full Control is the share permission on its own, Read is what a member of Users outside Sales gets over the network, and Read & execute is what that person gets when signed in at the computer itself, where only NTFS permissions apply.

question: A technician needs messages from known spam senders, and messages that carry known malicious links, stopped before they reach users' inboxes. Which logical control addresses this?
explanation: Email filtering inspects messages on their way to the mailbox and blocks known spam senders, phishing links and dangerous attachments before delivery. Email encryption keeps a message's contents private in transit but lets every message through, web content filtering blocks a malicious site only when someone tries to visit it, and data loss prevention stops sensitive data from leaving the organization.

question: A technician uses an AI tool to write a knowledge base article and publishes it under their own name without review or disclosure. Parts of it closely match a vendor's copyrighted documentation. Which concern does this raise MOST directly?
explanation: Presenting AI-generated text as your own original work, especially when it reproduces someone else's material, is plagiarism and may also infringe copyright; policies typically require reviewing AI output, citing sources and disclosing AI help. Data source is where an AI's information comes from, bias is unfair skew in results, and application integration is AI built into existing tools, so none of them describes passing off someone else's work.

question: On a BIOS-based PC the master boot record is intact, but the code in the first sector of the system partition, which loads Windows Boot Manager, is damaged. Which command should the technician run from the recovery Command Prompt?
explanation: The bootrec /fixboot command writes a new boot sector to the system partition, the part that loads Windows Boot Manager on a BIOS-based PC. The /fixmbr switch rewrites the master boot record instead, /rebuildbcd scans the disks and rebuilds the boot configuration data, and /scanos only lists the installations that the boot configuration data is missing.

question: Users can reach a file server by its IP address but not by its host name. Which command lets a technician send a query for that name to a chosen DNS server and read the reply?
explanation: The nslookup command sends a query straight to a DNS server, either the configured one or any server named on the command line, and prints the answer it gets back. The ipconfig /displaydns command lists only the records the PC has already cached, ipconfig /flushdns empties that cache, and pathping measures delay and packet loss at each router on the path to a host.

question: A technician opens Keychain Access on a Mac. Which task is it used for?
options: Turning on encryption of the startup disk
Granting apps permission to use the camera
Checking apps for a developer ID
explanation: Keychain Access manages the keychain, where macOS keeps saved passwords, certificates and private keys, so a company root certificate is marked as trusted there. Camera permission is granted in Privacy & Security settings, FileVault encrypts the startup disk, and Gatekeeper checks that downloaded apps come from an identified developer.

question: On most current Linux distributions, which component does the kernel start first, as process ID 1, to bring up and manage the system's services?
explanation: systemd is the init system and service manager on most modern distributions: the kernel starts it as PID 1, and it starts and supervises services, controlled with systemctl and logged with journalctl. GRUB is the bootloader that runs before the kernel, sudo runs a single command with elevated privileges, and cron runs scheduled jobs.

question: An attacker posts a forum comment containing hidden code. Whenever other members view the comment, the code runs in their browsers and sends their session cookies to the attacker. Which attack is this?
explanation: Cross-site scripting plants attacker code in a trusted website so that it runs in visitors' browsers, where it can steal session cookies or change what the page shows. SQL injection targets the site's database rather than its visitors, a drive-by download installs malware on the visitor's computer, and an on-path attack intercepts traffic in transit rather than running code in the page.

question: A data center has a fence around its grounds, badge readers on every door and guards at the main entrance. Which security principle does this combination of controls follow?
explanation: Defense in depth layers several independent controls, so an intruder who defeats one still has to get past the others. Zero trust means verifying every request instead of trusting anything because it is inside the network, least privilege gives each account only the access its work needs, and implicit deny blocks whatever a rule set does not explicitly allow.

question: A user receives a text message that claims to be from their bank and asks them to tap a link to confirm their account details. The message does not use the user's name. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: Smishing is phishing sent by text message, and a text that poses as a bank and asks the user to tap a link is a typical case. Bluejacking sends unsolicited messages over Bluetooth rather than through the phone network, spear phishing is aimed at a named person using details about them, and QR code phishing hides the link in a code that the victim scans. The user should not tap the link and should contact the bank through a number from the card or the bank's own website.

question: Before a firewall change goes to the change board, a second engineer checks the proposed rules and implementation steps for mistakes. Which part of the change management process is this?
explanation: Peer review has another qualified person check a change's plan or configuration, catching errors before implementation. Sandbox testing tries the change in an isolated environment, risk analysis rates how likely a failure is and how much harm it would do, and end-user acceptance confirms with users after the change that it works for them.

question: A user with low vision needs Magnifier to start automatically at every sign-in on a Windows PC. Which Control Panel item lets a technician set this up?
explanation: Ease of Access, through the Ease of Access Center, turns on Magnifier, Narrator and the On-Screen Keyboard and can set any of them to start at sign-in. Speech Recognition sets up control of the PC by voice, Mouse offers larger pointer schemes on its Pointers tab, and Fonts installs and removes typefaces rather than enlarging text.

question: An old internal web app depends on an ActiveX control that current browsers do not support. Which response BEST balances keeping the app working with security?
options: Allow ActiveX for that site in Chrome's settings
Open that site in Internet Explorer 11
Open that site in Chrome's compatibility view
Open that site in Edge's IE mode
explanation: Microsoft Edge's Internet Explorer mode can run a legacy site that needs ActiveX controls, limited to the sites an administrator lists, while everything else uses the modern engine and the app is replaced. The Internet Explorer 11 desktop app is retired and disabled on current versions of Windows, Chrome has never supported ActiveX controls, and Compatibility View was an Internet Explorer feature that Chrome does not have.

question: An administrator wants to run PowerShell commands on 50 remote Windows servers from one console using Invoke-Command. Which Windows service must be configured on the servers for this?
explanation: PowerShell remoting with Invoke-Command runs over Windows Remote Management (WinRM), Microsoft's implementation of the WS-Management protocol, and Enable-PSRemoting starts the service, creates a listener and opens the firewall. WMI provides management data that scripts can query, Remote Desktop Services gives a graphical session on one server at a time, and SNMP monitors devices rather than running commands.
