question: A technician partitions a disk with diskpart before a clean install of Windows 11. Which file system must the partition that will hold the Windows folder use?
explanation: Windows must be installed on an NTFS volume, which provides the permissions, journaling and large-file support that the OS depends on. FAT32 is used only for the small EFI system partition beside it, exFAT is meant for removable flash storage, and ReFS is designed for data volumes and is not supported as the Windows system volume.

question: A company must record each laptop's serial number, purchase date, warranty end date and assigned employee, and follow each one until disposal. Which system should hold these records?
explanation: An asset management system keeps the hardware inventory, with serial numbers, purchase and warranty dates and assigned users, and tracks each item from purchase to disposal. A ticketing system records support requests, a network monitoring system watches whether devices are up and performing, and a directory service holds the accounts and groups that people sign in with.

question: A user on a Windows 11 Home laptop follows an online guide and types a console name into the Run box, but Windows reports that it cannot find the file. The same command works on the user's Pro computer at work. Which console was it?
explanation: The Local Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) is included in Windows 11 Pro and higher editions but not in Home, so typing it on a Home computer returns a file-not-found error. Device Manager (devmgmt.msc), Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) and Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) are part of every edition, Home included.

question: A VM's network adapter is misconfigured, so RDP and SSH connections to the guest OS fail, but the technician can still see and use the VM's console through SPICE. Why does SPICE still work?
options: SPICE reaches the display through the hypervisor
SPICE tunnels through the guest's Remote Desktop service
SPICE adds its own virtual network adapter to the guest
SPICE falls back to the VM's serial console
explanation: With SPICE, the hypervisor serves the VM's display, keyboard and mouse, so the console works even when the guest's own networking is broken, which makes it ideal for fixing that network. RDP and SSH are services inside the guest that need its networking. SPICE needs no network adapter of its own inside the guest, does not pass through the guest's Remote Desktop service and does not switch to a serial console.

question: A technician asks a public AI chatbot for a Windows command, and it confidently gives a command-line switch that does not exist. Which AI concern does this show?
explanation: A hallucination is output that sounds confident and plausible but is false, such as an invented command switch, citation or setting; check AI-generated commands against vendor documentation before running them. Bias is skew learned from training data, plagiarism is passing off others' work as your own, and data privacy concerns how personal information is handled.

question: On a shared Windows 11 Pro laptop, a user wants a few personal documents to be unreadable to anyone who signs in with a different account, while the rest of the drive stays unencrypted. Which feature should the user turn on?
explanation: Encrypting File System (EFS) encrypts individual files and folders on an NTFS volume with a key tied to the user's account, so people who sign in with other accounts cannot open them. BitLocker Drive Encryption encrypts a whole drive and does not separate one account from another once Windows is running, BitLocker To Go protects removable drives, and controlled folder access stops untrusted apps from changing protected folders without encrypting anything.

question: Before removing malware from a Windows 11 PC, a technician turns off the feature that saves snapshots of the registry and of Windows files, because those snapshots may hold copies of the malware. Which feature is this?
explanation: System Restore keeps restore points that can contain infected files, so it is turned off before remediation, which deletes the old points, and turned back on with a new restore point once the PC is clean. File History keeps earlier versions of personal files rather than system snapshots, Storage Sense frees space by deleting temporary files, and BitLocker encrypts the drive.

question: In a small data center, every row of servers faces the same direction, so each row blows its exhaust into the intakes of the row behind it. Which change stops this?
options: Lower the temperature set on the cooling units
Arrange the racks in hot and cold aisles
Add a humidifier and air filters to the room
Connect each rack to a larger capacity UPS
explanation: A hot aisle and cold aisle layout turns alternate rows to face each other, so that intakes share a cold aisle, exhausts share a hot aisle and the two airflows no longer mix. A lower set point only cools the mixed air at a higher energy cost, a humidifier and air filters treat dry or dusty air, and a larger UPS gives more runtime in an outage, but none of them keeps exhaust away from the intakes.

question: A link in an email opens a page that looks exactly like a bank's sign-in page. Which check BEST shows whether the page really belongs to the bank?
options: The bank's logo and colors shown on the page
The domain name shown in the address bar
The padlock icon beside the address
The spelling and grammar of the text
explanation: The domain name in the address bar shows which site actually served the page, and a look-alike page is almost always hosted on a domain other than the bank's. The padlock only means the connection is encrypted, which phishing sites also achieve with free certificates, and a copied page can have the bank's exact logo, colors, spelling and grammar.

question: An employee working from home needs the company laptop itself to reach internal file shares, printers and intranet sites, just as it does in the office. Which technology is designed for this?
explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) builds an encrypted tunnel that places the remote laptop on the company network, so its own apps reach file shares, printers and intranet sites as they would in the office. RDP and VNC instead show the desktop of another computer, and SSH gives a command-line session or forwards single ports rather than joining the laptop to the network.

question: A technician must choose the OS for a machine that will host shared files and a database for 40 employees around the clock. What is a server OS designed for that a workstation OS is not?
options: Giving one user a fast desktop
Handling many network clients at once
Running one fixed task on dedicated hardware
explanation: A server OS is built to serve many network clients at once and to run its services around the clock, while a workstation OS is tuned for the one person at its keyboard. A fast desktop for one user is the goal of a workstation OS, saving battery on touch devices is the goal of a mobile OS, and running one fixed task on dedicated hardware describes an embedded OS.

question: A company uses a third-party remote desktop tool with unattended access, so technicians can reach office PCs at any hour through the provider's cloud service. Which control would stop someone with a stolen technician password from connecting?
options: Firewall rules that block inbound connections
Multifactor sign-in to the vendor account
Network Level Authentication on each PC
explanation: Multifactor authentication on the remote access tool's accounts means a stolen password alone cannot open a session, which matters most when unattended access lets the account reach the PCs at any time. Blocking inbound connections does not affect a tool that connects out to its provider, Network Level Authentication protects Remote Desktop, and key-based authentication protects SSH logins.

question: A Windows 11 Pro PC must be joined to an Active Directory domain. Where does a technician begin this?
options: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings
Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Connect
Settings > Accounts > Other users > Add account
Settings > System > Activation > Change product key
explanation: In Windows 11, Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Connect leads to the link that joins the PC to a local Active Directory domain, and the System Properties dialog, opened from Domain or workgroup on the About page, can do the same. Change product key upgrades Windows Home, which cannot join a domain, to an edition such as Pro, which this PC already runs, Add account under Other users adds a local or Microsoft account for another person, and Advanced network settings holds adapter and sharing options rather than domain membership.

question: A change request for a database upgrade includes a rollback plan that reinstalls the old version. The change board also asks for a backup plan. What should the backup plan cover?
options: A trial of the upgrade, run on a sandbox copy, to find problems in advance
A list of the users, kept with the request, to notify once the work is done
A verified copy of the data, taken first, to restore if the upgrade damages it
A second maintenance window, booked ahead, in case this one runs over
explanation: A rollback plan undoes the change itself, for example by reinstalling the previous version, while a backup plan protects the data with a verified copy taken beforehand, so it can be restored if the change or the rollback goes wrong. A sandbox trial tests the change before it is made, a notification list belongs to communicating the change, and a second maintenance window is part of scheduling.

question: A user who is hard of hearing wants on-screen text for any speech played on a Windows 11 PC, including videos and online meetings. Which Settings category turns this on?
explanation: Accessibility > Captions turns on live captions, which show any speech the PC plays, from videos to meetings, as on-screen text. Privacy & security holds the switch for online speech recognition, Time & language sets the language and voices used for speech, and System holds the sound output and input devices.

question: A printer is attached by USB to a Windows 11 workstation. Other users on the network need to print to it through that workstation. Which tab of the printer's Printer properties dialog does the technician use to allow this?
explanation: A printer attached to one Windows PC is offered to others on the Sharing tab of its Printer properties dialog, where Share this printer is turned on and a share name is set, with file and printer sharing also on. Security sets who may print or manage documents once the printer is shared, Ports picks the connection the printer uses, such as USB or a TCP/IP port, and Advanced sets the driver, spooling and the hours the printer is available.

question: A PC that has had no software or driver changes keeps showing a blue screen with the stop code MEMORY_MANAGEMENT. What should the technician do first?
options: Increase the virtual memory paging file
Test the RAM with Windows Memory Diagnostic
Roll back the most recent driver update
Run chkdsk /r on the system drive
explanation: The MEMORY_MANAGEMENT stop code points first to faulty RAM, so testing the memory with Windows Memory Diagnostic is the quickest way to confirm or rule out a bad module. A larger paging file answers low-memory warnings rather than stop errors, chkdsk /r looks for disk errors and bad sectors, and rolling back a driver helps only when the crashes began after a driver changed.

question: A workstation's processor stays busy although Task Manager shows no process using it, and a scan from bootable media finds files that Windows directory listings do not show. Which type of malware is this?
explanation: A rootkit changes what the operating system reports about processes and files, so tools that run inside Windows cannot see what it hides. A keylogger records keystrokes, ransomware makes itself known by encrypting files and demanding payment, and stalkerware secretly reports a person's location and messages to someone else.

question: An employee who read work email on a personal phone is leaving. IT must remove the company's apps, accounts and files from the phone but leave the employee's photos and personal apps alone. Which capability does this?
explanation: A selective wipe, also called an enterprise wipe, removes only the company's apps, accounts and data from a managed phone and leaves the owner's personal content in place. A full remote wipe erases everything and suits a lost company-owned phone, a remote passcode reset helps a user who is locked out, and a remote lock secures a missing phone without removing anything.

question: Since its last OS update, an Android phone restarts by itself several times a day. No newer update is available, it is not overheating, and its battery health shows as good. What should the technician do first?
explanation: Safe mode starts Android with every third-party app turned off, so if the restarts stop there, an app that does not work with the new OS version is the likely cause. A factory reset is the later step if the cause cannot be isolated, a battery replacement suits a worn battery with poor health, and a network settings reset is for Wi-Fi, cellular and Bluetooth faults.

question: A small company is setting up WPA2-Enterprise for its office Wi-Fi. Which server will the access points send each sign-in to for checking?
explanation: WPA2-Enterprise uses 802.1X, in which the access point passes each sign-in to a RADIUS server that checks the credentials, often against Active Directory, and tells the access point whether to let the device join. A TACACS+ server checks administrators who manage network devices, a Kerberos server issues tickets for domain services, and a proxy server filters and forwards web traffic.

question: An administrator creates a new hire's account in on-premises Active Directory at 9:05. At 9:10 the new hire can sign in to their domain PC but not to Microsoft 365, which says the account does not exist. Directory sync runs on Microsoft Entra Connect's default schedule. What is the MOST likely explanation?
options: The PC needs gpupdate /force run on it first
The account has not been copied to the cloud yet
The cloud account must also be created by hand
The account needs a license before it can exist
explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync runs a sync cycle every 30 minutes by default, so a new on-premises account reaches the cloud only after the next cycle, which an administrator can trigger sooner with Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta. Synced accounts are not created by hand, a Group Policy refresh does not sync accounts, and licenses are assigned to accounts that already exist in the cloud directory.

question: An engineer receives an email from an outside address that greets her by name, mentions the project she leads and the talk she gave last week, and asks her to sign in through a link to download the slides. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: Spear phishing aims a message at one person and uses details about them, such as their name, work and recent activity, to make it convincing. Whaling is the same approach aimed at a senior executive, smishing uses text messages, and business email compromise uses a hijacked or impersonated company or supplier mailbox to request payments or data.

question: A technician must make a USB headset the default playback device and raise its microphone's recording level on a Windows workstation. Which Control Panel item handles both?
explanation: The Sound item (mmsys.cpl) sets the default playback and recording devices and, in each device's properties, its volume levels. Devices and Printers shows the headset but does not set audio defaults or levels, Device Manager installs and rolls back its driver, and Speech Recognition sets up a microphone for voice commands.

question: A technician uses the manufacturer's recovery partition to return a laptop to its factory state. What will the laptop hold when the process finishes?
options: The original OS, with the user's files kept
The original OS and vendor software, with no user data
The current OS, returned to an earlier restore point
The newest Windows release, with no user data
explanation: A recovery partition holds the manufacturer's factory image, so restoring from it brings back the original OS and preinstalled software and erases user data and any apps added later. Keeping the user's files is the Keep my files choice of Reset this PC, the newest release comes from a cloud download or new installation media, and returning to a restore point is System Restore.

question: Old hard disk drives holding HR records will not be reused. Which destruction method erases them by exposing them to a powerful magnetic field?
explanation: Degaussing erases magnetic media by exposing it to a powerful magnetic field, which scrambles the stored data and leaves a modern hard drive unusable. Shredding cuts a drive into small pieces, incineration burns it at very high temperature, and drilling puts holes through its platters, so none of them relies on magnetism.

question: A sales team is replacing its iPads with Android tablets. Its ordering app was bought from Apple's App Store. What must be done for the team to use the app on the new tablets?
options: Copy the iPad app package to each tablet
Sign in to each tablet with the Apple ID
Install the Android version of the app
Restore the iPad backup to each Android tablet
explanation: Mobile apps are built for one platform, so an app bought for iPadOS will not run on Android, and an Android version from the vendor must be installed, usually from Google Play. An iPad backup restores only to Apple devices, an Apple ID restores past purchases only on Apple hardware, and an iPad app package cannot be installed on Android.

question: A user calls the help desk because a laptop cannot connect to the internet. When the technician opens a ticket for the call, what should be recorded first?
options: The support tier that the ticket is escalated to
The user's contact details and the symptoms
The fix that was applied and how it was verified
A category and a severity rating for the fault
explanation: A new ticket starts with who is reporting the problem, how to reach them, the device involved and a clear description of the symptoms, because every later step depends on that information. The category and severity are set from the description, an escalation tier is chosen only if the first tier cannot resolve the fault, and the fix and its verification are recorded when the work is finished.

question: A company sends old monitors, keyboards and mice, none of which store data, to an e-waste company. Which document should it keep as proof that the equipment was disposed of properly?
explanation: A certificate of recycling is the recycler's written confirmation that equipment was processed in line with environmental rules, and the company keeps it for audits. A memorandum of understanding records what two parties have agreed, a safety data sheet explains how to handle and dispose of a hazardous material such as toner, and a chain of custody form tracks who held items along the way.

question: On a Linux workstation, every user can read /etc/passwd, but regular users cannot read /etc/shadow. What does /etc/shadow hold that makes this restriction necessary?
options: The private keys that identify the SSH server
The password hashes of the local user accounts
The hashed passwords of the local groups
The sudo rules that grant users administrator rights
explanation: Password hashes, with their aging and expiry dates, are kept in /etc/shadow, which regular users cannot read, because hashes in a readable file could be copied and cracked offline. The /etc/passwd file holds the names, UIDs, home folders and shells that many programs need, and its password field normally shows only an x. SSH host keys are kept under /etc/ssh, sudo rules in /etc/sudoers, and group passwords in /etc/gshadow.

question: A guard sees a visitor slip through a secured door directly behind an employee who badged in and did not notice the visitor. Which threat is this?
explanation: Tailgating is following an authorized person through a secured entrance without presenting a credential of one's own. Impersonation means pretending to be someone else, such as a contractor or a manager, shoulder surfing is watching someone enter a password or PIN, and dumpster diving is searching discarded material for useful information.

question: A shopping site goes offline after thousands of home routers and cameras, all infected with the same malware, start sending it requests at the same moment. Which type of attack is this?
explanation: A distributed denial of service attack floods a target from many compromised devices at once, often a botnet of routers and cameras, so blocking one source address does not stop it. A DoS attack comes from a single source, a replay attack resends captured valid traffic to repeat a transaction or a sign-in, and an XSS attack runs injected code in visitors' browsers rather than overwhelming the site.

question: After a meeting, a presenter wants to send an outside client a slide deck stored in the company's cloud storage. The client should be able to see the slides but not change them, and the original must stay in the company's storage. What should the presenter do?
options: Create a company account for the client
Share the deck with view access
Move the deck to the client's cloud account
Share the deck with permission to edit
explanation: Cloud presentation tools such as PowerPoint for the web and Google Slides can share a file with view permission, so the client sees the current slides but cannot edit them, and the file stays in the company's storage. Edit permission would let the client change the deck, moving it hands over the original, and a company account gives the client far more access than needed.

question: A school will load Windows 11 onto 60 new computers with blank drives from its WDS server, using no USB drives or discs. Which setting must be turned on in each computer?
options: Secure Boot in the UEFI settings
Fast Boot in the UEFI settings
PXE boot on the network adapter
explanation: PXE lets the network adapter boot a computer from a deployment server such as WDS, so it must be enabled when there is no local boot media. Wake-on-LAN only powers a computer on from across the network, Fast Boot shortens startup by skipping device checks, and Secure Boot controls which boot loaders may run, so none of them starts a network boot.

question: Microsoft Defender Antivirus quarantines a program that the accounting team needs, and the vendor confirms that the file is safe. How can a technician get the program back?
options: Roll it back with System Restore
Recover it from the Recycle Bin
explanation: A quarantined file is held in a protected folder where it cannot run, and Protection history in Windows Security lists it with a Restore action that puts it back. The Recycle Bin holds only files that users delete, System Restore rolls back system settings and drivers rather than files held by Defender, and allowing a program through the firewall changes its network access without bringing it back.

question: A Linux workstation reaches websites by IP address but not by name, and ip route shows the correct default gateway. Which file should the technician check next?
explanation: /etc/resolv.conf lists the DNS servers (nameserver lines, up to three) and search domains the system's resolver uses, so a wrong or missing nameserver breaks name lookups while connections by IP address still work. On many systems a service such as NetworkManager or systemd-resolved writes this file. /etc/fstab controls mounts, /etc/shadow holds password hashes, and /etc/passwd holds account details.

question: Which stop code does Windows show if csrss.exe or wininit.exe is terminated?
explanation: CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED appears when a process that Windows cannot run without, such as csrss.exe, wininit.exe or services.exe, stops unexpectedly, so the whole system halts. VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE means the display driver stopped responding and could not be reset, NTFS_FILE_SYSTEM points to a fault in the driver that reads NTFS volumes, and MEMORY_MANAGEMENT points to a memory fault, often in RAM.

question: A training team may use AI to help write course material. Which practice BEST avoids plagiarism?
options: Have a manager review each draft and approve it for release
Cite the sources the drafts draw on and disclose the use of AI
Use the approved private AI tool and leave out client data
Check each draft's spelling and grammar, then fix its layout
explanation: AI can reproduce or closely paraphrase existing work, so drafts need reworking, citations for the sources they draw on and disclosure of AI help in line with policy. A private AI tool protects company data but can still copy text, a manager's approval checks quality without crediting anyone, and a spelling and grammar check fixes wording without showing where it came from.

question: A firewall accepts traffic from a partner's network. An outside attacker crafts packets whose source address field holds one of the partner's addresses, so the firewall lets them through. Which technique is this?
explanation: Spoofing falsifies the source of traffic, such as an IP address, a MAC address or an email sender, so that it appears to come from someone trusted. An on-path attack relays traffic between two parties rather than forging where it comes from, a replay attack resends traffic that was captured earlier, and phishing deceives people with fraudulent messages rather than deceiving a firewall.

question: A hardening checklist for reception PCs says to reduce their attack surface, and an audit finds several services running that the PCs never use. Which action BEST follows the checklist?
options: Run the unneeded services as the Local Service account
Set the startup type of the unneeded services to Disabled
Set the startup type of the unneeded services to Automatic (Delayed Start)
Stop the unneeded services from the Task Manager window
explanation: Every running service is potential attack surface, especially one that listens on the network, so services a computer does not need should be stopped and set to Disabled so that they cannot start again. Automatic (Delayed Start) only postpones a service at boot, stopping it in Task Manager lasts only until the next restart, and running it as Local Service lowers its privileges but leaves it running.

question: A technician runs a patch script that a stranger posted on an internet forum. The patches install, but the script also downloads a program that starts sending company files to an unknown server. Which scripting risk does this show?
explanation: Running a script from an untrusted source can bring in malware, because hidden lines can download and launch a malicious program alongside the work the script claims to do. An inadvertent settings change is an honest mistake in a script's own logic, a crash from mishandled resources comes from code that exhausts memory, and credential exposure comes from passwords written into a script. Reading the code and testing it in an isolated virtual machine first reduces this risk.

question: A company applies one policy to mobile OSs and another to workstation OSs. Which of these OSs falls under the mobile policy?
explanation: iPadOS is a mobile OS, in the same family as iOS and Android, even when an iPad is used with a keyboard like a laptop. ChromeOS, macOS and Linux are workstation OSs, although Chromebooks can also run Android apps and Android itself is built on the Linux kernel.

question: A user overwrote an important spreadsheet this morning and wants yesterday's version back, but also wants to keep today's version in case some of today's edits are needed. Which recovery option should the technician choose?
options: Restore the backup copy to an alternative location
Roll the PC back to a System Restore point
Restore the whole drive from last night's backup
Restore the backup copy in place over the current file
explanation: Restoring to an alternative location puts the backup copy in a different folder or under a different name, leaving the current file untouched so the user can compare and combine the two. An in-place restore would overwrite today's version, restoring the whole drive would roll back every other file as well, and System Restore returns system settings and drivers to an earlier state without recovering personal files.

question: A technician suspects a rootkit on a workstation, although the installed antivirus reports nothing. Which approach gives the BEST chance of detecting it?
options: Review the startup apps listed in Task Manager
Scan the disk from bootable media outside Windows
Run System File Checker from an elevated prompt
Run the installed antivirus again in Safe Mode
explanation: A rootkit hides itself from tools that run inside the infected operating system, so scanning the disk after starting from clean bootable media, when the rootkit is not running, is the most reliable way to find it. Safe Mode still starts the infected copy of Windows, where a rootkit driver can load, System File Checker repairs protected Windows files, and Task Manager shows only what the rootkit allows it to see.

question: A user wants a Mac to back itself up automatically every hour to an external drive. Which built-in macOS feature should be set up?
explanation: Time Machine backs up a Mac automatically to an external or network drive, keeping hourly backups for the past day, daily backups for the past month and weekly backups before that. Migration Assistant moves accounts and files to a new Mac, Disk Utility formats and repairs disks, and FileVault encrypts the startup disk.

question: A school issues tablets to students and must block adult and gambling websites on them, including when they are used on home Wi-Fi. Which mobile security control does this?
options: A locator app installed on each student's tablet
Remote wipe set up for lost or stolen tablets
explanation: Content filtering blocks websites and apps by category or list, and when it is applied on the device, through MDM or a filtering app, it works on any network rather than only behind the school's firewall. Device encryption protects stored data, remote wipe erases a lost device, and a locator app finds it.

question: A technician edits a router's configuration one evening without telling anyone, and the next morning a branch office cannot connect. Which control exists so that no one can alter a production system without others knowing?
options: Sandbox testing of the new settings
A rollback plan for the router
A risk analysis of the planned edit
explanation: Approval of a change request means each change is recorded, assessed and authorized before work starts, so that no one alters a production system without others knowing. Sandbox testing catches faults before a change goes live, a rollback plan sets out how to undo a change, and a risk analysis rates how likely and how harmful a failure would be, but none of these stops an unrecorded edit.

question: Microsoft Defender detects a suspicious file on a user's PC. The technician wants the file kept where it cannot run, so that it can be put back if the detection turns out to be a false positive. Which action should the technician take?
explanation: Quarantine moves a detected file into a protected area where it cannot run, and keeps it so that it can be restored if the detection proves to be a false positive. Deleting the file removes it for good, which suits a confirmed threat; allowing it lets it run, which is right only once it is known to be safe; and submitting it for analysis asks the vendor for a verdict but does not stop it from running.

question: The group that owns plan.txt must be able to change the file, and every other permission on it must stay as it is. Which command does this?
explanation: In the symbolic notation of chmod, g stands for the owning group and +w adds write permission without touching any other permission. Using o+w would give write to all other users, u+w would give it to the owner, and a+w would give it to the owner, the group and everyone else at once.

question: An email that appears to come from IT says the user's MFA must be re-registered and asks them to scan a QR code with their phone. Why would an attacker put the link in a QR code rather than a clickable link?
options: A QR code opens its link at once, and the phone shows no address for the user to check first
A QR code encrypts its link, and email filters cannot read anything inside encrypted content
A QR code hides its link from text filters, and the scan opens it on a less guarded phone
A QR code carries a signature, and phones trust signed links that come from IT
explanation: A QR code is an image, so filters that check the links in an email's text can miss it, and scanning it moves the victim to a phone that often lacks the company's web filtering and has a small screen that hides a suspicious address. Phones show the address a code holds before opening it, QR codes are an encoding rather than encryption, and they carry no signature that a phone could trust.

question: An Android phone will not pair with any Bluetooth accessory. Removing the old pairings, clearing the Bluetooth app's cache and restarting the phone did not help, and other phones pair with the same accessories normally. What should the technician try next?
options: Perform a factory reset on the phone
Reset the network and Bluetooth settings
Update the firmware and re-pair each accessory
Turn on Bluetooth scanning in the location settings
explanation: Android's network reset, labeled Reset Wi-Fi, mobile and Bluetooth on many phones, clears every saved pairing record along with the Wi-Fi and cellular settings. It is the next step when one phone fails with accessories that work with other phones. Updating and re-pairing the accessories would matter only if they failed with every phone, Bluetooth scanning helps location services find nearby devices rather than pair with them, and a factory reset erases the whole phone and comes after this reset.

question: On a PC that turns off at random, Event Viewer shows a Kernel-Power event with ID 41 after each failure. What does this event mean?
options: Windows recovered from a stop error and saved a dump
The system restarted without shutting down cleanly first
The event log service started during boot
A user or program requested a planned restart
explanation: Kernel-Power Event ID 41 is logged at the next startup when Windows finds that the system restarted without first shutting down cleanly, as happens after a power loss, a forced power-off or a hard crash. A planned restart by a user or program is logged as Event ID 1074, a recovered stop error as Event ID 1001, and the event log service starting at boot as Event ID 6005.

question: A six-month-old Android phone becomes very hot during long calls and then reboots without warning. It stays cool and stable when idle. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: A failing lithium-ion battery heats up under a sustained load such as a long call, and the phone reboots or shuts down to protect itself, so the battery should be inspected for swelling and replaced. A faulty proximity sensor leaves the screen on or lets a cheek press buttons during calls, a failing charging port causes slow or intermittent charging, and a faulty earpiece makes the caller hard to hear, but none of them makes the phone overheat.

question: Before a contract technician starts work on a law firm's servers, the firm asks the technician to sign a document promising to keep any client information they see confidential. What is this document?
explanation: An NDA is a legal agreement to keep specified information confidential, common for contractors who may see sensitive data. An SLA sets service levels, a EULA sets the terms for using software, and an AUP governs how users may use an organization's systems.

question: A licensed engineering program installs normally on a new laptop, but it starts only while a small USB device from the software vendor is plugged in. What is the USB device?
options: A FIDO2 key for signing in to Windows
A drive that holds the program's files
A Wi-Fi adapter that reaches the license server
A hardware token that holds the license
explanation: An external hardware token, often called a dongle, carries the license for some specialized programs, which refuse to run unless the token is attached. A FIDO2 security key signs a user in rather than licensing a program, a USB drive would store files instead of unlocking the software, and a Wi-Fi adapter connects the laptop to a network but holds no license.

question: Some files on a secondary data drive (D:) return read errors when users open them. A technician wants chkdsk to locate bad sectors on the drive and recover the readable information from them. Which command does this?
explanation: The /r switch makes chkdsk locate bad sectors and recover the readable information in them, and it includes every repair that /f makes. The /f switch fixes file system errors without scanning the disk surface, /x first forces the volume to dismount and then works like /f, and /scan checks an NTFS volume while it stays online.

question: A technician is following CompTIA's seven-step procedure for removing malware from a Windows 11 Home PC. Which of the procedure's steps comes last?
options: Enable System Restore and make a restore point
Educate the user on avoiding infection
Schedule scans and run the latest updates
explanation: CompTIA's malware removal procedure ends by educating the end user, so that the habits that let the malware in do not bring it back. Remediating the infected computer is the fourth step, scheduling scans and running updates is the fifth, and enabling System Restore and making a restore point is the sixth, just before education.

question: A technician adds a new, empty SSD to a desktop, but it does not appear in File Explorer. Which graphical tool should the technician use to initialize the drive, create a partition on it and give it a letter?
explanation: Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) initializes a new disk, creates and formats partitions and assigns drive letters in a graphical console. System Information and Device Manager can confirm that Windows detects the drive but cannot partition it, and Optimize Drives runs TRIM or defragmentation on volumes that already exist.

question: A sales manager who was passed over for promotion copies the customer database to a personal cloud drive, using only the access her job gives her, and sends it to a competitor. Which term describes this?
explanation: An insider threat comes from someone with legitimate access, such as an employee or contractor, who misuses it, so perimeter defenses do not stop it and controls such as least privilege and monitoring matter. A supply chain attack arrives through a supplier's product or service, impersonation means posing as someone else, and spoofing falsifies the source of traffic or messages; the manager needed none of them.

question: On battery, a laptop's external fingerprint reader stops responding after it sits unused for a few minutes, even while the user keeps working, and recovers once it is unplugged and plugged back in. Which Power Options setting is the likely cause?
explanation: USB selective suspend lets Windows cut power to an idle USB device to save battery, and some devices do not wake from it until they are reconnected. Turn on fast startup changes how the PC shuts down and starts, while Sleep after and Hibernate after put the whole laptop into a low-power state after idle time, not one device while the user works.

question: A VPN user's credentials are accepted, and the authentication server then tells the VPN concentrator which internal networks that user may reach. Which security function is the server performing at that point?
explanation: Authorization decides what a user who has already proved their identity is allowed to reach, such as which internal networks a VPN user may use. Authentication is the step just before it that checks the credentials, accounting records what the user does, such as session times and data used, and auditing is the later review of records like those.

question: A payroll service fails to start, and Event Viewer logs error 1053 for it. What does this error mean?
options: A service that it depends on failed to start
The service did not respond to Windows in time
The service account's password was rejected at logon
The service is set to a startup type of Disabled
explanation: Error 1053 means the service did not answer the start or control request from the Service Control Manager within the time allowed, often because it hangs while starting or waits on something that is unavailable. A rejected service account password produces error 1069, a startup type of Disabled produces error 1058, and a failed dependency produces error 1068.

question: Windows' Password must meet complexity requirements policy is enabled. Which new password would be accepted for the account jsmith, whose display name is John Smith?
explanation: Windows' complexity policy rejects a password that contains the account name or any word of the display name that is three or more characters long. It also requires characters from three of five categories: uppercase, lowercase, digits, symbols and other Unicode letters. Harbor7-Lantern uses four categories and no part of either name; Copper9-Smith contains Smith from the display name, Jsmith-2026 contains the account name, and maple-river uses only two categories.

question: An iPhone with 20 GB of free space fails every app update, even for free apps, with the message "Unable to Download App." Other phones on the same Wi-Fi update normally, and last week a subscription renewal on the account was charged to a card that had expired. What should the technician check next?
options: The App Store automatic updates setting
The payment status of the Apple ID
The space left in the iCloud plan
The Ask to Buy approval setting
explanation: An unpaid balance on an Apple ID, such as a renewal charged to an expired card, blocks App Store downloads, including updates to free apps, until the billing problem is fixed. An iCloud plan stores backups and files rather than apps, Ask to Buy holds a child's new downloads for a parent's approval, and the automatic updates setting decides only whether updates install on their own.

question: A newly installed program on a Windows 11 PC must accept connections from other PCs on the office network, but Windows Defender Firewall blocks its incoming traffic. What should the technician do?
options: Turn on file and printer sharing
Add the program to the allowed apps list
Add an outbound rule for the program
Turn on network discovery for this network
explanation: Windows Defender Firewall blocks unsolicited incoming connections by default, and adding a program to its allowed apps list creates an inbound exception for that program alone. Outgoing traffic is allowed by default, so an outbound rule does not help, and network discovery and file and printer sharing open only the ports that those features use.

question: A technician asks an AI chatbot for the latest firmware version for the company's router model, and it names a version that is two releases old. Which AI concern does this show, and what should the technician do?
options: Accuracy: its training data ends at a cutoff, so check the vendor's website
Bias: it favors popular releases, so compare it with a second chatbot
Hallucination: it made up the version, so ask again with a clearer prompt
Data source: it lacks company records, so connect it to the IT asset database
explanation: AI models are trained on data up to a cutoff date and may not know about recent releases, so answers about current versions can be wrong and should be checked against the vendor's own site. Company records would not show the vendor's newest release, the version it named is real rather than invented, and a second chatbot can share the same out-of-date training data.

question: An attacker signs in to a company's VPN with the valid user name and password of a person who stopped working there six months ago. Which practice would have prevented this?
options: Setting a longer minimum password length
Disabling accounts as part of offboarding
explanation: Disabling a person's accounts as soon as they leave, as part of offboarding, makes their old credentials useless to anyone who obtains them. Account lockout reacts only to failed attempts, and a longer minimum password length only makes passwords harder to guess or crack; neither helps when the correct password is used. Patching the VPN server fixes software flaws, but no flaw was needed here.

question: After a server outage stopped order processing for four hours, the IT manager writes a formal account of what happened and when, its cause, its effect on the business and the steps that will prevent a repeat. Which document is this?
explanation: An incident report is the formal record of a significant event: its timeline, cause, business impact and the actions taken to resolve it and to prevent it from happening again. A service ticket tracks one support request through to resolution, a change request asks for approval to modify a system, and a knowledge base article records a known problem and its fix for technicians to reuse.

question: A small business must make its web server reachable from the internet, yet keep an attacker who takes over that server from reaching the office computers. Which configuration meets both needs?
explanation: A screened subnet places public-facing servers on their own network segment, which the internet can reach but which has no open path into the internal network. Port mapping makes a server reachable but leaves it on the same LAN as the office computers, a guest network separates visiting wireless devices, and IP filtering blocks traffic to or from listed addresses.

question: A user wants hidden files, and the extensions at the end of file names, to be shown when browsing folders on a Windows PC. Which Control Panel item changes both?
explanation: File Explorer Options has a View tab where hidden files can be shown and Hide extensions for known file types can be cleared. Default Programs chooses which app opens each file type, File History backs up files from the user's folders to another drive, and Indexing Options decides which locations Windows Search catalogs.

question: A technician wants to run TRIM on a laptop's SSD by hand from a graphical tool and to see when each volume last had this done. Which built-in tool should be used?
explanation: Optimize Drives (dfrgui) sends TRIM to SSDs and defragments hard drives, and it lists the last run and current status of every volume. Disk Management creates and formats partitions, Disk Cleanup deletes temporary and unneeded files to free space, and Storage Spaces groups several drives into a pool that can mirror data.

question: A surge protector under a desk catches fire while it is still plugged in and powering two computers. In the United States system, which class of fire extinguisher is rated for this fire?
explanation: Class C extinguishers use agents that do not conduct electricity, such as carbon dioxide or dry chemical, so they are the ones rated for fires in equipment that is still energized. Class A is for ordinary combustibles such as paper and wood and often uses water, which conducts, Class B is for flammable liquids and gases, and Class D is for burning metals such as magnesium.

question: A technician wants the browser to show a full-page warning whenever a user tries to open a site that appears on a list of known phishing and malware sites. Which browser setting should be turned on?
explanation: Safe browsing checks each address against a regularly updated list of known phishing and malware sites and shows a warning page before the site opens. Private browsing only discards history and cookies when the window closes, browser sync copies bookmarks and settings between devices, and autofill enters saved form data.

question: In the Windows Defender Firewall item of Control Panel, which link opens the console where a technician can create an outbound rule that blocks one program?
options: Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall
Turn Windows Defender Firewall on or off
explanation: Advanced settings opens Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security, the console in which inbound and outbound rules are created for programs, ports and addresses. Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall only lets chosen apps receive incoming connections, Turn Windows Defender Firewall on or off sets the firewall for each network profile, and Change notification settings controls the alerts shown when an app is blocked.

question: A technician who usually works at a warehouse is sent for a day to a law office whose dress code calls for suits from staff and visitors alike. What should the technician wear?
explanation: A technician should dress to match the environment being visited, and a dress code that calls for suits means formal business attire. Business casual, such as slacks and a collared shirt without a tie, fits most ordinary offices, the usual work uniform fits the warehouse, and protective safety gear belongs on sites with physical hazards such as construction areas.

question: A user's phone joins a Wi-Fi network that has the company's SSID, but its access point belongs to an attacker parked outside. Soon after, the user's email password is stolen. Which attack is this?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue access point that copies a trusted network's SSID so that devices join it, which lets the attacker capture what users send through it. Wardriving only searches an area for wireless networks, shoulder surfing means watching someone type a password, and a brute-force attack guesses a password through many attempts, so none of them needs a fake access point.

question: Following CompTIA's SOHO malware removal procedure, a technician has just reimaged an infected Windows 11 Home PC. What should the technician do NEXT?
explanation: In CompTIA's procedure, reimaging or reinstalling is the last resort within remediation, and the next step is to schedule scans and run updates, followed by enabling System Restore and creating a restore point, and then educating the end user. Creating a restore point therefore comes one step later, quarantining the PC is the second step, done before remediation begins, and educating the end user is the final step.

question: A user must turn a folder into an encrypted .dmg file before sending it to a colleague. Which macOS tool can create it?
explanation: Disk Utility creates disk images, including an encrypted .dmg made from a folder, and it also checks, repairs and erases disks. FileVault encrypts the whole startup disk, Finder can compress a folder into an unencrypted .zip file, and Preview can protect a PDF with a password.

question: A technician wants a Windows 11 Pro workstation to require users to press Ctrl+Alt+Delete before they sign in, so that a fake sign-in screen cannot collect their passwords. Which tool holds this setting?
explanation: Local Security Policy holds the security option Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL, which is set to Disabled to make users press Ctrl+Alt+Delete before signing in. Only Windows can intercept that key combination, so pressing it always brings up the genuine sign-in screen rather than a program imitating it. Local Users and Groups manages accounts and group membership, System Configuration controls boot and startup options, and Credential Manager stores saved passwords for websites and network resources.

question: At the end of each day, a technician clears the cache and cookies on a library computer that the public shares. Which security benefit does this give?
options: Sites cannot open windows on their own
Downloads are checked for known malware
explanation: Clearing cookies deletes the session tokens that keep people signed in, and clearing the cache removes stored copies of pages, so the next person cannot reuse an earlier user's sign-in or see what was viewed. Checking downloads is the job of safe browsing, encrypted connections come from HTTPS, and stopping new windows is the pop-up blocker's job.

question: A Linux workstation must reach a test server called stage01 at 10.0.5.20, which is not in DNS. The technician wants this name to work on this workstation only. Which file should be edited?
explanation: /etc/hosts maps host names to IP addresses on the local machine, so a line such as '10.0.5.20 stage01' makes the name work there without a DNS record. The /etc/resolv.conf file lists the DNS servers and search domains to query, /etc/fstab lists file systems to mount, and /etc/passwd lists user accounts.

question: A software audit finds a design program installed on 30 workstations, but the company holds 25 licenses for it. Which action brings the company into compliance?
options: Buy licenses for the extra copies
Record the licenses in the asset inventory
Upgrade the licenses to the newest version
explanation: A company is compliant only when every installed copy is covered by a valid license, so 30 copies need 30 licenses, which means buying licenses for the 5 extra copies or removing those copies. Renewing the licenses already held still leaves 5 copies unlicensed, upgrading them changes which version they cover rather than how many copies, and recording them in the asset inventory tracks the shortfall without closing it.

question: A desktop shows "No operating system found" at power-on. In the firmware setup, its only drive appears neither in the boot order nor in the list of storage devices. What should the technician do first?
options: Run Startup Repair from recovery media
Move the drive to the top of the boot order
Check the drive's connection to the board
explanation: Firmware that cannot see a drive at all cannot boot from it, so the first step is to check the drive's physical connection, its cables or its seating in the slot, before any software repair. Startup Repair and bootrec /rebuildbcd fix boot files on a drive the computer can already read, and the boot order can be changed only for a drive that the firmware detects.

question: Task Manager shows the disk at 100 percent while processor and memory use stay low. Which tool shows the technician which files each process is reading and writing?
explanation: The Disk tab of Resource Monitor lists each process with the files it is reading and writing and the bytes per second for each, which shows what is keeping the disk busy. Performance Monitor graphs counters such as disk queue length without naming files, Disk Management creates and formats partitions, and System Information reports the hardware and software configuration.

question: A blind user on a Mac needs everything on the screen, including menus and buttons, read aloud. Which built-in feature should be turned on?
explanation: VoiceOver is the screen reader built into macOS: it speaks every item on the screen and is turned on in the Accessibility pane of System Settings. Narrator is the screen reader in Windows, Dictation turns the user's speech into typed text, and Live Captions turn spoken audio into text on the screen.

question: A company does not want the browsing history, saved passwords and bookmarks on its work laptops copied to employees' personal cloud accounts. Which feature should the technician disable through policy?
explanation: Browser data sync copies history, passwords, bookmarks and settings to whatever account the user signs in with, so on company devices it can move work data into personal accounts. Disabling private browsing does not stop syncing, turning off the password manager would leave history and bookmarks syncing, and tracking prevention only blocks trackers on websites.

question: When a Linux PC starts, which component shows the menu of installed kernels or operating systems and then loads the chosen kernel into memory?
options: The init system, such as systemd
explanation: The bootloader runs after the firmware (UEFI or BIOS) and loads the chosen kernel and its initial RAM disk; GRUB, the usual Linux bootloader, can offer a menu of kernels and other operating systems. The init system, systemd, starts only after the kernel is running, a desktop environment such as GNOME appears after login, and a shell such as Bash interprets typed commands.

question: A full scan of a PC's drive finds nothing, but an endpoint detection tool shows PowerShell running an encoded script that is read from a registry value and executed only in memory. Which type of infection is this?
explanation: Fileless malware runs in memory through tools already on the computer, such as PowerShell, and keeps its code in places like the registry, so a scan of files on the drive has nothing to find. A boot sector virus lives in the drive's boot area and a macro virus lives inside documents, so both leave something on disk, and a rootkit conceals its own processes, whereas here PowerShell is plainly visible.

question: An HR spreadsheet lists each employee's full name, home address, personal phone number and date of birth. Which type of regulated data does it hold?
explanation: Personally identifiable information is any data that can identify a specific person, such as a name combined with a home address, phone number or date of birth. Personal government-issued information means identifiers such as passport or driver's license numbers, credit card payment information covers card numbers, and protected health information covers health records, none of which the spreadsheet holds.

question: A photographer needs one USB drive that her Windows PC and her Mac can both read and write, and some of her videos are 10 GB each. Why is exFAT a better choice for it than FAT32?
options: It keeps a journal of file changes
It supports file and folder permissions
It allows far larger single files
It works with older cameras and consoles
explanation: FAT32 cannot store a single file of 4 GB or more, while exFAT allows far larger files and can be read and written by both Windows and macOS without extra software. Neither format keeps a journal or file permissions, which are features of NTFS, and FAT32 rather than exFAT is the format that older cameras and game consoles are most likely to accept.

question: A user wants a newly added network copier to become the default destination for documents sent from any app, and to see the documents waiting in its queue. Which Control Panel item handles both?
explanation: Devices and Printers is the Control Panel item for adding printers, choosing the default printer and opening a printer's queue of waiting documents. Device Manager installs, updates and rolls back the copier's driver, Color Management assigns color profiles to screens and printers, and Phone and Modem sets the dialing rules used by modems and fax lines.

question: A help desk reports each month what share of high-severity tickets it answered within 30 minutes and resolved within four hours. Which document sets those targets?
explanation: A service-level agreement sets the response and resolution times that a support team commits to, and monthly figures show whether those targets are being met. An acceptable use policy sets the rules for using company systems, a knowledge base article records a known problem and its fix, and an incident report documents one significant event.

question: After hours, a technician needs to sign in to an unattended Windows 11 Pro workstation and work on its full desktop, using only a feature built into Windows. Which remote access method should the technician use?
explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is built into Windows Pro, Enterprise and Education editions and opens a full desktop session on TCP port 3389 without anyone at the workstation. Microsoft Remote Assistance needs the user to send an invitation and accept the connection, VNC is third-party software, and the SSH server that Windows can add gives a command line rather than a desktop.

question: A user does not want the PC to restart by itself between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., the hours when it is in use. Where in Settings is this period set?
explanation: Active hours, set under Windows Update > Advanced options, are the period during which Windows does not restart the PC by itself to finish installing updates. Time & language sets the clock and time zone but not restart times, System covers power and sleep settings, and Apps manages installed apps. Windows 10 keeps active hours under Update & Security > Windows Update.

question: Ransomware encrypted a file share, and the technician has a clean backup from last night. The encrypted files are worthless, and users need the share back at its usual path as quickly as possible. Which recovery method fits BEST once the infection is removed?
options: Restore last night's backup to a different file server
Restore last night's backup to its original location
Restore last night's backup to a new folder on the share
Restore last week's full backup to its original location
explanation: In-place recovery writes the backup over the original files at their usual location, which suits data that is destroyed or worthless and must return to the same path. A new folder or a different server would give users a new path to find, and last week's backup would lose a week of work that last night's clean backup still holds. Remove the malware first so that the restored files are not encrypted again.

question: A user installed a free PDF reader from an unfamiliar website. The reader works normally, but soon afterward the IT team sees someone controlling the PC remotely. Which type of malware came with the reader?
explanation: A Trojan poses as useful software, such as a working PDF reader, and carries a hidden payload that often opens a back door for remote control. A virus spreads by infecting other files, a worm spreads across networks by itself, and a potentially unwanted program (PUP) is bundled software such as a toolbar that is unwanted but not built to give an attacker control.

question: Which physical destruction method can be done with an ordinary shop tool but leaves much of each platter's surface undamaged, so some data may still be readable?
explanation: Drilling puts a few holes through a hard drive's platters with an ordinary drill, which stops the drive from working but leaves much of each platter's surface intact, so some data may remain readable with specialist equipment. Shredding reduces the whole drive to small pieces, degaussing erases every platter with a magnetic field, and incineration burns the drive.

question: A technician needs to download a vendor's install script from https://downloads.example.com/tools/setup.sh into the current directory, keeping its file name. The link redirects to a mirror. Which command works?
explanation: With curl, -L follows redirects to the final location and -O saves the file in the current directory under its remote name, so the two together fetch setup.sh from the mirror. The -s option only hides the progress meter, and without -L curl saves the redirect response instead of the script; -o /tmp/setup.sh writes to another directory, and dnf installs RPM packages rather than shell scripts.

question: A user signs in to a stand-alone PC with a local account. Sign-in takes a long time, and Windows then says the user has been signed in with a temporary profile. What is the most likely cause?
options: The user's profile has become corrupted
The roaming profile share cannot be reached
The account has been locked out
explanation: Windows falls back to a temporary profile when it cannot load a user's own profile, most often because the profile or its NTUSER.DAT registry hive is corrupted, and the fix is to repair or rebuild that profile. An unreachable roaming profile share affects domain accounts that use roaming profiles, a locked-out account cannot sign in at all, and an expired password makes Windows ask for a new one first.

question: A file server's backup software is set to create a synthetic full backup every Sunday. How does the software build that backup?
options: It copies changes made since the last full backup
It copies changes made since the most recent backup
It reads each selected file from the source again
It merges the last full with later incrementals
explanation: A synthetic full backup is assembled on the backup system from the last full backup and the incremental backups taken after it, so the server is not read again to make it. Copying the changes since the last full is a differential backup, copying the changes since the most recent backup of any kind is an incremental, and reading every selected file from the source is an ordinary full backup.

question: On a shared family computer, a user wants one session in which the browser keeps history, cookies and form entries only until the window is closed, without changing anyone else's settings. Which feature meets this need?
explanation: Private browsing opens a window whose history, cookies and form entries are discarded when it closes, while the normal profile and its settings stay as they were. Clearing the cache removes stored page files but keeps history, browser data sync copies data to the user's account, and tracking prevention blocks trackers without stopping history from being saved. Private browsing does not hide activity from the network or the sites visited.

question: A SOHO router's setup guide recommends opening its management page over HTTPS rather than HTTP. What does this protect against?
options: Guessing of the factory default login
Capture of the password by a packet sniffer
Access by devices on the guest network
Logins to the router from the internet
explanation: HTTPS encrypts the management session, so a password typed into the router's settings page cannot be read by someone capturing traffic on the local network. Blocking logins from the internet is the job of turning off remote management, guessing a factory login is stopped by changing it, and keeping guest devices away from the settings page is the job of guest isolation.

question: Anti-malware tools have removed an infection from a Windows 11 Home PC, and a final check finds nothing more. What should the technician do next under CompTIA's procedure?
options: Teach the user to avoid future infections
Schedule recurring scans and install updates
Reimage the PC from a known-good image
Enable System Restore and create a restore point
explanation: Once remediation is complete, CompTIA's malware removal procedure schedules recurring scans and installs updates, so that any remnant or new infection is caught and the weakness the malware used is closed. Enabling System Restore and creating a restore point follows, educating the user comes last, and reimaging is for malware that removal cannot clear.

question: A junior technician wants to run a PowerShell script that an AI chatbot wrote to clean up user profiles on every company PC. What should happen FIRST?
options: Back up the profiles, then run it after hours
Review the script's code, then test it in a sandbox
Sign the script so the execution policy allows it
Have a senior technician approve the rollout
explanation: AI can produce scripts with invented parameters or destructive logic, so a person reviews the code, checks its cmdlets against documentation and tests it in a sandbox before change approval and rollout. Signing the script, backing up the profiles before a run and a senior technician's approval are all later steps, and taking them first would push untested code toward every PC.

question: Searches from the Start menu and File Explorer are slow and miss files in a new Projects folder on the D: drive. A technician wants Windows to catalog that folder and rebuild its search database. Which Control Panel item does this?
explanation: Indexing Options chooses which locations the Windows Search index covers and, under Advanced, rebuilds the index when searches are slow or incomplete. File History keeps backup copies of folders on another drive, Sync Center keeps offline copies of network files in step with the server, and Storage Spaces pools several drives into one volume.

question: An iPhone user taps Get on a large game in the App Store, but the download fails right away. The phone shows 900 MB free, and the game needs 3 GB. What should the technician do?
options: Switch the download from Wi-Fi to cellular data
Offload unused apps and delete old video files
Sign out of the App Store and sign back in
Update iOS to the newest version the phone supports
explanation: An app cannot install without enough free storage, so a 3 GB game on a phone with 900 MB free needs space made by offloading unused apps or deleting old videos (Settings, General, iPhone Storage). Updating iOS helps when an app needs a newer version, cellular data helps when a Wi-Fi network blocks the store, and signing out and back in clears account errors, but none of them frees space.

question: A technician is planning a 3D rendering computer that will run Windows 11 Pro. What is the largest amount of RAM that this edition can use?
explanation: Windows 11 Pro can use up to 2 TB of RAM, compared with 128 GB for Home and 6 TB for Pro for Workstations and Enterprise. A computer that needs more than 2 TB therefore needs Pro for Workstations or Enterprise, and 4 GB is the least memory that Windows 11 requires, not a ceiling.

question: A security policy requires passwords to include uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and symbols. Why does current guidance, such as NIST's, put more weight on password length than on these complexity rules?
options: Windows 11 no longer supports complexity rules, so length is the one rule left
Each added character multiplies the guesses, and forced rules breed patterns
Long passwords are hashed more times, so each guess takes the attacker longer
Phone keyboards often lack symbols, so complex passwords lock out mobile users
explanation: Each added character multiplies the number of possible passwords, while forced complexity tends to produce predictable patterns such as P@ssw0rd that cracking tools try early. NIST's guidance therefore favors long passphrases checked against lists of breached passwords over composition rules. A longer password is not hashed more times, Windows 11 still offers the complexity policy, and phone keyboards can enter symbols.

question: Students have been entering firmware setup on a school's library laptops, changing the boot order and starting the laptops from their own USB drives. Which setting stops them from making these changes?
explanation: A BIOS/UEFI administrator password locks the firmware settings, so that nobody without it can change the boot order or turn on booting from USB. Secure Boot still starts boot loaders signed with trusted keys, including many Linux tools, and can be switched off in an unlocked setup. BitLocker protects the data on the internal drive without stopping another system from starting, and disabling AutoRun only stops programs on media from launching inside Windows.

question: A user wants websites to stop asking for their location, and wants the camera and microphone blocked for every site except the company's videoconferencing site. Where should the technician set this?
options: The browser's settings for clearing site data
The pop-up blocker's list of allowed sites
explanation: Browsers can allow or block features such as camera, microphone, location and notifications for all sites or for each site (Site settings in Chrome, Cookies and site permissions in Edge). The pop-up blocker only handles new windows, clearing site data removes history and cookies, and tracking prevention exceptions only relax tracker blocking for listed sites.

question: While hardening a Windows workstation, a technician must keep the built-in Administrator account enabled for emergency recovery. Attack tools try that account first on every computer they reach. Which change makes it harder for those tools to target?
explanation: Renaming the built-in Administrator account defeats attacks that look for it under its well-known default name, while the account stays enabled for recovery, and it should also have a long, unique password. Disabling it or setting it to expire would take away the recovery account that has to be kept, and hiding it from the sign-in screen does not stop a tool that tries to sign in with the default name.

question: During hardening, a technician finds the built-in Guest account enabled on a Windows workstation that only named staff use. Which action stops anyone from signing in with that account?
explanation: The built-in Guest account should be disabled, because it lets someone use the computer without an account of their own and nobody is accountable for what it does. Windows does not allow the built-in Guest account to be deleted, renaming the account changes only the name an intruder would try, and auditing it records each sign-in without preventing any of them.

question: A small office is moving its computers into an Active Directory domain. On the one computer that runs Windows 11 Home, the technician finds no setting for joining a domain. What is the cause?
options: The DNS server address is the router
The clock is behind the domain controller
The adapter has an APIPA address
The installed edition cannot join a domain
explanation: Windows 11 Home cannot join an Active Directory domain, so it shows no setting for joining one, while Pro and higher editions can join. A clock out of step with the domain controller, a DNS setting that points to the router or an APIPA address would make a join attempt fail with an error, but none of them removes the setting.

question: Malware on a PC has inserted its code into several program files. Each time one of those programs runs, the code copies itself into more programs, but it reaches other computers only when an infected file is copied to them. Which type of malware is this?
explanation: A virus inserts its code into a host, such as a program file, and spreads when that host is run or copied, which is the main difference from a worm. A worm is a standalone program that copies itself across a network without needing a host or a user, a Trojan poses as a useful program but does not infect other files, and a rootkit hides itself rather than spreading.

question: Without any action by its user, a workstation was infected through a flaw in one of its programs that the vendor had already fixed in a newer version. After the malware is removed, which step will prevent the same infection?
options: Show the user how the infection began
explanation: Installing the vendor's updates closes the flaw the malware used, so the same exploit cannot work again, which is why updates follow remediation in the malware removal procedure. Regular scans find a new infection but leave the flaw open, a fresh restore point only provides a clean state to return to, and teaching the user cannot stop an exploit that needed no action from the user.

question: An audit finds the vsftpd FTP server running on a Linux workstation, though nobody uses FTP on it. Which command stops the service now and keeps it from starting at boot?
explanation: The systemctl disable --now command stops a service immediately and removes it from startup, which suits an unused FTP server that would otherwise send credentials in plain text. With enable --now the service starts at once and at every boot, stop ends it only until it starts again at the next boot, and reload-or-restart applies new settings while leaving it running.

question: A user wants Windows 11 to keep recording the screen in the background so that what just happened can be saved as a clip. Which Settings category holds the Captures page where this is turned on?
explanation: In Windows 11, the Gaming category of Settings holds the Game Bar, Captures and Game Mode pages, and Captures is where background recording is turned on. System covers display, sound, notifications, power and storage, Accessibility holds aids such as Narrator, Magnifier and captions, and Apps manages installed apps, default apps and startup apps.

question: An upgrade to the company's email system is complete, and its users have formally signed off on the result. What should the IT team do next to close out the change?
options: Repeat the sandbox tests on the new version
Run the steps in the rollback plan
Ask the change board to approve the work
explanation: A post-implementation review closes a change once users have accepted it, by checking that it met its goals, recording any problems and lessons learned, and filing the change records. The rollback plan is used only when a change has failed, while sandbox testing and change board approval both belong before the work is done.

question: Devices on a home network have been opening inbound ports on the router by themselves, with no rule entered by anyone. Which router feature should a technician disable to stop malware from doing the same?
explanation: Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) lets devices and programs on the LAN open inbound ports on the router without anyone approving it, so malware can use it to expose a computer to the internet. DHCP hands out IP addresses, WPS lets devices join the wireless network with a PIN or a button press, and QoS gives some traffic priority over the rest.

question: A user says that apps on a Windows 11 PC show too many pop-up alerts. In which Settings category can the technician switch these alerts off for one app at a time?
explanation: Windows 11 keeps notification settings under System > Notifications, where each app that sends notifications has its own switch. Personalization changes the background, lock screen and taskbar, Accessibility sets how long notifications stay on screen but not which apps send them, and Privacy & security decides which apps may read notifications rather than which may show them.

question: After a user visited a website, ads began popping up every few minutes in the corner of the screen, each labeled with the browser's name and the site's address, even when the site is closed. Which change stops them at their source?
options: Turn on Do not disturb in the Windows settings
Revoke the site's permission to send notifications
Clear the browsing history and cached images and files
Turn on the pop-up blocker in the browser's settings
explanation: Ads that arrive as notifications labeled with a site's address come from that site's permission to send notifications, which the user granted, often by clicking Allow on a prompt, so revoking the permission in the browser's site settings stops them. A pop-up blocker stops new browser windows rather than notifications, clearing history and cached files leaves the permission in place, and Do not disturb only hides every notification without removing the cause.

question: A workstation is listening on an unexpected TCP port, and a technician wants to know which program opened it. Which command, run from an elevated prompt, lists the executable behind each connection and listening port?
